question_data.passage:
Five classmates are planning their class booth for the school festival in a group chat.

**Hana:** Our class meeting is tomorrow, so let's decide what booth to run. Last year we did a haunted house, but the science club is doing one this year, so we should pick something different.

**Riku:** I vote for a takoyaki stand. Food sells well, but the problem is we'd need a teacher to supervise the cooking, and Mr. Sato already told me he can't stay after 3 p.m.

**Mei:** The festival runs until 5 p.m., so a food stand that closes early would lose its busiest hours. How about a board-game café instead? No cooking, no supervision rules, and we already own most of the games.

**Riku:** I like that, but a café needs a lot of tables. The art club booked the big room with tables. We'd be stuck in a small classroom.

**Hana:** Actually, a small room is fine for a quiet café. My worry is money — we only have a 6,000-yen budget, and new games cost a lot.

**Mei:** We don't need new ones. I can bring six games from home, and Riku has three. That's enough to start.

**Daiki:** Then let's go with the board-game café. I'll make the sign and a price list tonight. Hana, can you ask our homeroom teacher to reserve the small classroom before someone else takes it?

**Hana:** Sure, I'll email her right after dinner. Mei, please bring your games to school on Friday so we can test them.

**Yuki:** Great. I'll count how many chairs the small room has and report back tomorrow.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: Why does the group decide against running a food stand?
choices: Because the science club is already selling food at the festival
Because the festival ends before the busiest selling hours begin
Because no teacher can supervise the cooking for the full festival hours
Because the class budget is too small to buy any cooking ingredients
questions.explanation:
正解は「Because no teacher can supervise the cooking for the full festival hours」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `decide against ~ing` は「〜しないことに決める」。**against が否定を担う**ので、
  本文に not が無くても「やめた」と読む。
- 理由を問う設問は「誰の発言が決め手になったか」を探す。チャット形式では
  **一人の発言で完結せず、次の人が補って初めて理由が成立する**ことが多い。
- `supervise` は「上から (super) 見る (vise)」= 監督する。責任者としての立ち会い。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Riku の問題提起:
`the problem is [(that) we'd need [a teacher] [to supervise the cooking]]`
  S=the problem / V=is / C=that 節 (接続詞 that は省略)
  節内: S=we / V=would need / O=a teacher / C=to supervise the cooking (不定詞が O を説明)
Mei の補足:
`[a food stand [that closes early]] would lose [its busiest hours]`
  S=a food stand that closes early / V=would lose / O=its busiest hours
→ 「監督者が3時まで」+「祭りは5時まで」の二つが揃って初めて断念の理由になる。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Riku の発言。「I vote for a takoyaki stand. Food sells well, but the problem is we'd need a teacher to supervise the cooking, and Mr. Sato already told me he can't stay after 3 p.m.」
続く Mei の発言。「The festival runs until 5 p.m., so a food stand that closes early would lose its busiest hours.」
監督できるのが 3 時まで、開催は 5 時まで。この差が食べ物系をやめた理由。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Because the science club is already selling food at the festival」… 科学部がやるのは「the science club is doing one this year」の one = a haunted house (お化け屋敷) であって食べ物ではない。本文の haunted house を読み飛ばすと引っかかる。
- 「Because the festival ends before the busiest selling hours begin」… 「祭りが忙しい時間帯の前に終わる」は本文と逆。祭りは 5 時まで続き、早く閉まるのは食べ物の屋台の方 (a food stand that closes early)。主語のすり替え。
- 「Because the class budget is too small to buy any cooking ingredients」… 6,000 円の予算は Hana が**ボードゲーム**購入について心配した点であり、食材費の話ではない。心配の対象がずれている。

questions.stem: What does Hana say is her main concern about the board-game café?
choices: That the small classroom would be too quiet for customers
That the art club has already taken all the tables
That no teacher would agree to supervise the booth
That buying new board games would cost too much money
questions.explanation:
正解は「That buying new board games would cost too much money」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `worry` は名詞で「心配の種」。`My worry is ~` は「私が気にしているのは〜だ」。
- ダッシュ (—) は**直前の語を言い換える・具体化する**合図。`money — we only have a
  6,000-yen budget` は「お金 = つまり予算が6千円しかない」という関係。
- 「誰が何を心配したか」型は、発言者を取り違えると全滅する。**話者名と内容を必ず紐づける。**

## 🔬 文構造分析
Hana の発言:
`[My worry] is [money] — [we] only have [a 6,000-yen budget], and [new games] cost [a lot].`
  S=My worry / V=is / C=money
  ダッシュ以下は等位節が2つ: S=we / V=have / O=a 6,000-yen budget
                            S=new games / V=cost / O=a lot
→ C の money を、後続の2文が「予算が少ない」「新品は高い」と両側から説明している。
  つまり心配の中身は **新しいゲームの購入費**。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第5発言 Hana。「Actually, a small room is fine for a quiet café. My worry is money — we only have a 6,000-yen budget, and new games cost a lot.」
直後 Mei が「We don't need new ones. I can bring six games from home, and Riku has three.」と返し、
この心配が「新しいゲームを買う費用」であったことが確定する。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「That the small classroom would be too quiet for customers」… 小部屋については Hana 自身が「a small room is fine for a quiet café」と述べ、むしろ問題ないと明言している。心配の対象ではない。
- 「That the art club has already taken all the tables」… テーブル不足を言ったのは Riku (「a café needs a lot of tables. The art club booked the big room with tables.」)。話者が違う。
- 「That no teacher would agree to supervise the booth」… 監督者が必要なのは調理を伴う takoyaki stand の話。ボードゲームカフェは Mei が「No cooking, no supervision rules」と述べており、監督は不要。

question_data.passage:
You are a member of your school's volleyball club. Your club is going to a two-day training camp at Lake Mori, and your team members are sharing information in a group chat.

Kenta: Hi everyone! Just a reminder about the camp this weekend. We meet at the school's main gate at 7:30 a.m. on Saturday, NOT in front of the gym like last year. The bus leaves at 7:45 sharp, so don't be late!

Aoi: Thanks, Kenta. Coach Tanaka told me the bus company changed, so the new bus is smaller. We can only bring one bag each — a big sports bag is fine, but please don't bring a suitcase. We'll share the ball cart for the volleyballs, so leave your own balls at home.

Riku: Got it. What about meals? Do we need to bring lunch for Saturday?

Aoi: Good question. Dinner and Sunday meals are provided at the lodge, but Saturday lunch is NOT. So bring your own lunch and some snacks. There's a convenience store near the gate if you forget.

Kenta: One more thing — the weather report says it might rain on Sunday morning. Bring a rain jacket just in case. We'll still practice indoors, so it won't be cancelled.

Mei: I just remembered — I have a dentist appointment Saturday morning and can't take the bus. Coach said it's okay if I come by train and arrive at the lodge by noon. Is anyone else doing that?

Riku: No, I'll take the bus. But I can send you the lodge map, Mei, so you don't get lost from the station.

Mei: That would really help, thanks Riku!
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: What does Aoi tell the members about what to bring to the camp?
choices: They should carry their own volleyballs in the ball cart on the bus.
They should each bring only one bag and leave their own volleyballs at home.
They should bring a suitcase because the new bus is larger than before.
They should bring two bags, one for clothes and one for sports gear.
questions.explanation:
正解は「They should each bring only one bag and leave their own volleyballs at home.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `only one bag each` の `each` は「一人あたり」。**個数制限を配る副詞**として働く。
- `leave ~ at home` は「〜を家に置いていく」。leave は「その場に残す」が核。
- 持ち物系の設問は、**禁止 (don't bring) と指示 (bring) を取り違えない**こと。
  否定の位置がそのまま正誤の分かれ目になる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Aoi の指示文:
`[We] can only bring [one bag each] — [a big sports bag] is [fine], but please don't bring [a suitcase].`
  S=We / V=can bring / O=one bag each / M=only (制限)
  補足の等位節: S=a big sports bag / V=is / C=fine
  命令文: V=don't bring / O=a suitcase
続けて `[We]'ll share [the ball cart] [for the volleyballs], so leave [your own balls] [at home].`
  S=We / V=will share / O=the ball cart / M=for the volleyballs
  結果の命令文: V=leave / O=your own balls / M=at home
→ 「バッグは一人1つ」「自分のボールは持参しない」の2点が並んでいる。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Aoi の1つ目の発言。「Coach Tanaka told me the bus company changed, so the new bus is smaller. We can only bring one bag each — a big sports bag is fine, but please don't bring a suitcase. We'll share the ball cart for the volleyballs, so leave your own balls at home.」
バスが小さくなった (smaller) ことが、荷物制限の理由として置かれている。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「They should carry their own volleyballs in the ball cart on the bus.」… ボールは「We'll share the ball cart」= 部の台車で共有するので、各自が自分のボールを持ち込むのではない。「leave your own balls at home」と明確に禁止されている。
- 「They should bring a suitcase because the new bus is larger than before.」… バスは「the new bus is smaller」= 小さくなったのであり larger は逆。スーツケースも「please don't bring a suitcase」と禁止されている。二重に誤り。
- 「They should bring two bags, one for clothes and one for sports gear.」… 「one bag each」= 一人1つなので、2つは制限違反。衣類用と用具用に分けるという記述も本文に無い。

questions.stem: Riku asked whether lunch was needed. What is the correct answer based on the chat?
choices: No meals are provided, so everyone must bring all their own food.
All meals including Saturday lunch are provided at the lodge.
Saturday lunch is not provided, but the other meals are.
Only snacks are provided, and members must buy lunch at the lodge.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Saturday lunch is not provided, but the other meals are.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 大文字強調の `NOT` は「ここだけが例外」の合図。**例外の範囲を正確に切り出す**のがコツ。
- `A and B are provided, but C is NOT` は「A と B は提供、C だけ提供なし」。
  but の前後で提供/非提供がきれいに分かれる。
- 「何が含まれ、何が含まれないか」型は、**列挙された項目を一つずつ ○×** で処理する。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Aoi の回答:
`[Dinner and Sunday meals] are provided [at the lodge], but [Saturday lunch] is NOT.`
  前半: S=Dinner and Sunday meals (等位の複数主語) / V=are provided (受動態) / M=at the lodge
  後半: S=Saturday lunch / V=is NOT (provided が省略された否定)
→ but が「提供される群」と「されない1つ」の境界。省略された provided を補って読む。
続く `So bring [your own lunch] and [some snacks].` は V=bring / O=your own lunch と some snacks。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Aoi の2つ目の発言。「Dinner and Sunday meals are provided at the lodge, but Saturday lunch is NOT. So bring your own lunch and some snacks. There's a convenience store near the gate if you forget.」
土曜の昼食だけが対象外で、夕食と日曜の食事は宿で提供される。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「No meals are provided, so everyone must bring all their own food.」… 夕食と日曜の食事は「are provided at the lodge」と明記されている。「一切提供されない」は本文と矛盾。
- 「All meals including Saturday lunch are provided at the lodge.」… 土曜の昼食は「Saturday lunch is NOT」と大文字で否定されている。「すべて提供」は正反対。
- 「Only snacks are provided, and members must buy lunch at the lodge.」… スナックは「bring your own lunch and some snacks」= 各自持参する側。宿で昼食を買うという記述も無い。

questions.stem: What can be understood about Mei's plan for the camp?
choices: She will not attend the camp because of her dentist appointment.
She will take the same bus but get off at a different stop.
She will arrive at the school gate later, at around noon.
She will travel separately by train and meet the others at the lodge.
questions.explanation:
正解は「She will travel separately by train and meet the others at the lodge.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `come by train` の `by + 交通手段` は無冠詞。「電車という手段で」という様態を表す。
- `arrive at ~ by noon` の `by` は**期限**の by。「正午までに (それより前に) 着く」。
  `at noon` (正午ちょうど) との差が設問の分かれ目になる。
- 推論型は「本文が明言していないが、書かれた条件から必然的に導ける」ものを選ぶ。
  **欠席か遅刻か別ルートか**を、許可された内容から絞る。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Mei の発言:
`Coach said [(that) [it]'s okay [if [I] come [by train] and arrive [at the lodge] [by noon]]].`
  S=Coach / V=said / O=that 節 (that 省略)
  節内: 形式主語 S=it / V=is / C=okay / 真の内容=if 節
  if 節: S=I / V=come と arrive の2つが等位 / M=by train, at the lodge, by noon
→ 許可されたのは「電車で来て、正午までに **lodge に** 着く」こと。
  到着地が集合場所の gate ではなく lodge である点が問3の核心。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Mei の発言。「I just remembered — I have a dentist appointment Saturday morning and can't take the bus. Coach said it's okay if I come by train and arrive at the lodge by noon. Is anyone else doing that?」
Riku も「I can send you the lodge map, Mei, so you don't get lost from the station」と応じており、
駅から宿へ自力で向かう前提が共有されている。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「She will not attend the camp because of her dentist appointment.」… 「can't take the bus」はバスに乗れないだけで、欠席とは述べていない。むしろコーチが電車での参加を許可している。
- 「She will take the same bus but get off at a different stop.」… 「can't take the bus」と明言しているのでバス利用ではない。降車場所の話も本文に無い。
- 「She will arrive at the school gate later, at around noon.」… 正午までに着くのは「the lodge」であって school gate ではない。Mei はそもそも集合場所に行かない。到着地のすり替え。

question_data.passage:
**NOTICE: Changes to Library Rules — From July 1**

Hello, students! The Greenfield High School Library is making some changes from July 1. Please read this notice carefully before your next visit.

**Opening hours.** Until now, the library closed at 4:30 p.m. on weekdays. From July, it will stay open until 6:00 p.m. on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays so that students who join after-school clubs can still use it. On Tuesdays and Thursdays, the library will close at the usual time of 4:30 p.m. The Saturday morning hours (9:00 a.m.–12:00 noon) will not change.

**Borrowing.** You used to be able to borrow up to three books for two weeks. Now you may borrow up to five books, but the loan period is shorter: one week. If you need a book longer, you can renew it once online from the library website. You cannot renew a book that another student has already reserved.

**Eating and drinking.** Food is still not allowed anywhere in the library. However, students may now bring a drink in a bottle with a lid into the Reading Corner only. Drinks are still not allowed near the computers.

**Returning books.** A new return box has been placed outside the main door. You may drop books there at any time, even when the library is closed. Books left in the old box inside the library will no longer be collected.

If you have any questions, please ask Ms. Carter at the front desk.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: A student has a club activity every weekday afternoon and wants to use the library after the club ends at 5:00 p.m. On which days can the student use the library after the club?
choices: Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays
Tuesdays and Thursdays
Every weekday
Saturdays only
questions.explanation:
正解は「Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `stay open until ~` は「〜まで開いたままでいる」。stay は**状態の継続**を表す動詞。
- `so that S can V` は目的の副詞節。「〜できるように」。**誰のための変更か**が読める。
- 曜日・時刻の条件付き設問は、条件 (5時に部活が終わる) を先に固定してから
  本文の時刻表と突き合わせる。**先に条件を数値化する**のが最短。

## 🔬 文構造分析
本文 Opening hours:
`[it] will stay [open] [until 6:00 p.m.] [on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays] [so that
 [students [who join after-school clubs]] can still use [it]]`
  S=it (=the library) / V=will stay / C=open / M=until 6:00 p.m., on Mondays...
  so that 節: S=students who join after-school clubs / V=can use / O=it
対比文: `[On Tuesdays and Thursdays], [the library] will close [at the usual time of 4:30 p.m.]`
  M=On Tuesdays and Thursdays (文頭に出た時の副詞句) / S=the library / V=will close
  M=at the usual time of 4:30 p.m.
→ 「6時まで」の曜日と「4時半まで」の曜日が明示的に振り分けられている。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Opening hours の段落。「From July, it will stay open until 6:00 p.m. on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays so that students who join after-school clubs can still use it. On Tuesdays and Thursdays, the library will close at the usual time of 4:30 p.m.」
部活が 5 時に終わる生徒が使えるのは、6 時まで開いている月・水・金だけ。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Tuesdays and Thursdays」… 火・木は「will close at the usual time of 4:30 p.m.」= 4時半閉館なので、5時に部活が終わってからでは間に合わない。
- 「Every weekday」… 火・木が 4 時半閉館である以上、平日すべては成立しない。曜日で扱いが分かれている点を読み落とした選択肢。
- 「Saturdays only」… 土曜は「9:00 a.m.–12:00 noon」の午前のみ。そもそも平日の部活後という条件に合わない。

questions.stem: What is true about borrowing books under the new rules?
choices: The number of books and the loan period both stay the same.
Students can borrow more books than before, but must return them sooner.
Students can borrow fewer books, but keep them longer than before.
Students can renew any book as many times as they like.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Students can borrow more books than before, but must return them sooner.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `used to be able to V` は「以前は〜できた (今は違う)」。**used to が過去との対比**を担う。
- `but the loan period is shorter` の比較級は比較対象が省略されている。
  「(以前より) 短い」と補って読む。**比較級を見たら「何と比べて」を必ず補う。**
- 「増えたもの / 減ったもの」型は、**方向が逆の変化が同時に起きている**ことが狙われる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
本文 Borrowing:
`[You] used to be able to borrow [up to three books] [for two weeks].`
  S=You / V=used to be able to borrow / O=up to three books / M=for two weeks
`Now [you] may borrow [up to five books], but [the loan period] is [shorter]: one week.`
  S=you / V=may borrow / O=up to five books
  逆接: S=the loan period / V=is / C=shorter (than before が省略)
→ O の数は 3→5 で**増**、C の期間は 2週間→1週間で**減**。増減が逆向きに同居している。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Borrowing の段落。「You used to be able to borrow up to three books for two weeks. Now you may borrow up to five books, but the loan period is shorter: one week. If you need a book longer, you can renew it once online from the library website. You cannot renew a book that another student has already reserved.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The number of books and the loan period both stay the same.」… 冊数は 3→5、期間は 2週間→1週間で、どちらも変わっている。「両方そのまま」は本文と正反対。
- 「Students can borrow fewer books, but keep them longer than before.」… 冊数は増えており (up to three → up to five)、期間は短くなっている。増減の方向が両方とも逆。
- 「Students can renew any book as many times as they like.」… 更新は「you can renew it once」= 1回だけ。さらに「You cannot renew a book that another student has already reserved」と制限もある。「何度でも」は誤り。

question_data.passage:
**Greenfield Park Cleanup — Volunteers Wanted!**

Greenfield Park needs your help! After last month's summer festival, our park is covered in litter, and the river path has become muddy and overgrown. Join the **Greenfield Community Cleanup** and help bring our park back to life.

**When:** Saturday, July 18, from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. (rain date: Sunday, July 19)
**Where:** Meet at the East Gate, next to the parking lot.

Volunteers will be divided into three teams:
- **River Team** — clears weeds and trash along the muddy river path (boots provided; long sleeves and trousers required)
- **Garden Team** — plants flowers and waters the flower beds near the playground
- **Sorting Team** — separates collected items into recyclable and non-recyclable trash at the East Gate

You may choose your team when you sign up online by July 14. If you do not choose, we will place you in the team that needs the most people. **Students under 15 must bring an adult.**

Gloves, trash bags, and bottled water are free for everyone. Please wear clothes that can get dirty, and bring a hat and sunscreen. We will **not** provide lunch, so eat before you come or bring your own.

Everyone who finishes the morning will receive a "Green Helper" certificate, and the local café will give each volunteer a coupon for a free drink. Sign up at www.greenfieldpark.org/clean. Let's make Greenfield shine again!
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: What is one thing volunteers must do before the day of the cleanup?
choices: Buy their own gloves and trash bags
Bring a doctor's note if they are under 15
Pay a fee to receive a free drink coupon
Choose a team online by July 14 to be sure of their team
questions.explanation:
正解は「Choose a team online by July 14 to be sure of their team」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `may` は「〜してもよい」= **許可**。義務の must と読み分ける。
  ただし「希望を通したいなら期限内に」という条件付きの許可は、実質の締切になる。
- `If you do not ~, we will ~` は「しなければ、こちらで決める」。
  **不作為のときの既定値**を示す構文。ここが「事前にすべきこと」を浮かび上がらせる。
- 募集チラシ型は「無料で提供されるもの / 各自持参するもの / 事前手続き」の3つに仕分ける。

## 🔬 文構造分析
本文の申込規定:
`[You] may choose [your team] [when [you] sign up online [by July 14]].`
  S=You / V=may choose / O=your team / M=when 節 (時)
  when 節: S=you / V=sign up / M=online, by July 14
`[If [you] do not choose], [we] will place [you] [in the team [that needs the most people]].`
  M=If 節 (条件) / S=we / V=will place / O=you / M=in the team that needs the most people
→ 選ばなければ運営が割り振る。**希望チームを確実にする**には 7/14 までの選択が要る。

## 📍 本文の根拠
申込の段落。「You may choose your team when you sign up online by July 14. If you do not choose, we will place you in the team that needs the most people. Students under 15 must bring an adult.」
持ち物の段落。「Gloves, trash bags, and bottled water are free for everyone.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Buy their own gloves and trash bags」… 手袋とゴミ袋は「Gloves, trash bags, and bottled water are free for everyone」= 無料提供。購入は不要。
- 「Bring a doctor's note if they are under 15」… 15歳未満に求められるのは「must bring an adult」= 大人の同伴。医師の診断書という記述は本文に無い。
- 「Pay a fee to receive a free drink coupon」… クーポンは「the local café will give each volunteer a coupon for a free drink」= 参加者全員に無料で配られる。支払いは発生しない。

questions.stem: Mika wants to help but does not like getting muddy and prefers working with plants. Which team best fits her, and what must she remember?
choices: The Garden Team; she should bring her own lunch
The Sorting Team; she should report to the playground
The River Team; she should wear long sleeves and trousers
The Garden Team; lunch will be provided for her
questions.explanation:
正解は「The Garden Team; she should bring her own lunch」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 条件マッチ型 (人物の希望 → 最適な選択) は、**希望を2つに分解**してから照合する。
  ここでは「泥を避けたい」と「植物を扱いたい」の2条件。
- `We will not provide lunch, so eat before you come or bring your own.`
  の `so` は結果を導く。**禁止ではなく「だから各自で」という指示**として読む。
- 選択肢が「チーム名 + 注意点」の2要素なら、**両方が正しいものだけが正解**。
  片方合っていても、もう片方が誤りなら切る。

## 🔬 文構造分析
チーム説明 (Garden Team):
`plants [flowers] and waters [the flower beds] [near the playground]`
  V=plants / O=flowers、V=waters / O=the flower beds / M=near the playground
  → 泥の記述が無く、植物を扱う唯一のチーム。
昼食の指示:
`[We] will not provide [lunch], so eat [before you come] or bring [your own].`
  S=We / V=will not provide / O=lunch
  結果節は命令文が2つ等位: V=eat / M=before you come ｜ V=bring / O=your own
→ 「昼食は出ない」+「食べてくるか持参せよ」。Mika が忘れてはいけないのはここ。

## 📍 本文の根拠
チーム説明。「**Garden Team** — plants flowers and waters the flower beds near the playground」
「**River Team** — clears weeds and trash along the muddy river path (boots provided; long sleeves and trousers required)」
持ち物の段落。「We will **not** provide lunch, so eat before you come or bring your own.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The Sorting Team; she should report to the playground」… Sorting Team はゴミの分別で、植物を扱わない。また作業場所は「separates collected items into recyclable and non-recyclable trash at the East Gate」= East Gate であって playground ではない。二重に誤り。
- 「The River Team; she should wear long sleeves and trousers」… River Team は「the muddy river path」で作業する。泥を避けたいという Mika の希望と正面から衝突する。服装の記述自体は正しいが、チーム選択が誤り。
- 「The Garden Team; lunch will be provided for her」… チームは合っているが、昼食は「We will not provide lunch」と明記されている。提供されるという後半が誤り。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the condition of Greenfield Park before the cleanup?
choices: It had been closed to the public for a whole year
It was damaged by heavy rain during the summer festival
A recent event left it dirty and the river path hard to walk on
The playground equipment had become old and dangerous
questions.explanation:
正解は「A recent event left it dirty and the river path hard to walk on」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 推論型は「本文の記述から**必ず言えること**」を選ぶ。書かれていない事情を足したら負け。
- `After last month's summer festival, our park is covered in litter` の
  `After ~` は時の副詞句。**直前の出来事が現在の状態を作った**という因果を含意する。
- `has become muddy and overgrown` は現在完了。「(今も) その状態が続いている」。
  完了形は**過去の一点ではなく現在への影響**を語る。

## 🔬 文構造分析
冒頭の状況説明:
`[After last month's summer festival], [our park] is [covered in litter], and
 [the river path] has become [muddy and overgrown].`
  M=After last month's summer festival (時)
  前半: S=our park / V=is / C=covered in litter (受動の形で状態を表す)
  後半: S=the river path / V=has become / C=muddy and overgrown
→ 「最近の催し (夏祭り)」→「ゴミだらけ」「川沿いが泥で草だらけ」。
  選択肢はこの2つの結果を言い換えたものを選ぶ。

## 📍 本文の根拠
冒頭。「Greenfield Park needs your help! After last month's summer festival, our park is covered in litter, and the river path has become muddy and overgrown.」
River Team の説明も「clears weeds and trash along the muddy river path」と、同じ状態を裏づけている。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「It had been closed to the public for a whole year」… 公園が1年間閉鎖されていたという記述は本文に無い。むしろ先月まで夏祭りが開かれている。
- 「It was damaged by heavy rain during the summer festival」… 泥の原因を大雨と断定する記述は無い。本文が挙げるのは「After last month's summer festival」= 祭りの後という時間関係のみ。原因のすり替え。
- 「The playground equipment had become old and dangerous」… 遊具については「waters the flower beds near the playground」と場所として触れるだけ。老朽化や危険性の記述は無い。

question_data.passage:
[Group chat: "Tomorrow's Test"]

Hana: Hey everyone! Our biology test is on Thursday, so I think we should hold one study session before then. How about meeting at the city library this Wednesday afternoon?

Riku: Wednesday doesn't work for me. I have soccer practice until 5 p.m., and the library closes at 6. That's too little time. Can we do it on Tuesday instead?

Mei: Tuesday is fine for me, but the library is closed on Tuesdays this month for repairs. We could use the study room at the community center near the station. It's free if we book it in advance.

Hana: Good idea, Mei. I didn't know the library was closed. Riku, are you free on Tuesday?

Riku: Yes, Tuesday afternoon is open for me. Let's do that. But I can't book the room because I don't have a community center card. Mei, you have one, right?

Mei: I do. I'll reserve the room from 3 to 6 p.m. We need at least two people's names to book it, so I'll add Hana too.

Hana: Perfect. Should we ask Daichi? He's good at biology and could help us with the hard parts.

Riku: Let's ask him, but he told me he works at his family's shop on weekday afternoons until 4. He might join us late.

Mei: That's okay. We'll already be there. Daichi, if you see this, come whenever you finish work!
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: Where and when will the group hold their study session?
choices: At the city library on Wednesday afternoon
At the community center on Tuesday afternoon
At the city library on Tuesday afternoon
At the community center on Wednesday afternoon
questions.explanation:
正解は「At the community center on Tuesday afternoon」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 予定調整のチャットは**「提案 → 却下 → 対案 → 同意」の連鎖**で最終形が決まる。
  最初の提案 (Wednesday / library) は途中で潰れるので、そこで読み止めると外す。
- `Let's do that.` の `that` は**直前に出た案**を指す。指示語の中身を必ず特定する。
- 場所と日時の2要素は別々に確定させる。片方だけ合っている選択肢が必ず紛れ込む。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Mei の対案:
`[We] could use [the study room [at the community center [near the station]]].`
  S=We / V=could use / O=the study room (at ~ near ~ が二重に後置修飾)
Riku の同意:
`[Tuesday afternoon] is [open] [for me]. Let's do [that].`
  S=Tuesday afternoon / V=is / C=open / M=for me
  続く命令文: V=Let's do / O=that (=火曜午後に community center で集まる案)
→ 場所は community center、日時は Tuesday afternoon で確定する。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Mei の発言。「Tuesday is fine for me, but the library is closed on Tuesdays this month for repairs. We could use the study room at the community center near the station. It's free if we book it in advance.」
Riku の返答。「Yes, Tuesday afternoon is open for me. Let's do that.」
Mei の確定。「I'll reserve the room from 3 to 6 p.m.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「At the city library on Wednesday afternoon」… Wednesday は Riku が「Wednesday doesn't work for me」と断り、日程も場所も採用されていない。最初の提案のまま止まった読み。
- 「At the city library on Tuesday afternoon」… 火曜は「the library is closed on Tuesdays this month for repairs」= 修理で休館。日は合っているが場所が誤り。
- 「At the community center on Wednesday afternoon」… 場所は合っているが、Wednesday は Riku の都合で流れている。日が誤り。

questions.stem: Why is Mei the one who will book the room?
choices: Because she is the best at biology in the group
Because she lives closest to the community center
Because she has a community center card that the others do not have
Because the library asked her to reserve it
questions.explanation:
正解は「Because she has a community center card that the others do not have」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 理由を問う設問では、**否定文が答えの在りかを示す**ことが多い。
  「A にはできない (なぜなら〜が無いから)」→「では B がやる」という流れ。
- `I don't have a community center card` → `Mei, you have one, right?` の
  `one` は **a community center card** の代用。指示語・代名詞の中身を戻して読む。
- `I do.` は `I do have one.` の省略。**do は前の動詞句をまるごと受ける代動詞**。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Riku の発言:
`[I] can't book [the room] [because [I] don't have [a community center card]].`
  S=I / V=can't book / O=the room / M=because 節 (理由)
  because 節: S=I / V=don't have / O=a community center card
Mei の応答:
`[I] do. [I]'ll reserve [the room] [from 3 to 6 p.m.].`
  S=I / V=do (= have a community center card の代動詞)
  次文: S=I / V=will reserve / O=the room / M=from 3 to 6 p.m.
→ 「カードが無いからできない」↔「私は持っている」の対で、予約役が決まる。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Riku の発言。「But I can't book the room because I don't have a community center card. Mei, you have one, right?」
Mei の応答。「I do. I'll reserve the room from 3 to 6 p.m. We need at least two people's names to book it, so I'll add Hana too.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Because she is the best at biology in the group」… 生物が得意だと述べられているのは Daichi (「He's good at biology」)。Mei ではないうえ、予約の理由にもならない。
- 「Because she lives closest to the community center」… 誰がどこに住んでいるかは本文に一切書かれていない。距離を理由にするのは本文外の推測。
- 「Because the library asked her to reserve it」… 図書館は今月休館中で、予約を依頼する立場にない。community center の予約とも無関係。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about Daichi from the chat?
choices: He will arrive at the session before the others because he is good at biology
He cannot join the session at all because the room is already full
He will book the room since he has a community center card
He may join the session later than the others because of his part-time work
questions.explanation:
正解は「He may join the session later than the others because of his part-time work」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `might join us late` の `might` は**可能性の推量**。断定ではないので、
  選択肢も「〜かもしれない」の幅を持つものを選ぶ。断定形の選択肢は言い過ぎ。
- `come whenever you finish work` の `whenever` は「いつでも、〜したときに」。
  **到着時刻を相手に委ねる**表現で、遅れて来る前提が読み取れる。
- 推論型では「予約は3〜6時」「仕事は4時まで」という**数値の重なり**を確認する。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Riku の発言:
`[he] works [at his family's shop] [on weekday afternoons] [until 4]. [He] might join [us] [late].`
  S=he / V=works / M=at his family's shop, on weekday afternoons, until 4
  次文: S=He / V=might join / O=us / M=late
Mei の呼びかけ:
`[Daichi], [if [you] see [this]], come [whenever [you] finish [work]]!`
  M=if 節 (条件) / V=come (命令文) / M=whenever 節 (時)
→ 仕事は 4 時まで、勉強会は 3〜6 時。重なりは 4〜6 時なので、遅れての合流になる。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Riku の発言。「Let's ask him, but he told me he works at his family's shop on weekday afternoons until 4. He might join us late.」
Mei の発言。「That's okay. We'll already be there. Daichi, if you see this, come whenever you finish work!」
予約は「I'll reserve the room from 3 to 6 p.m.」なので、4時以降に合流できる。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「He will arrive at the session before the others because he is good at biology」… 「He might join us late」= 遅れて来る可能性であり、早く着くとは述べていない。生物が得意なことと到着時刻は無関係。
- 「He cannot join the session at all because the room is already full」… Mei は「That's okay. We'll already be there.」と受け入れており、参加不可とは述べていない。部屋が満員という記述も無い。
- 「He will book the room since he has a community center card」… カードを持っていて予約するのは Mei (「I do. I'll reserve the room」)。Daichi ではない。

question_data.passage:
You are reading a group chat among five classmates in Class 2-B. They are deciding who will take charge of each role for the school sports festival next month.

【Class 2-B Sports Festival Chat】

Haruka: Hi everyone! We need to fill four roles by Friday: cheer leader, equipment manager, scoreboard keeper, and program designer. Who wants what?

Kenji: I'll happily do equipment. My older brother did it last year and left me all his notes, so I already know where everything is stored.

Mei: I really want to be cheer leader, but I have club practice every afternoon until 4. The cheer team has to practice from 3:30, so I don't think I can make it. Maybe I'll take program designer instead — I love drawing.

Sora: I can be cheer leader then! I quit the basketball club last week, so my afternoons are free now. I've never led cheers, but I'm willing to learn.

Haruka: Great, Sora! That leaves scoreboard keeper. I'd take it myself, but I'm already the class representative, so I'll be too busy on the day running between teachers.

Tomo: Then I'll do the scoreboard. I'm good with numbers and I stay calm under pressure. But there's one condition — someone has to teach me how the new digital board works. I've only ever used the old chalk one.

Kenji: No problem, Tomo. I'll show you on Thursday when I check the equipment.

Mei: Perfect! So everything is decided except one thing — Haruka, can you email the teacher our list before Friday?

Haruka: Sure, I'll send it tonight. Thanks, everyone!
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: Why is Mei unable to become the cheer leader?
choices: Her club practice ends after the cheer team's practice begins.
She does not enjoy leading cheers in front of others.
She has already promised to become the program designer.
She does not know how to use the new digital scoreboard.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Her club practice ends after the cheer team's practice begins.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `I don't think I can make it.` の `make it` は「間に合う・都合をつける」。
  **think を否定して後ろの内容を否定する**(否定の繰り上げ)のが英語の癖。
- 時刻の前後関係が理由になる型。「部活は4時まで」「応援練習は3:30から」を
  **数直線に置く**と、重なっていないことが一目で分かる。
- 理由が「時間の衝突」なのか「意欲の欠如」なのかは、本文の語で判定する。
  Mei は `I really want to be cheer leader` と言っており、意欲はある。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Mei の発言:
`[I] really want [to be cheer leader], but [I] have [club practice] [every afternoon] [until 4].`
  S=I / V=want / O=to be cheer leader / M=really
  逆接: S=I / V=have / O=club practice / M=every afternoon, until 4
`[The cheer team] has to practice [from 3:30], so [I] don't think [(that) [I] can make [it]].`
  S=The cheer team / V=has to practice / M=from 3:30
  結果節: S=I / V=don't think / O=that 節 → 節内 S=I / V=can make / O=it
→ 応援練習の開始 (3:30) より部活の終了 (4:00) が後。だから間に合わない。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Mei の発言。「I really want to be cheer leader, but I have club practice every afternoon until 4. The cheer team has to practice from 3:30, so I don't think I can make it. Maybe I'll take program designer instead — I love drawing.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「She does not enjoy leading cheers in front of others.」… Mei は「I really want to be cheer leader」と述べており、嫌っているのではない。理由は時間の衝突。
- 「She has already promised to become the program designer.」… program designer は「Maybe I'll take program designer instead」= 応援団長を諦めた**結果**の代案であり、原因ではない。因果が逆。
- 「She does not know how to use the new digital scoreboard.」… デジタル掲示板が分からないのは Tomo (「I've only ever used the old chalk one」)。人物が違う。

questions.stem: What can be understood about Sora from the chat?
choices: He has led cheers many times and offers his experience to the others.
He will teach Tomo how to operate the new scoreboard on Thursday.
He became available to lead cheers because he recently left a club.
He asked Haruka to email the role list to the teacher before Friday.
questions.explanation:
正解は「He became available to lead cheers because he recently left a club.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `so` は**結果**を導く等位接続詞。`I quit ~, so my afternoons are free now` は
  「辞めた → だから空いた」。**原因が前、結果が後**。
- `I've never led cheers` の現在完了 (経験) の否定は「一度も〜したことがない」。
  経験の有無を問う選択肢と直結する。
- チャット型の推論では「誰が何を言ったか」の帰属が最大の罠。
  **発言者名を指でなぞりながら**選択肢を潰す。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Sora の発言:
`[I] quit [the basketball club] [last week], so [my afternoons] are [free] [now].`
  前半: S=I / V=quit / O=the basketball club / M=last week
  結果節: S=my afternoons / V=are / C=free / M=now
`[I]'ve never led [cheers], but [I]'m willing [to learn].`
  S=I / V=have led / O=cheers / M=never (経験の否定)
  逆接: S=I / V=am / C=willing to learn
→ 「辞めた」が原因、「午後が空いた」が結果。だから引き受けられる、という論理。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Sora の発言。「I can be cheer leader then! I quit the basketball club last week, so my afternoons are free now. I've never led cheers, but I'm willing to learn.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「He has led cheers many times and offers his experience to the others.」… 「I've never led cheers」= 一度も経験が無いと明言している。経験豊富というのは正反対。
- 「He will teach Tomo how to operate the new scoreboard on Thursday.」… 木曜に掲示板の使い方を教えるのは Kenji (「I'll show you on Thursday when I check the equipment」)。Sora ではない。
- 「He asked Haruka to email the role list to the teacher before Friday.」… 教員へのメールを頼んだのは Mei (「Haruka, can you email the teacher our list before Friday?」)。Sora ではない。

questions.stem: Which role still needs help before it can be carried out smoothly?
choices: The equipment manager, because Kenji has lost his brother's notes.
The scoreboard keeper, because Tomo needs to be taught the new board.
The cheer leader, because Sora must find a replacement.
The program designer, because Mei dislikes drawing pictures.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The scoreboard keeper, because Tomo needs to be taught the new board.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「まだ手当てが要るのはどれか」型は、**条件付きの引き受け**を探す。
  `But there's one condition —` のような**留保の合図**が目印。
- `has to` は外部からの必要性。`someone has to teach me` は
  「(自分では無理なので) 誰かが教える必要がある」という未解決の要求。
- 他の選択肢は本文と**矛盾**していることが多い。矛盾は「本文にそう書いていない」より強い否定材料。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Tomo の条件提示:
`But there's [one condition] — [someone] has to teach [me] [how the new digital board works].`
  There 構文: V=there's / S=one condition
  ダッシュ以下: S=someone / V=has to teach / O1=me / O2=how 節 (間接疑問)
`[I]'ve only ever used [the old chalk one].`
  S=I / V=have used / O=the old chalk one / M=only ever (経験の限定)
→ 「新しい板の操作を誰かが教える」が未達の条件。引き受けは条件付き。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Tomo の発言。「Then I'll do the scoreboard. I'm good with numbers and I stay calm under pressure. But there's one condition — someone has to teach me how the new digital board works. I've only ever used the old chalk one.」
Kenji の応答。「No problem, Tomo. I'll show you on Thursday when I check the equipment.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The equipment manager, because Kenji has lost his brother's notes.」… Kenji は「My older brother did it last year and left me all his notes, so I already know where everything is stored」と述べ、ノートは手元にある。失っていない。
- 「The cheer leader, because Sora must find a replacement.」… Sora は自ら「I can be cheer leader then!」と引き受けており、代役を探す必要は無い。
- 「The program designer, because Mei dislikes drawing pictures.」… Mei は「I love drawing」と述べている。嫌いというのは正反対。

question_data.passage:
**Greenwood High School — Library Committee Members Wanted!**

Do you love books and want to help your school? The Greenwood High School Library is looking for new student committee members for this year. No special experience is needed — just bring your energy and a friendly smile!

**What committee members do:**
- Help students find and borrow books at the front desk (Monday to Thursday, after school)
- Put returned books back on the shelves and keep the reading corner tidy
- Plan one "Book Week" event each term to get more students reading

**When and where to apply:**
Come to the library on Friday, May 8, between 3:30 p.m. and 5:00 p.m. Ms. Tanaka, the school librarian, will explain the job and answer your questions. You do not need to sign up before this meeting — just come on the day.

**Important points:**
- You must be free at least one afternoon a week. Members who join the front desk team work in pairs, so you will never be alone.
- First-year students are welcome, but you will need a short note from a parent. Second- and third-year students do not need this note.
- If you cannot come on May 8 but still want to join, send an email to Ms. Tanaka by May 15. She will arrange another time to meet you.

We hope to see many of you on May 8. Reading is more fun when we share it!
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: What is one thing library committee members are expected to do?
choices: Teach reading lessons to younger students every morning
Buy new books for the library with school money
Repair damaged books in the reading corner
Organize a Book Week event once each term
questions.explanation:
正解は「Organize a Book Week event once each term」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 箇条書きの募集要項は、**動詞の原形**が仕事内容の列挙を担う (Help / Put / Plan)。
  各行の先頭動詞だけを拾うと仕事の全体像が最短で取れる。
- `one ~ each term` の `each` は「〜ごとに」。**頻度**を表す。
- 「本文に書かれている仕事」を選ぶ問題では、**もっともらしいが書かれていない**
  選択肢が並ぶ。本文に語が実在するかで機械的に切る。

## 🔬 文構造分析
仕事内容の3行目:
`Plan [one "Book Week" event] [each term] [to get [more students] [reading]]`
  V=Plan (原形・箇条書きの列挙) / O=one "Book Week" event / M=each term
  目的の不定詞: to get / O=more students / C=reading (get O C = O に C させる)
→ get O ~ing は「O を〜している状態にする」。「もっと多くの生徒に読ませる」ための企画。

## 📍 本文の根拠
What committee members do の箇条書き。「Plan one "Book Week" event each term to get more students reading」
他の2行は「Help students find and borrow books at the front desk (Monday to Thursday, after school)」
「Put returned books back on the shelves and keep the reading corner tidy」。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Teach reading lessons to younger students every morning」… 朝の読書指導という記述は本文に無い。仕事の時間帯は「Monday to Thursday, after school」= 放課後。
- 「Buy new books for the library with school money」… 本の購入は本文に無い。委員の仕事は貸出補助・返却整理・イベント企画の3つ。
- 「Repair damaged books in the reading corner」… 本の修理は本文に無い。reading corner についての仕事は「keep the reading corner tidy」= 整頓のみ。

questions.stem: A first-year student who wants to join the committee must
choices: bring a short note from a parent
pay a small fee before the meeting
work alone at the front desk
apply only by email before May 8
questions.explanation:
正解は「bring a short note from a parent」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `you will need ~` は「〜が必要になる」= 実質の要件。**must と同じ強さ**で読む。
- `First-year students are welcome, but ...` の but 以降が**学年限定の条件**。
  直後に「Second- and third-year students do not need this note.」と対比が置かれ、
  条件が1年生だけに掛かることが確定する。
- 「〜な生徒は何をしなければならないか」型は、**対象を絞る語 (first-year)** に印を付ける。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Important points の2つ目:
`[First-year students] are [welcome], but [you] will need [a short note [from a parent]].`
  前半: S=First-year students / V=are / C=welcome
  逆接: S=you / V=will need / O=a short note (from a parent が後置修飾)
対比文: `[Second- and third-year students] do not need [this note].`
  S=Second- and third-year students / V=do not need / O=this note
→ 同じ O (note) を、学年で要否が分かれる形に置いている。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Important points。「First-year students are welcome, but you will need a short note from a parent. Second- and third-year students do not need this note.」
また「Members who join the front desk team work in pairs, so you will never be alone.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「pay a small fee before the meeting」… 料金についての記述は本文に一切無い。無料であることも有料であることも書かれていないが、要件として挙がっていない。
- 「work alone at the front desk」… 「Members who join the front desk team work in pairs, so you will never be alone」= 必ず2人組。一人で働くことはない。
- 「apply only by email before May 8」… メール申込は「If you cannot come on May 8 but still want to join」= 5月8日に来られない人向けの代替。1年生一般の要件ではない。さらに本文は「You do not need to sign up before this meeting」とも述べている。

questions.stem: What should a student do if he or she cannot come to the library on May 8?
choices: Wait until next term and apply again
Email Ms. Tanaka by May 15 to set up another time
Ask another student to attend in his or her place
Sign up online before the meeting date
questions.explanation:
正解は「Email Ms. Tanaka by May 15 to set up another time」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `If you cannot ~ but still want to ~, do X` は**例外時の手順**を示す型。
  「できない + それでも希望する」の2条件が揃ったときの行き先を読む。
- `by May 15` の by は**期限**。「15日までに」。until (継続の終点) との差に注意。
- `arrange another time` は「別の日時を設定する」。arrange は「整えて手配する」が核。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Important points の3つ目:
`[If [you] cannot come [on May 8] but still want [to join]], send [an email] [to Ms. Tanaka] [by May 15].`
  M=If 節 (条件): S=you / V=cannot come と want の2つが but で等位
  主節は命令文: V=send / O=an email / M=to Ms. Tanaka, by May 15
`[She] will arrange [another time] [to meet [you]].`
  S=She / V=will arrange / O=another time / to meet you が O を後置修飾
→ 条件が揃えば「5/15までにメール」→「別日程を組んでもらえる」。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Important points。「If you cannot come on May 8 but still want to join, send an email to Ms. Tanaka by May 15. She will arrange another time to meet you.」
また When and where to apply。「You do not need to sign up before this meeting — just come on the day.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Wait until next term and apply again」… 来学期まで待つという記述は本文に無い。むしろ 5/15 までのメールという当期内の道が用意されている。
- 「Ask another student to attend in his or her place」… 代理出席についての記述は本文に無い。案内は本人がメールで連絡することを求めている。
- 「Sign up online before the meeting date」… 本文は「You do not need to sign up before this meeting — just come on the day.」と、事前登録が不要であることを明示している。正反対。

question_data.passage:
**Greenwood High School Culture Festival — A Blog from the Drama Club**

Hi everyone! This is Mika from the Drama Club. Our school's Culture Festival is finally here, and all the arts clubs want you to come and watch us on the stage in the Main Hall. Here is what we have planned for Saturday, June 6.

We open the day at 10:00 a.m. The Brass Band plays first. They will perform movie themes that I think almost everyone will know, so it is a relaxing way to start. After that, the Dance Club takes the stage at 11:30 a.m. They have been practicing a new routine every lunchtime since April, and even our teachers say it looks amazing.

My own club, the Drama Club, performs in the afternoon at 1:30 p.m. We are doing a short comedy this year instead of the serious play we did last year. We wanted the audience to laugh and relax, because last year a lot of people told us our story was too sad!

The Choir closes the festival at 3:00 p.m. with songs the whole audience can sing along to. If you can only stay for one show, the teachers recommend this one, because it is the most fun when the hall is full.

One more thing: tickets are not needed, but seats fill up fast. Please come about fifteen minutes early to get a good seat. We can't wait to see you there!
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: Why did the Drama Club decide to perform a comedy this year?
choices: Their teachers asked them to make people laugh.
They did not have enough time to practice a serious play.
A comedy is easier to perform than a serious play.
Last year many people felt their play was too sad.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Last year many people felt their play was too sad.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `A instead of B` は「B ではなく A」。**採用されたのは instead of の前**。
- `because` の後ろが理由の本体。ブログ体では**理由が文末に置かれる**ことが多く、
  読み急ぐと落とす。
- `tell 人 that S V` の伝達内容が、そのまま「昨年の評価」になる。
  **誰が誰に言ったか**を押さえると、選択肢の主語すり替えを弾ける。

## 🔬 文構造分析
筆者 Mika の説明:
`[We] are doing [a short comedy] [this year] [instead of the serious play [we did last year]].`
  S=We / V=are doing / O=a short comedy / M=this year, instead of ~
  instead of の O=the serious play (we did last year が関係節で後置修飾)
`[We] wanted [the audience] [to laugh and relax], because [last year] [a lot of people]
 told [us] [(that) our story was too sad]!`
  S=We / V=wanted / O=the audience / C=to laugh and relax
  because 節: S=a lot of people / V=told / O1=us / O2=that 節 (that 省略)
→ 理由は「観客に笑ってほしい」+「昨年**多くの人に**悲しすぎると言われた」。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第3段。「My own club, the Drama Club, performs in the afternoon at 1:30 p.m. We are doing a short comedy this year instead of the serious play we did last year. We wanted the audience to laugh and relax, because last year a lot of people told us our story was too sad!」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Their teachers asked them to make people laugh.」… 教師の依頼という記述は本文に無い。教師が登場するのは「even our teachers say it looks amazing」(ダンス部)と「the teachers recommend this one」(合唱)の2箇所のみ。
- 「They did not have enough time to practice a serious play.」… 練習時間が足りなかったという記述は本文に無い。練習量に触れるのは Dance Club の「practicing a new routine every lunchtime since April」だけ。
- 「A comedy is easier to perform than a serious play.」… 喜劇の方が易しいという記述は本文に無い。理由として挙がるのは観客の反応。

questions.stem: If a visitor can stay for only one performance, what would the writer most likely suggest?
choices: Arriving at 10:00 a.m. for the Brass Band's relaxing opening
Watching the Dance Club's new lunchtime routine at 11:30 a.m.
Coming to the Choir at 3:00 p.m. and sitting in a full hall
Seeing the Drama Club's comedy at 1:30 p.m. in the afternoon
questions.explanation:
正解は「Coming to the Choir at 3:00 p.m. and sitting in a full hall」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `If you can only stay for one show, the teachers recommend this one` の
  `this one` は**直前に述べた公演**を指す。指示語の中身を必ず前に戻して特定する。
- `it is the most fun when the hall is full` は最上級 + when 節。
  「満員のときが一番楽しい」→ **満席で見ることが推奨の内容に含まれる**。
- 「筆者が最も勧めるのは」型は、**推奨を明示した1文だけ**を根拠にする。
  他の公演の魅力的な描写に引きずられない。

## 🔬 文構造分析
最終段の推奨文:
`[If [you] can only stay [for one show]], [the teachers] recommend [this one],
 because [it] is [the most fun] [when [the hall] is [full]].`
  M=If 節 (条件): S=you / V=can stay / M=only, for one show
  主節: S=the teachers / V=recommend / O=this one (=the Choir)
  because 節: S=it / V=is / C=the most fun / M=when 節
  when 節: S=the hall / V=is / C=full
→ this one が指すのは直前文の主語 The Choir。満員であることが「一番楽しい」条件。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第4段。「The Choir closes the festival at 3:00 p.m. with songs the whole audience can sing along to. If you can only stay for one show, the teachers recommend this one, because it is the most fun when the hall is full.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Arriving at 10:00 a.m. for the Brass Band's relaxing opening」… Brass Band は「a relaxing way to start」と紹介されるだけで、1公演だけ見る人への推奨としては挙がっていない。
- 「Watching the Dance Club's new lunchtime routine at 11:30 a.m.」… Dance Club は「even our teachers say it looks amazing」と評価されるが、「1つだけなら」の推奨対象ではない。
- 「Seeing the Drama Club's comedy at 1:30 p.m. in the afternoon」… Drama Club は筆者自身の部だが、「If you can only stay for one show」の推奨は The Choir に向けられている。

question_data.passage:
**Greenwood Hall Dining Survey Results**

Greenwood Hall, one of the largest student dormitories at Maple State University, runs a shared dining hall that serves breakfast and dinner to about 400 residents every day. Last month, the dormitory management team asked all residents to complete an online survey about the dining hall. A total of 312 students replied. The management posted the following summary on the dormitory website so that residents could see the results and decide what to improve first.

When asked how satisfied they were with the dining hall overall, 38% of students said they were "very satisfied," 41% said they were "somewhat satisfied," and the remaining 21% said they were "not satisfied." Students were also asked to choose the single area they most wanted the dining hall to improve. The most common answer was "more vegetarian and vegan choices" (34%), followed by "longer opening hours" (29%), "lower prices" (22%), and "better seating space" (15%). In a separate question, 67% of students said they ate at the dining hall at least five times a week, while only 9% said they almost never used it. Based on these numbers, the management announced that, starting next term, the dinner service would stay open one hour later and that two new plant-based main dishes would be added to the weekly menu. The management also noted that prices would not change for now, because the dining hall already runs at a small loss. To explain the results in more detail, two residents agreed to share their personal comments.

**Daniel (second-year student):**
I eat dinner at Greenwood almost every night because I have practice until late and cooking in my room is impossible. Honestly, the food itself is fine, but the old closing time was my biggest problem. I often arrived just before they stopped serving, and twice I got nothing at all. So I'm really glad the hours are being extended — that change alone makes my week much easier. I do wish there were more vegetarian dishes too, since my roommate is vegetarian and complains a lot, but for me the later hours matter most.

**Sophie (first-year student):**
I think the survey missed something important. The numbers show people want more vegan food, and I agree that's good news, but nobody asked about how the food actually tastes. To me, two new plant-based dishes mean nothing if they are not cooked well. I've eaten there since April, and the vegetables are often overcooked and bland. I'd rather see the staff improve the recipes they already have than simply add new ones. I also don't mind the current prices — they seem reasonable for the portion sizes we get.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: According to the survey summary posted by the management, which statement is a fact rather than an opinion?
choices: Adding two new plant-based dishes will make residents happier with the dining hall.
Twenty-two percent of the students who replied chose lower prices as the area they most wanted to improve.
The dining hall should keep its prices the same because students do not mind them.
Longer opening hours are the change that matters most to the residents.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Twenty-two percent of the students who replied chose lower prices as the area they most wanted to improve.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- **事実 (fact) と意見 (opinion) の切り分け**は、①数値・出典があるか ②検証できるか の2点。
  `should` / `will make ~ happier` / `matters most` はいずれも書き手の判断 = 意見。
- `the area they most wanted the dining hall to improve` は関係節で the area を修飾。
  `want O to V` (O に V してほしい) が節の中に埋まっている。
- 調査結果型では、**%付きの記述だけが事実**と割り切ってよい。

## 🔬 文構造分析
調査結果の列挙文:
`[The most common answer] was ["more vegetarian and vegan choices" (34%)], followed by
 ["longer opening hours" (29%)], ["lower prices" (22%)], and ["better seating space" (15%)].`
  S=The most common answer / V=was / C="more vegetarian and vegan choices"
  followed by ~ は分詞構文で、順位の続きを並べる
設問側の選択肢:
`[Twenty-two percent of the students [who replied]] chose [lower prices] [as the area
 [they most wanted to improve]].`
  S=Twenty-two percent of the students who replied / V=chose / O=lower prices
  M=as ~ (資格・位置づけ)
→ 数値 22% が本文の "lower prices" (22%) と一致する。検証可能 = 事実。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段の調査結果。「The most common answer was "more vegetarian and vegan choices" (34%), followed by "longer opening hours" (29%), "lower prices" (22%), and "better seating space" (15%).」
22% という数値がそのまま示されており、誰の判断も入っていない。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Adding two new plant-based dishes will make residents happier with the dining hall.」… 「will make residents happier」は**これから起きること**の予測。まだ起きていないので検証できず、意見にあたる。
- 「The dining hall should keep its prices the same because students do not mind them.」… 「should keep」は当為 (〜すべきだ) の助動詞。価格据え置きの是非は判断であり、意見。なお「students do not mind them」も Sophie 個人の感想。
- 「Longer opening hours are the change that matters most to the residents.」… 「the change that matters most」は重要度の順位づけ。調査では longer opening hours は 29% で 1 位ではなく、しかも「最も重要」は評価語。

questions.stem: What did the management decide to do based on the survey results?
choices: Lower the price of meals because the dining hall earns a profit.
Close the dining hall on days when fewer than 400 residents eat there.
Keep dinner service open one hour later and add two plant-based main dishes.
Replace all current dishes with newly developed vegetarian recipes.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Keep dinner service open one hour later and add two plant-based main dishes.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `announced that A and that B` は that 節を2つ並べた形。**2つ目の that を省略しない**
  のは、どこまでが発表内容かを明示するため。
- `stay open one hour later` は「1時間遅くまで開いている」。
  比較級 later が**従来との差**を表す。
- 発表内容を問う型は、**決定したこと**と**しないと明言したこと**を両方拾う。
  ここでは「価格は変えない」も重要な決定。

## 🔬 文構造分析
管理側の発表:
`[the management] announced [that, starting next term, [the dinner service] would stay
 [open] [one hour later]] and [that [two new plant-based main dishes] would be added
 [to the weekly menu]].`
  S=the management / V=announced / O=that 節 × 2 (and で等位)
  節1: S=the dinner service / V=would stay / C=open / M=one hour later
  節2: S=two new plant-based main dishes / V=would be added (受動) / M=to the weekly menu
補足: `[prices] would not change [for now], because [the dining hall] already runs [at a small loss].`
  S=prices / V=would not change / M=for now
  because 節: S=the dining hall / V=runs / M=at a small loss (わずかな赤字で運営)

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段。「Based on these numbers, the management announced that, starting next term, the dinner service would stay open one hour later and that two new plant-based main dishes would be added to the weekly menu. The management also noted that prices would not change for now, because the dining hall already runs at a small loss.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Lower the price of meals because the dining hall earns a profit.」… 価格は「prices would not change for now」= 据え置き。しかも理由は「the dining hall already runs at a small loss」= 赤字であり、利益が出ているという前提が本文と逆。
- 「Close the dining hall on days when fewer than 400 residents eat there.」… 利用者数による休業という記述は本文に無い。400 は「serves breakfast and dinner to about 400 residents」= 寮生の総数。
- 「Replace all current dishes with newly developed vegetarian recipes.」… 追加されるのは「two new plant-based main dishes」= 2品。既存メニューの全面入れ替えではない。

questions.stem: Which of the following best matches Daniel's opinion about the dining hall?
choices: Cooking meals in his own room is a good alternative to eating at the hall.
The dining hall needs more vegetarian dishes more than anything else.
The food at the dining hall tastes bad and the recipes should be improved.
The most useful change for him personally is the extension of the opening hours.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The most useful change for him personally is the extension of the opening hours.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 個人の意見を問う型は、**その人が自分で優先順位を宣言した文**を探す。
  `for me ~ matter most` / `my biggest problem` が最上級の目印。
- `I do wish there were ~` の do は強調。were は仮定法過去で「実際はそうでない」含み。
  **願望ではあるが最優先ではない**という温度差が読める。
- `that change alone` の alone は「それだけで」。**限定の副詞が後ろから名詞に掛かる**用法。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Daniel の優先順位の宣言:
`[the old closing time] was [my biggest problem]`
  S=the old closing time / V=was / C=my biggest problem
`[I]'m really glad [the hours are being extended] — [that change alone] makes [my week] [much easier].`
  S=I / V=am / C=glad + that 節 (that 省略)
  ダッシュ以下: S=that change alone / V=makes / O=my week / C=much easier
締め: `but [for me] [the later hours] matter [most].`
  M=for me / S=the later hours / V=matter / M=most
→ biggest problem → makes my week much easier → matter most と、三度も同じ順位を宣言している。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Daniel のコメント。「Honestly, the food itself is fine, but the old closing time was my biggest problem.」
「So I'm really glad the hours are being extended — that change alone makes my week much easier.」
「I do wish there were more vegetarian dishes too, since my roommate is vegetarian and complains a lot, but for me the later hours matter most.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Cooking meals in his own room is a good alternative to eating at the hall.」… Daniel は「cooking in my room is impossible」と述べており、自室調理は選択肢になっていない。正反対。
- 「The dining hall needs more vegetarian dishes more than anything else.」… ベジタリアン料理については「I do wish there were more vegetarian dishes too」と望むにとどまり、直後に「but for me the later hours matter most」と順位を明示している。最優先ではない。
- 「The food at the dining hall tastes bad and the recipes should be improved.」… Daniel は「the food itself is fine」= 料理自体は問題ないと述べている。まずいと言っているのは Sophie。

questions.stem: On what point would Sophie most likely disagree with the management's response to the survey?
choices: She believes adding new vegan dishes is pointless unless the cooking quality improves.
She thinks the dining hall should lower its current prices right away.
She wants the dining hall to close earlier rather than stay open longer.
She argues that too few students responded for the survey to be trusted.
questions.explanation:
正解は「She believes adding new vegan dishes is pointless unless the cooking quality improves.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「どの点で反対しそうか」型は、**相手の決定内容**と**その人の主張**を突き合わせる。
  管理側の決定は「新メニュー2品追加」「時間延長」「価格据え置き」の3つ。
- `A mean nothing if they are not cooked well` は条件節付きの否定。
  「うまく調理されなければ意味がない」= **追加そのものへの疑義**。
- `would rather A than B` は「B より A の方がよい」。**A が主張、B が退ける側**。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Sophie の中心主張:
`[two new plant-based dishes] mean [nothing] [if [they] are not cooked [well]].`
  S=two new plant-based dishes / V=mean / O=nothing / M=if 節 (条件)
  if 節: S=they / V=are not cooked / M=well
`[I]'d rather see [the staff] [improve the recipes [they already have]] than simply add [new ones].`
  S=I / V=would rather see / O=the staff / C=improve ~ (原形不定詞)
  比較の than 以下: (rather than) add / O=new ones
→ 「追加より改善」。管理側が決めた「2品追加」と正面から食い違う。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Sophie のコメント。「To me, two new plant-based dishes mean nothing if they are not cooked well. I've eaten there since April, and the vegetables are often overcooked and bland. I'd rather see the staff improve the recipes they already have than simply add new ones.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「She thinks the dining hall should lower its current prices right away.」… Sophie は「I also don't mind the current prices — they seem reasonable for the portion sizes we get」と述べ、据え置きに賛同している。値下げは求めていない。
- 「She wants the dining hall to close earlier rather than stay open longer.」… 閉店時間についての言及は Sophie のコメントに無い。時間延長を歓迎しているのは Daniel。
- 「She argues that too few students responded for the survey to be trusted.」… 回答者数への疑義は本大問の Sophie ではなく、別の話題。Sophie が問題にしたのは「nobody asked about how the food actually tastes」= 設問項目の欠落であって回答数ではない。

question_data.passage:
You are a member of the Greenfield High School Library Club. The library staff has posted a notice about new opening hours, along with comments from two students who use the library.

NOTICE: New Library Opening Hours from October

Starting in October, the Greenfield High School Library will change its opening hours. From Monday to Friday, the library will open one hour later, at 9:00 a.m. instead of 8:00 a.m., but it will stay open three hours longer in the evening, closing at 8:00 p.m. instead of 5:00 p.m. On Saturdays, the library will now open from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. It was closed on Saturdays before. The library will remain closed on Sundays.

We decided to make these changes after collecting opinions from more than 300 students last spring. Many students told us they could not use the library after club activities, which usually finish around 6:00 p.m. We hope the new evening hours will help these students. Please note that the study rooms on the second floor must now be reserved online at least one day in advance. Drinks in closed bottles are now allowed in the reading area, but food is still not permitted anywhere in the library.

Mark (Grade 11):
I am really happy about the new hours because I belong to the soccer team, and our practice ends at six o'clock. Before, the library was already closed by the time I finished, so I had to study at home, where my younger brothers are always noisy. Now I can stay and concentrate until eight. The one thing I am not sure about is the new rule for the study rooms. Last week I wanted a quiet room right after practice, but I could not book one because I forgot to reserve it the day before. I think students should be able to reserve a room on the same day if there are empty seats.

Lisa (Grade 12):
The longer evening hours are not very useful for me because I go to a cram school three evenings a week and have to leave school early. What I really wanted was for the library to open earlier in the morning, since I like to review my lessons before class. Opening at nine instead of eight actually makes my mornings harder. However, I am glad the library is finally open on Saturdays. I live far from any public library, so having a place to study near home on weekends will be a big help for me before the university entrance exams.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: According to the notice, which change will the library make starting in October?
choices: The library will open later on weekdays and stay open three more hours in the evening.
The library will open earlier on weekday mornings and close earlier in the evening.
The library will close one hour later on weekday mornings but stay open until the evening.
The library will be open every day of the week, including Sundays.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The library will open later on weekdays and stay open three more hours in the evening.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `A instead of B` は「B ではなく A」。時刻の変更は**この形で新旧を並べる**のが定型。
- `open one hour later` と `stay open three hours longer` は方向が逆の変化。
  **朝は遅く、夜は長く**という組み合わせを取り違えないこと。
- `remain closed` は「閉まったまま」。remain は状態の継続で、**変更が無い**ことを示す。

## 🔬 文構造分析
お知らせの中心文:
`[the library] will open [one hour later], [at 9:00 a.m. instead of 8:00 a.m.], but
 [it] will stay [open] [three hours longer] [in the evening], closing [at 8:00 p.m.
 instead of 5:00 p.m.].`
  前半: S=the library / V=will open / M=one hour later (at ~ が同格で具体化)
  後半: S=it / V=will stay / C=open / M=three hours longer, in the evening
  closing ~ は分詞構文で結果を添える
→ 朝は「1時間遅く」、夜は「3時間長く」。両方の方向を保った選択肢だけが正しい。

## 📍 本文の根拠
NOTICE の第1段。「From Monday to Friday, the library will open one hour later, at 9:00 a.m. instead of 8:00 a.m., but it will stay open three hours longer in the evening, closing at 8:00 p.m. instead of 5:00 p.m. On Saturdays, the library will now open from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. It was closed on Saturdays before. The library will remain closed on Sundays.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The library will open earlier on weekday mornings and close earlier in the evening.」… 朝は「open one hour later」= 遅くなるので earlier は逆。夜も「stay open three hours longer」= 延長なので close earlier も逆。二重に誤り。
- 「The library will close one hour later on weekday mornings but stay open until the evening.」… 「close one hour later on weekday mornings」は日本語にすると「朝に1時間遅く閉まる」で意味を成さない。本文は開館が1時間遅くなると述べている。
- 「The library will be open every day of the week, including Sundays.」… 「The library will remain closed on Sundays」= 日曜は引き続き休館。毎日は成立しない。

questions.stem: Why did the library decide to change its opening hours?
choices: Because students complained that the study rooms were always full.
Because many students could not use the library after their club activities ended.
Because the staff wanted to allow students to eat and drink in the library.
Because more than 300 students asked the library to open on Sundays.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Because many students could not use the library after their club activities ended.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 変更理由を問う型は `We decided to ~ after ~` / `Many students told us ~` のような
  **根拠を示す定型文**を探す。
- `which usually finish around 6:00 p.m.` の which は前の club activities を受ける
  **非制限用法**の関係代名詞。補足説明であり、限定ではない。
- 数値 (300人) は**意見を集めた規模**であって、要望の中身ではない。
  数値の役割を取り違えると誤答に引っかかる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
理由の中心文:
`[Many students] told [us] [(that) [they] could not use [the library] [after club activities],
 [which usually finish [around 6:00 p.m.]]].`
  S=Many students / V=told / O1=us / O2=that 節 (that 省略)
  節内: S=they / V=could not use / O=the library / M=after club activities
  which 節 (非制限): S=which (=club activities) / V=finish / M=around 6:00 p.m.
→ 「部活後に使えない」が理由。which 節はその部活が6時ごろ終わるという補足。

## 📍 本文の根拠
NOTICE の第2段。「We decided to make these changes after collecting opinions from more than 300 students last spring. Many students told us they could not use the library after club activities, which usually finish around 6:00 p.m. We hope the new evening hours will help these students.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Because students complained that the study rooms were always full.」… 自習室が満室という苦情は本文に無い。自習室に触れるのは「must now be reserved online at least one day in advance」= 予約制の告知のみ。
- 「Because the staff wanted to allow students to eat and drink in the library.」… 飲食については「Drinks in closed bottles are now allowed in the reading area, but food is still not permitted anywhere」= 規則の説明であって、時間変更の理由ではない。
- 「Because more than 300 students asked the library to open on Sundays.」… 300人超は「collecting opinions from more than 300 students」= 意見を集めた人数。日曜開館を求めたわけではなく、日曜は引き続き休館。

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses Lisa's opinion about the changes?
choices: The new evening hours are a great improvement for students who join club activities.
Reserving study rooms one day in advance is a fair and helpful rule.
The later morning opening is inconvenient, but the new Saturday hours are welcome.
The library should stop allowing drinks because they make the reading area dirty.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The later morning opening is inconvenient, but the new Saturday hours are welcome.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「その人の意見はどれか」型は、**発言者ごとに ○ / × を仕分ける**のが基本。
  片方が合っていても、もう片方が別人の意見なら不正解。
- `A is not very useful for me because ~` は**やんわりした否定**。
  「あまり役に立たない」= 恩恵を受けていない側。
- `However, I am glad ~` の However が**評価の反転点**。
  1人のコメントの中に不満と歓迎が同居する型で、両方を拾った選択肢が正解。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Lisa の不満:
`Opening [at nine instead of eight] actually makes [my mornings] [harder].`
  S=Opening at nine instead of eight (動名詞句が主語) / V=makes / O=my mornings / C=harder
Lisa の歓迎:
`However, [I] am [glad [(that) the library is finally open [on Saturdays]]].`
  S=I / V=am / C=glad + that 節 (that 省略)
  節内: S=the library / V=is / C=open / M=finally, on Saturdays
→ 「朝が遅くなって不便」+「土曜開館は嬉しい」。この2点を両方含む選択肢を選ぶ。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Lisa のコメント。「What I really wanted was for the library to open earlier in the morning, since I like to review my lessons before class. Opening at nine instead of eight actually makes my mornings harder. However, I am glad the library is finally open on Saturdays.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The new evening hours are a great improvement for students who join club activities.」… 夜の延長を歓迎しているのは Mark (「Now I can stay and concentrate until eight」)。Lisa は「The longer evening hours are not very useful for me」と述べている。人物が逆。
- 「Reserving study rooms one day in advance is a fair and helpful rule.」… 前日予約の規則に不満を述べているのは Mark (「I think students should be able to reserve a room on the same day」)。Lisa は自習室に触れていない。
- 「The library should stop allowing drinks because they make the reading area dirty.」… 飲み物についての意見は Lisa も Mark も述べていない。本文にあるのは規則の告知のみ。

question_data.passage:
Your student council is reviewing the school's uniform policy. Last month, the council posted the following notice and survey results on the school website, along with two student comments.

NOTICE FROM THE STUDENT COUNCIL
Thank you to everyone who answered our online survey about the school uniform. We received responses from 480 students in all three grades. The council will present these results to the school board next week. Here is what we found.

We asked, "Should students be allowed to choose between a uniform and free clothing?" In response, 62% answered "yes," 25% answered "no," and 13% answered "not sure." We also asked which single change students most wanted. The most popular answer, chosen by 41%, was permission to wear the school's sports jacket on cold days. The second most popular, at 33%, was a free choice of trousers or a skirt regardless of gender. Only 9% asked for a completely new uniform design.

When we asked students to give one reason for keeping the uniform, the most common reason written in was "it saves time in the morning." When we asked for one reason against it, the most common was "the fabric is uncomfortable in summer." The council has not yet decided what to recommend; we will hold an open meeting on July 3 before writing our final report.

Comment from Mei (Grade 11):
I voted to keep the uniform, but I still think it needs changes. Last winter I was often cold because we are not allowed to wear our sports jacket in the hallways, even when the heating is weak. A friend of mine caught a cold in January, and she blamed the thin blazer. I am glad that wearing the sports jacket was the change most students wanted, because that shows I am not alone. I do not want to throw the uniform away. I just want a sensible rule that lets us stay warm and healthy.

Comment from Daniel (Grade 12):
Honestly, I think the survey question was unfair. Asking "uniform or free clothing" makes it sound like an all-or-nothing choice, so people who only wanted small changes had to pick a side. I would have preferred questions about each specific item. Also, I doubt 480 replies really speak for the whole school of over 1,200 students. I am not against keeping a uniform, and I actually like how it looks. My worry is only that the council may treat these numbers as the final voice of every student, when in fact many never replied at all.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: According to the notice, what will the student council do after collecting the survey results?
choices: Immediately design a completely new uniform for all grades.
Hold an open meeting before writing its final report to the board.
Cancel the current uniform policy starting next week.
Send a second survey to the students who did not reply.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Hold an open meeting before writing its final report to the board.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `has not yet decided ~; we will ~` のセミコロンは、**前の文を受けて次の行動を述べる**。
  「まだ決めていない → だからこうする」の関係。
- `before writing our final report` は前置詞 + 動名詞で**順序**を示す。
  「最終報告を書く前に」= 公開会議が先。
- 「この後どうするか」型は、**未来を表す表現 (will / going to)** に印を付けて拾う。

## 🔬 文構造分析
告知の締めくくり:
`[The council] has not yet decided [what to recommend]; [we] will hold [an open meeting]
 [on July 3] [before writing [our final report]].`
  前半: S=The council / V=has not decided / O=what to recommend (疑問詞 + 不定詞)
  後半: S=we / V=will hold / O=an open meeting / M=on July 3, before writing ~
→ 「未決」→「7/3 に公開会議」→「最終報告」という時系列が1文に収まっている。

## 📍 本文の根拠
NOTICE の第3段。「The council has not yet decided what to recommend; we will hold an open meeting on July 3 before writing our final report.」
また第1段。「The council will present these results to the school board next week.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Immediately design a completely new uniform for all grades.」… 新デザインは「Only 9% asked for a completely new uniform design」= 要望として少数だったにとどまり、作成の予定は述べられていない。
- 「Cancel the current uniform policy starting next week.」… 制服方針の廃止は本文に無い。来週予定されているのは「present these results to the school board」= 結果の提出。
- 「Send a second survey to the students who did not reply.」… 再調査という記述は本文に無い。未回答者に触れたのは Daniel のコメント (「many never replied at all」) であり、生徒会の予定ではない。

questions.stem: Which of the following is a fact stated in the notice rather than an opinion expressed by a student?
choices: The survey question forced students into an all-or-nothing choice.
The uniform fabric is too uncomfortable to wear in summer.
A free choice of trousers or a skirt was the second most requested change.
Students should be allowed to wear the sports jacket to stay healthy.
questions.explanation:
正解は「A free choice of trousers or a skirt was the second most requested change.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 事実 / 意見の切り分けは**「誰が言ったか」と「数値があるか」**の2点で決まる。
  お知らせ本体の%付き記述 = 事実、生徒コメントの評価 = 意見。
- `The second most popular, at 33%, was ~` は挿入句 (at 33%) が数値を添える形。
  **順位 + 数値**が揃えば検証可能。
- 調査で「書き込まれた意見」を紹介する文 (the most common reason written in was ~) は、
  **意見の紹介**であって告知が断定する事実ではない。ここが引っかけになる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
告知の事実文:
`[The second most popular], [at 33%], was [a free choice of trousers or a skirt
 [regardless of gender]].`
  S=The second most popular / V=was / C=a free choice of trousers or a skirt
  挿入=at 33% / M=regardless of gender (性別を問わず)
対して意見の紹介文:
`[the most common reason [written in]] was ["the fabric is uncomfortable in summer"]`
  S=the most common reason written in / V=was / C=引用された生徒の書き込み
→ 後者は「そういう意見が多かった」という報告で、内容自体は生徒の判断。

## 📍 本文の根拠
NOTICE の第2段。「The second most popular, at 33%, was a free choice of trousers or a skirt regardless of gender. Only 9% asked for a completely new uniform design.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The survey question forced students into an all-or-nothing choice.」… これは Daniel の「Asking "uniform or free clothing" makes it sound like an all-or-nothing choice」という主張。生徒個人の評価であり意見。
- 「The uniform fabric is too uncomfortable to wear in summer.」… これは調査に書き込まれた生徒の意見の紹介 (「the most common reason was "the fabric is uncomfortable in summer"」)。快適かどうかは主観であり、告知が断定する事実ではない。
- 「Students should be allowed to wear the sports jacket to stay healthy.」… 「should be allowed」は当為の助動詞。Mei の「I just want a sensible rule that lets us stay warm and healthy」に対応する意見。

questions.stem: What is Mei's main point in her comment?
choices: The uniform should be abolished and replaced with free clothing.
A completely new uniform design should be the council's top priority.
The survey did not include enough students to be trusted.
The uniform should be kept, but a rule allowing the sports jacket is needed.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The uniform should be kept, but a rule allowing the sports jacket is needed.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 主張を問う型は**「否定 + 肯定」のセット**を探す。
  `I do not want A. I just want B.` の B が主張の核。
- `just` は「ただ〜だけ」。**要求の範囲を限定する**副詞で、過激な主張ではないことを示す。
- `a rule that lets us stay warm` の let は使役動詞。`let O V(原形)` で「O が V するのを許す」。
  **許可を求めている**のであって、制度の廃止を求めているのではない。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Mei の主張:
`[I] do not want [to throw the uniform away]. [I] just want [a sensible rule
 [that lets [us] [stay warm and healthy]]].`
  文1: S=I / V=do not want / O=to throw the uniform away
  文2: S=I / V=want / O=a sensible rule / M=just
  関係節: S=that (=rule) / V=lets / O=us / C=stay warm and healthy (原形不定詞)
冒頭も同じ構え: `[I] voted [to keep the uniform], but [I] still think [(that) [it] needs [changes]].`
  S=I / V=voted / O=to keep the uniform ｜ 逆接: S=I / V=think / O=that 節
→ 「維持」+「ただし規則の変更」。両方を含む選択肢が正解。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Mei のコメント。「I voted to keep the uniform, but I still think it needs changes. Last winter I was often cold because we are not allowed to wear our sports jacket in the hallways, even when the heating is weak.」
「I do not want to throw the uniform away. I just want a sensible rule that lets us stay warm and healthy.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The uniform should be abolished and replaced with free clothing.」… Mei は「I do not want to throw the uniform away」と明言している。廃止は正反対。
- 「A completely new uniform design should be the council's top priority.」… 新デザインを最優先とする主張は誰もしていない。調査でも「Only 9% asked for a completely new uniform design」と少数。
- 「The survey did not include enough students to be trusted.」… 回答数への疑義は Daniel の主張 (「I doubt 480 replies really speak for the whole school」)。Mei ではない。

questions.stem: Why does Daniel question the value of the survey?
choices: He believes the results may not represent students who never replied.
He dislikes the appearance of the current uniform and wants it changed.
He thinks the council asked too many detailed questions about each item.
He is firmly opposed to keeping any kind of school uniform.
questions.explanation:
正解は「He believes the results may not represent students who never replied.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `I doubt (that) S V` は「〜ではないと思う」。**doubt は否定を含む動詞**。
  suspect (そうだと思う) と方向が逆なので注意。
- `speak for ~` は「〜を代弁する」。調査の代表性を問題にする定型表現。
- `My worry is only that ~` の only が**懸念の範囲を限定**する。
  「制服そのものには反対でない」という留保とセットで読む。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Daniel の懸念:
`[I] doubt [(that) [480 replies] really speak [for the whole school of over 1,200 students]].`
  S=I / V=doubt / O=that 節 (that 省略)
  節内: S=480 replies / V=speak / M=really, for the whole school of over 1,200 students
締めの文:
`[My worry] is only [that [the council] may treat [these numbers] [as the final voice of
 every student], [when in fact many never replied at all]].`
  S=My worry / V=is / C=that 節 / M=only
  節内: S=the council / V=may treat / O=these numbers / M=as ~ (〜として扱う)
→ 480 対 1,200 という数の差が、代表性への疑義の根拠になっている。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Daniel のコメント。「Also, I doubt 480 replies really speak for the whole school of over 1,200 students.」
「My worry is only that the council may treat these numbers as the final voice of every student, when in fact many never replied at all.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「He dislikes the appearance of the current uniform and wants it changed.」… Daniel は「I actually like how it looks」= 見た目は好きだと述べている。正反対。
- 「He thinks the council asked too many detailed questions about each item.」… Daniel は「I would have preferred questions about each specific item」= むしろ項目ごとの質問を望んでいる。多すぎると批判したのではなく、逆。
- 「He is firmly opposed to keeping any kind of school uniform.」… Daniel は「I am not against keeping a uniform」と明言している。制服反対ではない。

question_data.passage:
Greenfield Online Academy ran a survey from May 6 to May 20 asking the 312 students who had taken at least one of its live online classes this term to share their experiences. The results are now posted on our website, and we have invited two students to add their own comments below.

Survey Results
- 78% of students said they joined classes from home, while 22% joined from places such as a relative's house, a café, or a public library.
- When asked about the biggest benefit, 41% chose "saving travel time," 33% chose "being able to rewatch the recording," and 19% chose "asking questions in the chat box without feeling shy." The remaining 7% chose "other."
- 64% reported that their internet connection cut out at least once during a class this term.
- Only 28% said they had spoken aloud using a microphone more than three times. Many wrote that they preferred typing.
- 88% said they would recommend at least one online class to a friend, but 52% added that they would not want all of their classes to be online.

Comment from Mei
I live forty minutes by bus from the academy, so the online classes have changed my week completely. I used to arrive tired, and now I use that time to review my notes instead. The part I value most is the recording. Last month I was sick for three days, yet I did not fall behind because I watched every missed lesson at night.
