Honestly, I still feel nervous about turning on my microphone, so I almost always type my questions. The teachers answer typed questions just as carefully, which is why typing suits me.

Comment from Daniel
I joined the academy hoping to meet other students who love science, and at first the online format worried me. The chat box surprised me, though. Because I can write a question the moment I think of it, I now ask far more than I ever did in a normal classroom. That said, my home internet is not reliable, so I sometimes lose the audio in the middle of an explanation. When that happens the recording saves me, but I wish the academy would also share a short written summary after each class so that students with weak connections are not left guessing.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: What is one fact reported in the survey results, rather than an opinion?
choices: Most students believe online classes are better than classroom lessons.
More than half of the students experienced their internet cutting out at least once.
Typing questions is the most effective way to learn in an online class.
Every student would recommend an online class to a friend.
questions.explanation:
正解は「More than half of the students experienced their internet cutting out at least once.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 事実は**%で示され検証できるもの**。`better` / `most effective` は比較の評価語で意見。
- `more than half` は「半分より多い」。64% がこれに当たるかを**数で確認**する。
- `Every / All` のような**全称の語**は、本文の数値 (88%) と噛み合わなければ即座に切れる。
  全称と部分の差は、共通テストで最も安定した切り口。

## 🔬 文構造分析
調査結果の該当行:
`[64%] reported [(that) [their internet connection] cut out [at least once] [during a class]
 [this term]].`
  S=64% / V=reported / O=that 節 (that 省略)
  節内: S=their internet connection / V=cut out / M=at least once, during a class, this term
選択肢側:
`[More than half of the students] experienced [their internet cutting out [at least once]].`
  S=More than half of the students / V=experienced / O=their internet cutting out (動名詞句・
  their internet が意味上の主語)
→ 64% は half (50%) を超える。数値の言い換えとして正しい。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Survey Results の箇条書き。「64% reported that their internet connection cut out at least once during a class this term.」
「88% said they would recommend at least one online class to a friend, but 52% added that they would not want all of their classes to be online.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Most students believe online classes are better than classroom lessons.」… 「better than classroom lessons」という比較評価は調査項目に無い。むしろ 52% が「would not want all of their classes to be online」と答えている。
- 「Typing questions is the most effective way to learn in an online class.」… 「most effective」は効果の順位づけであり評価。調査が示すのは「Many wrote that they preferred typing」= 好みであって効果ではない。
- 「Every student would recommend an online class to a friend.」… 推薦したのは 88% であって Every student ではない。全称に置き換えた時点で誤り。

questions.stem: Which statement best matches what both Mei and Daniel say in their comments?
choices: Both of them say they have stopped feeling nervous about using a microphone.
Both of them prefer joining classes from a public library rather than from home.
Both of them feel that recordings have helped them when they could not follow a class normally.
Both of them want every class at the academy to be held online.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Both of them feel that recordings have helped them when they could not follow a class normally.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「両者に共通するのは」型は、**二人のコメントを別々に要約してから重ねる**。
  片方だけが述べた内容を選ぶのが最も多い誤答パターン。
- `I did not fall behind because I watched every missed lesson` と
  `the recording saves me` は、**表現は違うが同じ機能**(録画に助けられた)を語っている。
  言い換えを見抜くのがこの型の核心。
- `yet` は逆接の接続詞 (but と同義)。「病気だった、それでも遅れなかった」。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Mei の該当文:
`Last month [I] was [sick] [for three days], yet [I] did not fall [behind] because
 [I] watched [every missed lesson] [at night].`
  S=I / V=was / C=sick / M=for three days
  逆接 yet: S=I / V=did not fall / M=behind
  because 節: S=I / V=watched / O=every missed lesson / M=at night
Daniel の該当文:
`When [that] happens [the recording] saves [me]`
  M=When 節 (時): S=that / V=happens
  主節: S=the recording / V=saves / O=me
→ 一方は欠席、他方は音声途切れ。**授業を追えなかった場面で録画に救われた**点で一致する。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Mei のコメント。「The part I value most is the recording. Last month I was sick for three days, yet I did not fall behind because I watched every missed lesson at night.」
Daniel のコメント。「my home internet is not reliable, so I sometimes lose the audio in the middle of an explanation. When that happens the recording saves me」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Both of them say they have stopped feeling nervous about using a microphone.」… Mei は「I still feel nervous about turning on my microphone」と現在も緊張していると述べている。Daniel はマイクに触れていない。両者ともに当てはまらない。
- 「Both of them prefer joining classes from a public library rather than from home.」… 図書館から参加すると述べた学生はコメントに現れない。Mei は通学時間の話 (「I live forty minutes by bus」)、Daniel は自宅回線の話をしている。
- 「Both of them want every class at the academy to be held online.」… 全授業のオンライン化を望むとは両者とも述べていない。調査では 52% が「would not want all of their classes to be online」と答えている。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about why Mei usually types her questions instead of speaking?
choices: She believes typed questions receive less careful answers than spoken ones.
Her bus ride leaves her too tired to speak during class.
The academy does not allow students to use microphones in class.
She still feels uneasy about using her microphone, but finds typing works well for her.
questions.explanation:
正解は「She still feels uneasy about using her microphone, but finds typing works well for her.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 理由の推論は、**本人が並べた2文の因果**をそのまま拾えばよい。
  `I still feel nervous ~, so I almost always type` の so が因果を明示している。
- `which is why S V` は「そういうわけで〜」。**前文全体を受ける関係代名詞**。
  ここでは「丁寧に答えてもらえる → だからタイプが合う」。
- `just as carefully` の as は同等比較。「(話す場合と) 同じくらい丁寧に」。
  **劣っているとは述べていない**点が誤答の分かれ目。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Mei の説明:
`Honestly, [I] still feel [nervous] [about turning on my microphone], so [I] almost always
 type [my questions].`
  S=I / V=feel / C=nervous / M=still, about turning on my microphone
  結果節: S=I / V=type / O=my questions / M=almost always
`[The teachers] answer [typed questions] [just as carefully], [which is why typing suits me].`
  S=The teachers / V=answer / O=typed questions / M=just as carefully
  which 節: S=which (=前文全体) / V=is / C=why typing suits me
→ 「緊張する」→「タイプする」→「同じくらい丁寧に答えてもらえる」→「だから合っている」。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Mei のコメント。「Honestly, I still feel nervous about turning on my microphone, so I almost always type my questions. The teachers answer typed questions just as carefully, which is why typing suits me.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「She believes typed questions receive less careful answers than spoken ones.」… Mei は「The teachers answer typed questions just as carefully」= 同じくらい丁寧だと述べている。劣るという読みは正反対。
- 「Her bus ride leaves her too tired to speak during class.」… バスで疲れる話は「I used to arrive tired, and now I use that time to review my notes instead」= 通学していた頃の話。オンラインになった今の発言と時制がずれている。
- 「The academy does not allow students to use microphones in class.」… マイクの使用禁止という記述は本文に無い。調査でも「Only 28% said they had spoken aloud using a microphone more than three times」= 使う学生は存在する。

questions.stem: What does Daniel suggest the academy should do?
choices: Provide a short written summary after each class for students with poor connections.
Stop posting recordings because they make students lazy.
Require all students to turn on their microphones during class.
Move the science classes back to a normal classroom.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Provide a short written summary after each class for students with poor connections.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 提案を問う型は `I wish ~ would V` / `should` などの**願望・当為の形**を探す。
- `I wish the academy would also share ~` の would は**まだ実現していないこと**への願望。
  also が「録画に加えて」という追加であることを示す。
- `so that S are not left guessing` は目的の副詞節。`leave O ~ing` は「O を〜のままにする」。
  **なぜその提案が要るか**が節の中に書かれている。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Daniel の提案:
`[I] wish [(that) [the academy] would also share [a short written summary] [after each class]
 [so that [students with weak connections] are not left [guessing]]].`
  S=I / V=wish / O=that 節 (that 省略)
  節内: S=the academy / V=would share / O=a short written summary / M=also, after each class
  so that 節: S=students with weak connections / V=are not left / C=guessing (受動 + 分詞)
→ 求めているのは「各授業後の短い文章のまとめ」。録画の**置き換え**ではなく**追加**。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Daniel のコメント。「my home internet is not reliable, so I sometimes lose the audio in the middle of an explanation. When that happens the recording saves me, but I wish the academy would also share a short written summary after each class so that students with weak connections are not left guessing.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Stop posting recordings because they make students lazy.」… Daniel は「the recording saves me」と録画に助けられたと述べている。廃止を求めるのは正反対。
- 「Require all students to turn on their microphones during class.」… マイクの義務化という記述は無い。Daniel が評価しているのは「The chat box surprised me」= 文字で質問できる点。
- 「Move the science classes back to a normal classroom.」… 対面教室への回帰は述べていない。「at first the online format worried me」と当初の不安を語ったうえで、チャットの利点を認めている。

question_data.passage:
Your local citizen gym, Greenfield Community Fitness Center, posted the following notice and survey results on its website.

**Greenfield Community Fitness Center — Member Satisfaction Survey 2026**

Thank you to the 480 members who answered our annual survey last month. We share the main results below so that everyone can see how we plan to improve the center this year.

When we asked members what they liked most, the friendly staff received the highest praise (62%), followed by the clean changing rooms (58%) and the low monthly fee (51%). However, two problems were mentioned by many members. First, 45% said the machines in the weight room are often all in use during the evening, between 6 p.m. and 9 p.m. Second, 38% said the swimming pool is too cold in winter.

Based on these results, we will take two actions. From July, we will buy six new running machines and place them in a second room on the first floor. From September, we will raise the pool's water temperature by two degrees during the winter months. The monthly fee will not change. We will also start an online booking system so that members can reserve a machine before they arrive.

We asked two long-time members to share their honest thoughts.

**Mr. Tanaka (member for 8 years):**
I come to the gym almost every evening after work, so the crowded weight room is a real problem for me. Many times I have waited twenty minutes just to use one machine, which is frustrating after a long day. I think buying new running machines is a smart first step, but honestly, running machines are not what the evening crowd fights over — we all want the weight machines. I hope the center will count how many people actually wait each evening before deciding that six running machines are enough. The booking system sounds useful, though I worry some members will reserve a machine and then not come.

**Ms. Lopez (member for 3 years):**
I mainly use the pool, and I am very happy that the water will finally be warmer in winter. Last January I stopped swimming for three weeks because the water was simply too cold for me. What I value most about this gym, however, is the price. My old gym charged almost double, so keeping the fee the same is the best news in this notice. I would gladly pay a little more if it meant longer pool hours on weekends, but I understand that many members are on a tight budget. The new booking system may help the pool too, since the lanes also get busy on Sunday mornings.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: According to the survey results reported by the center, which statement is a fact rather than an opinion?
choices: The friendly staff is the best feature of the center.
Clean changing rooms were praised by more members than the low monthly fee was.
Six new running machines will be enough to solve the evening crowding.
Members would prefer warmer water to a lower fee.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Clean changing rooms were praised by more members than the low monthly fee was.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 事実 (fact) は**数値で検証できるもの**。best / enough / would prefer は評価・予測 = 意見。
- `A received the highest praise (62%), followed by B (58%) and C (51%)` は
  **順位と%を同時に示す**定型。%の大小関係そのものが事実になる。
- 「A の方が B より多く支持された」型の選択肢は、**本文の2つの数値を引き算**して検証する。
  58% > 51% なので成立する。

## 🔬 文構造分析
調査結果の中心文:
`[the friendly staff] received [the highest praise (62%)], followed by [the clean changing
 rooms (58%)] and [the low monthly fee (51%)].`
  S=the friendly staff / V=received / O=the highest praise
  followed by ~ は分詞構文。順位の続きを2つ並べる
選択肢側:
`[Clean changing rooms] were praised [by more members] [than the low monthly fee was].`
  S=Clean changing rooms / V=were praised (受動) / M=by more members
  比較の than 節: S=the low monthly fee / V=was (praised が省略)
→ 58% と 51% の比較。数の大小だけで判定でき、誰の判断も入らない。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段。「When we asked members what they liked most, the friendly staff received the highest praise (62%), followed by the clean changing rooms (58%) and the low monthly fee (51%).」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The friendly staff is the best feature of the center.」… 「the best feature」は価値の判断。62% が最多という事実は本文にあるが、「最良の特徴」と評価するのは意見。
- 「Six new running machines will be enough to solve the evening crowding.」… 「will be enough to solve」は**これから起きること**の予測。Mr. Tanaka 自身が「I hope the center will count how many people actually wait」と疑っており、事実として確定していない。
- 「Members would prefer warmer water to a lower fee.」… 水温と料金を天秤にかける設問は調査に無い。Ms. Lopez 個人が「I would gladly pay a little more」と述べただけで、会員全体の選好ではない。

questions.stem: Which concern does Mr. Tanaka raise about the center's plan?
choices: The monthly fee should be lowered for evening members.
The pool water will still be too cold after the change.
The new running machines may not solve the problem the evening crowd actually has.
The changing rooms are not cleaned often enough.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The new running machines may not solve the problem the evening crowd actually has.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 懸念を問う型は `but honestly` / `I worry` / `I hope ~ before deciding` といった
  **留保の合図**を探す。
- `A is not what B fights over` は関係代名詞 what を使った否定。
  「B が奪い合っているのは A ではない」= **対策と原因のずれ**を指摘する形。
- ダッシュ (—) の後は**言い換え・補足**。`— we all want the weight machines` が
  「本当に足りないもの」を名指ししている。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Mr. Tanaka の懸念:
`[running machines] are not [what the evening crowd fights over] — [we] all want
 [the weight machines].`
  S=running machines / V=are not / C=what 節 (関係代名詞 what = the thing which)
  ダッシュ以下: S=we / V=want / O=the weight machines / M=all
続けて `[I] hope [the center will count [how many people actually wait each evening]
 [before deciding [(that) six running machines are enough]]].`
  S=I / V=hope / O=that 節 (that 省略)
→ 「増設するのはランニング機、混むのはウェイト機」というずれが懸念の中身。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Mr. Tanaka のコメント。「I think buying new running machines is a smart first step, but honestly, running machines are not what the evening crowd fights over — we all want the weight machines. I hope the center will count how many people actually wait each evening before deciding that six running machines are enough.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The monthly fee should be lowered for evening members.」… 月謝についての言及は Mr. Tanaka のコメントに無い。料金を語るのは Ms. Lopez。
- 「The pool water will still be too cold after the change.」… プールの水温を語るのは Ms. Lopez (「I am very happy that the water will finally be warmer in winter」)。Mr. Tanaka は夜のウェイトルームの話をしている。
- 「The changing rooms are not cleaned often enough.」… 更衣室は調査で「the clean changing rooms (58%)」と**好評**の項目。清掃不足という記述は無い。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the two members' attitudes toward the monthly fee?
choices: Both members want the fee to be reduced immediately.
Mr. Tanaka thinks the fee is too high, while Ms. Lopez thinks it is too low.
Neither member mentions the fee in their comments.
Ms. Lopez values the unchanged fee, and she would even accept a higher fee for longer weekend pool hours.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Ms. Lopez values the unchanged fee, and she would even accept a higher fee for longer weekend pool hours.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「二人の態度を推論する」型は、**片方しか述べていない話題**を選ぶと誤る。
  料金に触れているのは Ms. Lopez だけなので、両者に共通する主張は作れない。
- `I would gladly pay a little more if it meant ~` は仮定法。
  「〜を意味するなら喜んで少し多く払う」= **条件付きの値上げ容認**。
- `keeping the fee the same is the best news` の動名詞句主語は
  「据え置きであること」を名詞化したもの。**現状評価**を示す。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Ms. Lopez の評価:
`[keeping the fee the same] is [the best news [in this notice]].`
  S=keeping the fee the same (動名詞句) / V=is / C=the best news
条件付き容認:
`[I] would gladly pay [a little more] [if [it] meant [longer pool hours on weekends]],
 but [I] understand [(that) many members are on a tight budget].`
  S=I / V=would pay / O=a little more / M=gladly, if 節
  if 節: S=it / V=meant / O=longer pool hours on weekends (仮定法過去)
→ 「据え置きは最良の知らせ」+「条件次第では値上げも可」。両方を含む選択肢が正解。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Ms. Lopez のコメント。「What I value most about this gym, however, is the price. My old gym charged almost double, so keeping the fee the same is the best news in this notice. I would gladly pay a little more if it meant longer pool hours on weekends, but I understand that many members are on a tight budget.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Both members want the fee to be reduced immediately.」… 値下げを求める発言は両者ともしていない。Ms. Lopez はむしろ据え置きを歓迎し、条件次第では値上げも受け入れると述べている。
- 「Mr. Tanaka thinks the fee is too high, while Ms. Lopez thinks it is too low.」… Mr. Tanaka は料金に一切触れていない。Ms. Lopez も「too low」とは述べておらず、双方向に誤り。
- 「Neither member mentions the fee in their comments.」… Ms. Lopez は「What I value most about this gym, however, is the price」と明確に料金に言及している。「どちらも触れていない」は事実に反する。

question_data.passage:
Last spring, I had an experience that changed the way I think about kindness.

It was a rainy Saturday morning, and I was on my way to the city library to return some books. Because the train was crowded, I had to stand near the door, holding my heavy bag with both hands. When the train reached my station, I rushed out so quickly that I did not notice something fall from my pocket. I only realized it after I had walked up the stairs and reached the ticket gate. When I checked my pocket, my train pass was gone. My face turned pale. The pass was not only expensive but also held a small photo of my grandmother inside the case, and that photo meant a lot to me.

I ran back down to the platform, but of course the train had already left. I felt like crying. A station worker told me kindly that lost items are sometimes brought to the office, but he could not promise anything. I left my name and phone number and went home, feeling heavy and sad all day.

Three days later, on Tuesday afternoon, my phone rang. It was the station office. A high school girl had found my pass on the train floor and handed it to a worker at the next station. When I went to pick it up, the worker gave me a short note. The girl had written, "I saw the photo inside and thought someone must be missing this. I hope it finds its way home." She had not left her name, only those words. Holding the note, I felt warm tears in my eyes.

That evening, I decided I wanted to do something similar for someone else. The very next morning, while waiting for the bus, I saw a wallet lying on the bench beside me. Remembering the girl's kindness, I picked it up at once and took it to the nearest police box. The officer thanked me and said the owner would be very relieved. As I walked away, I felt lighter than I had in days.

Looking back now, I understand that the girl gave me more than my pass. She showed me that a small act of care can travel from one stranger to another, like a gift passed quietly from hand to hand. I never learned her name, but I think of her often, especially on rainy mornings. Now, whenever I find something that someone has lost, I do not hesitate. I simply pass the kindness along, hoping it will keep moving forward.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: Why did the writer fail to notice that the train pass had fallen?
choices: Because the writer was busy reading the returned library books on the train.
Because the writer had placed the pass inside the heavy bag, not a pocket.
Because a station worker had already taken the pass at the ticket gate.
Because the writer hurried off the crowded train without paying attention.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Because the writer hurried off the crowded train without paying attention.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `so ~ that S V` は「あまりに〜なので…」。**程度が結果を生む**構文。
  ここでは「急ぎすぎた → 気づかなかった」。
- `notice something fall` は知覚動詞 + O + 原形不定詞。
  「何かが落ちるのを (一部始終) 目にする」。**原形は動作の完結**を表す。
- 理由を問う型では、that 節の中の**否定 (did not notice)** が答えの核になる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
筆者の回想:
`[I] rushed out [so quickly] [that [I] did not notice [something] [fall from my pocket]].`
  S=I / V=rushed out / M=so quickly
  that 節 (結果): S=I / V=did not notice / O=something / C=fall from my pocket (原形不定詞)
先行文: `Because [the train] was [crowded], [I] had to stand [near the door], holding
 [my heavy bag] [with both hands].`
  M=Because 節 / S=I / V=had to stand / M=near the door
  holding ~ は分詞構文 (付帯状況)
→ 「混雑」→「両手がふさがる」→「急いで降りる」→「落下に気づかない」の連鎖。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段。「Because the train was crowded, I had to stand near the door, holding my heavy bag with both hands. When the train reached my station, I rushed out so quickly that I did not notice something fall from my pocket.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Because the writer was busy reading the returned library books on the train.」… 本は「on my way to the city library to return some books」= 返却しに行く途中で持っていただけ。車内で読んでいたという記述は無い。
- 「Because the writer had placed the pass inside the heavy bag, not a pocket.」… 定期券はポケットにあった (「fall from my pocket」「When I checked my pocket, my train pass was gone」)。鞄の中ではない。
- 「Because a station worker had already taken the pass at the ticket gate.」… 駅員が改札で取ったという記述は無い。駅員は「lost items are sometimes brought to the office」と説明した側。

questions.stem: Put the following events in the order in which they actually happened: ① The writer took a stranger's wallet to a police box. ② The writer noticed the train pass was missing at the ticket gate. ③ The station office called to say the pass had been found. ④ A high school girl handed the pass to a worker. ⑤ The writer left a name and phone number with a station worker. Which is the correct order?
choices: ② → ⑤ → ④ → ③ → ①
② → ④ → ⑤ → ③ → ①
⑤ → ② → ④ → ① → ③
② → ⑤ → ③ → ④ → ①
questions.explanation:
正解は「② → ⑤ → ④ → ③ → ①」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 時系列問題は**段落の順 = 出来事の順**とは限らない。過去完了 (had + 過去分詞) や
  日付表現が「実際の前後」を示す合図になる。
- `Three days later, on Tuesday afternoon, my phone rang.` は日付を明示した転換点。
  電話 (③) より前に、拾得と引き渡し (④) が起きていなければならない。
- `The very next morning` は「そのすぐ翌朝」。**最後の出来事**を確定させる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
発見の報告文:
`[A high school girl] had found [my pass] [on the train floor] and handed [it] [to a worker]
 [at the next station].`
  S=A high school girl / V=had found と handed の2つが等位 (過去完了)
  O=my pass / it / M=on the train floor, to a worker, at the next station
→ **過去完了**なので、電話 (過去形 my phone rang) より前に起きている。
届け出の文: `[I] left [my name and phone number] and went [home]`
  S=I / V=left と went が等位 / O=my name and phone number
→ 紛失に気づいた当日 (雨の土曜) の行動。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段。「I only realized it after I had walked up the stairs and reached the ticket gate. When I checked my pocket, my train pass was gone.」
第3段。「I left my name and phone number and went home, feeling heavy and sad all day.」
第4段。「Three days later, on Tuesday afternoon, my phone rang. It was the station office. A high school girl had found my pass on the train floor and handed it to a worker at the next station.」
第5段。「The very next morning, while waiting for the bus, I saw a wallet lying on the bench beside me.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「② → ④ → ⑤ → ③ → ①」… ④ (高校生が渡す) を⑤ (名前と電話番号を残す) より前に置いている。⑤は紛失当日の土曜、④は電話 (火曜) 以前の出来事だが、本文は⑤を先に語り、④は過去完了で後から明かされる。土曜の届け出が先。
- 「⑤ → ② → ④ → ① → ③」… ⑤を②より前に置いているが、名前を残したのは紛失に気づいた**後**。また①(財布を届ける)を③(電話)より前に置いている点も、本文の「The very next morning」= 受け取った翌朝と合わない。
- 「② → ⑤ → ③ → ④ → ①」… ③ (電話) を④ (高校生が渡す) より前に置いている。渡されていない物を「見つかった」と連絡できないので、因果が逆転している。

questions.stem: What does the writer most clearly learn from this experience?
choices: That lost items are almost always returned if you wait long enough.
That a small act of kindness can be passed on from one person to another.
That it is safer to keep important photos at home rather than carry them.
That station workers are the people most responsible for helping others.
questions.explanation:
正解は「That a small act of kindness can be passed on from one person to another.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 主旨を問う型は**最終段落の一般化された文**を根拠にする。
  体験談は「出来事 → そこから得た教訓」の順で書かれる。
- `travel from one stranger to another` は「見知らぬ人から別の人へと渡っていく」。
  **親切の連鎖**の比喩。直後の `like a gift passed quietly from hand to hand` が言い換え。
- `pass ~ along` は「(次へ) 回す」。句動詞の along が**継承**の含みを担う。

## 🔬 文構造分析
最終段の中心文:
`[She] showed [me] [that [a small act of care] can travel [from one stranger to another],
 [like a gift [passed quietly from hand to hand]]].`
  S=She / V=showed / O1=me / O2=that 節
  節内: S=a small act of care / V=can travel / M=from one stranger to another
  like ~ は直喩。passed ~ は gift を後置修飾する過去分詞
締め: `[I] simply pass [the kindness] [along], hoping [(that) [it] will keep moving forward].`
  S=I / V=pass / O=the kindness / M=along
  hoping ~ は分詞構文

## 📍 本文の根拠
最終段。「Looking back now, I understand that the girl gave me more than my pass. She showed me that a small act of care can travel from one stranger to another, like a gift passed quietly from hand to hand.」
「Now, whenever I find something that someone has lost, I do not hesitate. I simply pass the kindness along, hoping it will keep moving forward.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「That lost items are almost always returned if you wait long enough.」… 落とし物が必ず戻るという主張は無い。むしろ駅員は「he could not promise anything」と述べており、戻ったのは偶然の親切による。
- 「That it is safer to keep important photos at home rather than carry them.」… 写真を家に置くべきという教訓は本文に無い。写真は「that photo meant a lot to me」と、失った痛みの説明として出てくるだけ。
- 「That station workers are the people most responsible for helping others.」… 駅員の責任という主張は無い。筆者が心を動かされたのは名前も残さなかった高校生の行為。

question_data.passage:
When I was eleven, I could not swim at all. Every summer my friends went to the city pool, but I always stayed home because I was afraid of deep water. One afternoon in June, my older cousin Mika visited us. She had been a member of her school swimming team, and when she heard about my fear, she smiled and said, "By the end of August, you will swim across the pool. I promise."

The next morning, she took me to the pool early, before it became crowded. At first, I would not even put my face in the water. Mika did not laugh at me. Instead, she sat on the edge with me and showed me how to blow bubbles. We practiced only that for the whole first day. It felt silly, but slowly I stopped feeling so nervous.

After about a week, I could put my whole head under the water and open my eyes. Then Mika taught me how to float on my back. This was the hardest part for me. Whenever I tried, I was sure I would sink, so my body became stiff and I went straight down. Mika kept one hand under my back and told me to relax and breathe slowly. "The water wants to hold you," she said. "You just have to trust it." One quiet morning, she quietly took her hand away, and I floated alone for almost ten seconds. I was so surprised that I stood up and shouted with joy.

Once I could float, learning to move was easier than I had expected. Mika showed me how to kick my legs and pull the water with my arms. We practiced near the wall so I could grab it if I felt tired. Day by day, I swam a little farther. Some days I swallowed water and wanted to quit, but Mika always reminded me how far I had already come.

Finally, on the last Saturday of August, Mika stood at the far end of the pool and called my name. I pushed off from the wall and swam toward her without stopping. When my hand touched the wall on the other side, I could not believe it. I had crossed the whole pool by myself. Mika hugged me and said she had never doubted me for a moment.

That summer taught me something I will never forget. The thing I feared most became the thing I loved most. Now, whenever a new challenge looks too big, I remember the feeling of floating alone on the water, and I tell myself to trust, relax, and keep going.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: According to the story, in what order did these events happen? (1) The writer floated alone for about ten seconds. (2) Mika showed the writer how to blow bubbles. (3) The writer swam across the whole pool by herself. (4) The writer learned to kick and pull the water to move forward.
questions.explanation:
正解は「(2) → (1) → (4) → (3)」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 時系列問題は**段落の切れ目**が最大の手がかり。この文章は
  「初日 → 約1週間後 → 浮けた後 → 8月最終土曜」と時の副詞句で刻まれている。
- `Once I could float, learning to move was easier` の Once は「いったん〜すると」。
  **浮けること が 進めること の前提**であることを明示する接続詞。
- `Finally, on the last Saturday of August` の Finally が**最後の出来事**を確定させる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
順序を決める2文:
`[Once [I] could float], [learning to move] was [easier [than I had expected]].`
  M=Once 節 (時・条件): S=I / V=could float
  主節: S=learning to move (動名詞句) / V=was / C=easier
`Finally, [on the last Saturday of August], [Mika] stood [at the far end of the pool]
 and called [my name].`
  M=Finally, on the last Saturday of August / S=Mika / V=stood と called が等位
→ Once 節が「浮く (1)」→「進み方 (4)」の順を固定する。
  初日の bubbles (2) が最初、8月最終土曜の完泳 (3) が最後。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段。「Instead, she sat on the edge with me and showed me how to blow bubbles. We practiced only that for the whole first day.」
第3段。「One quiet morning, she quietly took her hand away, and I floated alone for almost ten seconds.」
第4段。「Once I could float, learning to move was easier than I had expected. Mika showed me how to kick my legs and pull the water with my arms.」
第5段。「Finally, on the last Saturday of August, Mika stood at the far end of the pool and called my name.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「(2) → (4) → (1) → (3)」… (4) 進み方を (1) 浮くより前に置いている。本文は「Once I could float, learning to move was easier」と、浮けたことが前提だと明示している。
- 「(1) → (2) → (4) → (3)」… (1) 浮くを (2) バブルより前に置いている。バブルは「the whole first day」= 初日の練習で、最初の段階。
- 「(2) → (1) → (3) → (4)」… (3) 完泳を (4) 進み方の練習より前に置いている。完泳は「Finally, on the last Saturday of August」で締めくくられる最後の出来事。

questions.stem: What does the writer most want to express in the last paragraph?
choices: Swimming is a skill that everyone should learn while still young
A cousin is always the best person to teach a difficult sport
Facing something frightening can change it into something we love and give us courage for new challenges
The city pool is the safest place to practice swimming in summer
questions.explanation:
正解は「Facing something frightening can change it into something we love and give us courage for new challenges」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 最終段落の主旨は `That summer taught me something I will never forget.` のような
  **総括文**の直後に置かれる。
- `The thing I feared most became the thing I loved most.` は
  同じ形 (the thing I ~ most) を2度使った**対句**。恐怖 → 愛への転換が要点。
- `whenever a new challenge looks too big` は「〜のときはいつでも」。
  **その後も続く行動指針**であることを示す。過去の一回の成功談で終わっていない。

## 🔬 文構造分析
最終段の総括:
`[The thing [I feared most]] became [the thing [I loved most]].`
  S=The thing I feared most (関係節が後置修飾) / V=became / C=the thing I loved most
続く指針:
`Now, [whenever [a new challenge] looks [too big]], [I] remember [the feeling of floating
 alone on the water], and [I] tell [myself] [to trust, relax, and keep going].`
  M=whenever 節 (時): S=a new challenge / V=looks / C=too big
  主節1: S=I / V=remember / O=the feeling of ~
  主節2: S=I / V=tell / O1=myself / O2=to trust, relax, and keep going (不定詞3つが等位)
→ 「恐れたものが好きになった」+「新しい挑戦にも同じ姿勢で臨む」。

## 📍 本文の根拠
最終段。「That summer taught me something I will never forget. The thing I feared most became the thing I loved most. Now, whenever a new challenge looks too big, I remember the feeling of floating alone on the water, and I tell myself to trust, relax, and keep going.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Swimming is a skill that everyone should learn while still young」… 年齢や「若いうちに習うべき」という主張は本文に無い。11歳という記述は状況説明にすぎない。
- 「A cousin is always the best person to teach a difficult sport」… いとこが最良の教師という一般論は述べていない。Mika は具体的な恩人として描かれるが、最終段の主旨は自分の変化。
- 「The city pool is the safest place to practice swimming in summer」… プールの安全性についての記述は無い。最終段の主題は場所ではなく心の持ち方。

question_data.passage:
Last summer, I played in the regional badminton tournament for my high school. I had practiced for months, but on the morning of the match, my hands felt cold and my heart would not stop racing. I am usually a calm person, yet that day I could not even tie my shoes properly. My doubles partner, Kenta, noticed and gave me a small smile, but I was too nervous to smile back.

When we arrived at the gym, the noise of the crowd hit me like a wave. There were hundreds of people in the seats, and the bright lights made the court look enormous. I remember thinking, "Everyone is watching. What if I make a mistake?" My legs felt heavy, and I wanted to sit down in a corner and hide. Kenta must have seen my pale face, because he walked over and said quietly, "Just breathe. We've done this a thousand times in practice. Today is no different." His calm words did not magically fix my fear, but they reminded me that I was not alone.

Our first match began at ten o'clock. In the opening minutes, I missed three easy shots in a row. My hands were shaking, and I could feel my face turning red. The other team scored point after point, and soon we were losing badly. During a short break, our coach, Ms. Mori, knelt beside me. Instead of scolding me, she said, "Stop thinking about the score. Watch the shuttlecock, and trust your body." I closed my eyes, took a long breath, and tried to forget the crowd completely.

Something changed after that. When the match restarted, I stopped worrying about the audience and focused only on each shot, one at a time. Slowly, my movements became smoother, and my old confidence returned. Kenta and I began to work together as we always had in practice, calling out to each other and covering the court. We did not win that first match, but we lost by only two points, and I no longer felt afraid.

By the afternoon, I was a different player. In our second match, my hands were steady and my mind was clear. We won easily, and as I shook hands with our opponents, I realized something important. The crowd had not disappeared, and my fear had not vanished forever. What had changed was me: I had learned to act despite my nervousness instead of waiting for it to go away. That lesson, I think, was worth far more than any trophy.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: Why did the writer feel encouraged when Kenta spoke to him before the matches began?
choices: Because Kenta promised that they would surely win the tournament that day
Because Kenta offered to play the difficult shots so the writer would not have to
Because Kenta told him that the crowd in the gym was actually very small
Because Kenta reminded him that they had prepared together and that he was not facing the pressure alone
questions.explanation:
正解は「Because Kenta reminded him that they had prepared together and that he was not facing the pressure alone」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 励まされた理由は、**相手の発言 + それを受けた自分の記述**の2つを合わせて読む。
  発言だけでは「なぜ効いたか」が確定しない。
- `We've done this a thousand times in practice.` の現在完了は経験の蓄積。
  誇張の a thousand times が「十分やってきた」という安心の根拠になる。
- `did not magically fix ~, but they reminded me ~` は譲歩 + 主張。
  **but の後ろが効いた中身**。「不安は消えないが、独りではないと思い出させた」。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Kenta の言葉と筆者の受け止め:
`"Just breathe. [We]'ve done [this] [a thousand times] [in practice]. [Today] is [no different]."`
  V=breathe (命令文) ｜ S=We / V=have done / O=this / M=a thousand times, in practice
  ｜ S=Today / V=is / C=no different
`[His calm words] did not magically fix [my fear], but [they] reminded [me] [that [I] was
 not [alone]].`
  S=His calm words / V=did not fix / O=my fear / M=magically
  逆接: S=they / V=reminded / O1=me / O2=that 節 → 節内 S=I / V=was / C=not alone
→ 効いたのは「一緒に積み上げてきた」+「独りではない」の2点。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段。「Kenta must have seen my pale face, because he walked over and said quietly, "Just breathe. We've done this a thousand times in practice. Today is no different." His calm words did not magically fix my fear, but they reminded me that I was not alone.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Because Kenta promised that they would surely win the tournament that day」… 勝利の約束はしていない。Kenta が述べたのは「Today is no different」= 練習と変わらないという確認。実際に第1試合は敗れている。
- 「Because Kenta offered to play the difficult shots so the writer would not have to」… 難しい球を代わりに打つという申し出は本文に無い。試合では「Kenta and I began to work together as we always had in practice」と協働している。
- 「Because Kenta told him that the crowd in the gym was actually very small」… 観客が少ないという発言は無い。本文はむしろ「There were hundreds of people in the seats」と多さを描いている。

questions.stem: Put the following events in the order in which they actually happened in the story, and choose the correct sequence. ① The writer won a match easily in the afternoon.  ② The writer struggled to tie his shoes in the morning.  ③ The writer missed three easy shots at the start of the first match.  ④ Ms. Mori told the writer to watch the shuttlecock and trust his body.  ⑤ The writer and Kenta lost the first match by only two points.
choices: ② → ③ → ④ → ⑤ → ①
③ → ② → ④ → ① → ⑤
② → ④ → ③ → ① → ⑤
③ → ② → ⑤ → ④ → ①
questions.explanation:
正解は「② → ③ → ④ → ⑤ → ①」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 時系列は**時刻・時間帯の語**で刻む。この文章は「朝 → 10時の第1試合 → 休憩 →
  再開 → 午後の第2試合」と一直線に進む。
- `Our first match began at ten o'clock.` `By the afternoon` が区切りの目印。
- `In the opening minutes, I missed three easy shots in a row.` の
  `in the opening minutes` は「開始直後」。**休憩中の助言より前**であることが確定する。

## 🔬 文構造分析
時間を刻む文:
`[Our first match] began [at ten o'clock]. In the opening minutes, [I] missed
 [three easy shots] [in a row].`
  S=Our first match / V=began / M=at ten o'clock
  次文: M=In the opening minutes / S=I / V=missed / O=three easy shots / M=in a row
`During a short break, [our coach, Ms. Mori], knelt [beside me].`
  M=During a short break / S=our coach, Ms. Mori (同格) / V=knelt / M=beside me
`[We] did not win [that first match], but [we] lost [by only two points]`
  S=We / V=did not win / O=that first match ｜ 逆接: S=we / V=lost / M=by only two points
→ ③ (打ち損じ) は開始直後、④ (助言) は休憩中、⑤ (2点差負け) は試合終了時。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第1段。「on the morning of the match, my hands felt cold and my heart would not stop racing... that day I could not even tie my shoes properly.」
第3段。「Our first match began at ten o'clock. In the opening minutes, I missed three easy shots in a row.」「During a short break, our coach, Ms. Mori, knelt beside me. Instead of scolding me, she said, "Stop thinking about the score. Watch the shuttlecock, and trust your body."」
第4段。「We did not win that first match, but we lost by only two points」
第5段。「By the afternoon, I was a different player. In our second match, my hands were steady and my mind was clear. We won easily」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「③ → ② → ④ → ① → ⑤」… ③ (打ち損じ) を② (靴紐) より前に置いている。靴紐は「on the morning of the match」= 試合前の朝、打ち損じは10時開始の試合中。順序が逆。
- 「② → ④ → ③ → ① → ⑤」… ④ (Ms. Mori の助言) を③ (打ち損じ) より前に置いている。助言は「During a short break」= 打ち損じて劣勢になった後の休憩中。また①(午後の勝利)を⑤(第1試合の2点差負け)より前に置いている点も誤り。
- 「③ → ② → ⑤ → ④ → ①」… ③ (打ち損じ) を② (靴紐) より前に置き、さらに⑤ (2点差負け) を④ (助言) より前に置いている。助言は試合途中の休憩で、敗戦はその後。

questions.stem: What did the writer finally realize after the second match?
choices: That the real change was within himself, because he had learned to perform even while still feeling nervous
That his nervousness had completely disappeared and would never return
That winning a trophy was the only way to overcome his fear of crowds
That he should not have played in the tournament because the pressure was too great
questions.explanation:
正解は「That the real change was within himself, because he had learned to perform even while still feeling nervous」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 気づきを問う型は `I realized ~` / `What had changed was ~` を探す。
  **強調構文 (What ~ is/was ...)** は「本当に〜だったのは」と焦点を絞る形。
- `The crowd had not disappeared, and my fear had not vanished forever.` の
  過去完了 + 否定が「消えていない」ことを二重に確認している。
- `act despite my nervousness instead of waiting for it to go away` が結論の核。
  **despite (〜にもかかわらず)** が「消すのではなく抱えたまま動く」を表す。

## 🔬 文構造分析
最終段の気づき:
`[The crowd] had not disappeared, and [my fear] had not vanished [forever].`
  S=The crowd / V=had not disappeared ｜ S=my fear / V=had not vanished / M=forever
`[What had changed] was [me]: [I] had learned [to act [despite my nervousness]]
 [instead of waiting [for it to go away]].`
  S=What had changed (関係代名詞 what の名詞節) / V=was / C=me
  コロン以下: S=I / V=had learned / O=to act / M=despite my nervousness, instead of ~
  for it to go away は不定詞の意味上の主語つき (it = my nervousness)
→ 「観客も恐怖も消えていない。変わったのは自分」。この対比が答えの形を決める。

## 📍 本文の根拠
最終段。「The crowd had not disappeared, and my fear had not vanished forever. What had changed was me: I had learned to act despite my nervousness instead of waiting for it to go away. That lesson, I think, was worth far more than any trophy.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「That his nervousness had completely disappeared and would never return」… 「my fear had not vanished forever」= 恐怖は完全には消えていないと明言している。正反対。
- 「That winning a trophy was the only way to overcome his fear of crowds」… 「That lesson, I think, was worth far more than any trophy」= 教訓の方がトロフィーより価値があると述べている。トロフィーが唯一の道というのは逆。
- 「That he should not have played in the tournament because the pressure was too great」… 出場を後悔する記述は無い。むしろその経験から得た教訓を高く評価している。

question_data.passage:
Eco Week at Sakura High: A Report from the Environment Club

Last month, our Environment Club held its first-ever Eco Week, and I would like to share what we did and what we learned. When we first proposed the idea to our teachers, some of them were not sure that students would really (1) participate, because earlier club events had drawn small crowds. <A> However, the response surprised everyone. By Friday, more than three hundred students had joined at least one of our activities, which was far more than we had hoped for.

We planned a different theme for each day. On Monday, we set up a "second-hand book corner" in the library, where students could leave books they no longer needed and take ones they wanted to read. <B> On Tuesday, we ran a workshop on making small bags from old T-shirts, and the sewing room was full all afternoon. On Wednesday, members of the science club measured how much electricity the school uses each day and explained simple ways to reduce it, such as turning off classroom lights during lunch. <C>

Thursday was the busiest day. We asked the cafeteria to weigh the food that students threw away, and the result shocked us. In a single lunch, our school produced almost forty kilograms of food waste. When we showed this number on a large poster, many students said they had never imagined the total could be so high. <D> On Friday, we asked everyone to bring a reusable bottle instead of buying drinks in plastic ones, and the number of plastic bottles in the recycling bins dropped sharply compared with a normal day.

Of course, (2) not everything went smoothly. The weather on Wednesday was rainy, so the outdoor garden activity had to move indoors at the last minute, and some students went home before they found the new room. We also realized that one week is too short to change daily habits. Still, the feedback we collected was encouraging. Several students wrote that they had started carrying their own bottles even after Eco Week ended, and two teachers asked us to repeat the food-waste survey next term.

Looking back, I think the most valuable lesson was not about the environment itself but about people. We learned that (3) students will take action when they can see a clear reason to do so. A poster with a shocking number changed more behavior than any long speech could have. For our club, Eco Week was therefore not only an event but also (4) a turning point. We now have many new members and a clear plan for the future.

Comments:
(1) Add words after the underline that explain why the teachers doubted students.
(2) This phrase introduces the problems the club faced. Make sure the example that follows matches it.
(3) The underlined sentence is a bit weak. Replace it with a clearer statement of your main finding.
(4) Choose words that summarize the overall meaning of Eco Week for the club.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: You want to add the sentence "This idea was so popular that the shelf was almost empty by the end of the day." Where is the best position, <A>, <B>, <C>, or <D>?
questions.explanation:
正解は「<B>」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 文挿入問題は**指示語が指す先**で位置が決まる。`This idea` / `the shelf` の
  **2つの語が同時に成立する場所**は1つしかない。
- `so ~ that S V` は「あまりに〜なので…」。人気の**結果**を述べる文なので、
  企画そのものを紹介した直後にしか置けない。
- 段落ごとの話題 (月曜=古本、水曜=電気、木曜=食品ロス) を先に一覧化してから
  指示語を照合すると、消去が一瞬で終わる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
挿入する文:
`[This idea] was [so popular] [that [the shelf] was [almost empty] [by the end of the day]].`
  S=This idea / V=was / C=so popular
  that 節 (結果): S=the shelf / V=was / C=almost empty / M=by the end of the day
直前の本文 (<B> の前):
`[we] set up [a "second-hand book corner"] [in the library], [where [students] could leave
 [books [they no longer needed]] and take [ones [they wanted to read]]]`
  S=we / V=set up / O=a "second-hand book corner" / M=in the library
  where 節: S=students / V=could leave と take が等位
→ 「本を置いて持ち帰る棚」がここで初めて登場する。This idea も the shelf もここを指す。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段。「On Monday, we set up a "second-hand book corner" in the library, where students could leave books they no longer needed and take ones they wanted to read. <B> On Tuesday, we ran a workshop on making small bags from old T-shirts」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「<A>」… <A> の前後は「some of them were not sure that students would really participate」= 参加者数の見込みの話。棚も企画も出ていない。
- 「<C>」… <C> の直前は「members of the science club measured how much electricity the school uses each day」= 電気使用量の話。shelf が指すものが無い。
- 「<D>」… <D> の直前は「our school produced almost forty kilograms of food waste」= 食品ロスの話。ここも棚とは無関係。

questions.stem: The teacher says underline (3) "students will take action when they can see a clear reason to do so" is a bit weak. Which sentence best replaces it while keeping the writer's main finding?
choices: People remembered the busy Thursday more than any other day of the week.
The Environment Club should hold Eco Week every single month from now on.
Concrete facts, such as the weight of wasted food, moved students to act far more than words alone.
Most students already knew that wasting food and plastic was bad for the planet.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Concrete facts, such as the weight of wasted food, moved students to act far more than words alone.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「弱い文を言い換えよ」型は、**直後の文が根拠**になっていることが多い。
  下線部の次の文がそのまま「なぜそう言えるか」を説明している。
- `A moved B to V` は「A が B を V する気にさせた」。
  **無生物主語 + move O to V** は、原因を主語に置く英語らしい形。
- `far more than words alone` の比較が、下線直後の
  「long speech よりポスターが効いた」を正確に受けている。

## 🔬 文構造分析
下線部 (3) とその直後:
`[students] will take [action] [when [they] can see [a clear reason [to do so]]].`
  S=students / V=will take / O=action / M=when 節
`[A poster [with a shocking number]] changed [more behavior] [than any long speech could have].`
  S=A poster with a shocking number / V=changed / O=more behavior
  比較節: S=any long speech / V=could have (changed が省略)
選択肢側:
`[Concrete facts], [such as the weight of wasted food], moved [students] [to act]
 [far more than words alone].`
  S=Concrete facts / V=moved / O=students / C=to act
→ 「具体的な数字 > 言葉」という同じ骨格。下線部の一般論を具体化した言い換えになる。

## 📍 本文の根拠
最終段。「We learned that」…「students will take action when they can see a clear reason to do so. A poster with a shocking number changed more behavior than any long speech could have.」
根拠となる数字は第3段。「In a single lunch, our school produced almost forty kilograms of food waste.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「People remembered the busy Thursday more than any other day of the week.」… 曜日の印象は主旨ではない。木曜が忙しかったのは事実だが、下線部が述べているのは「行動を起こす条件」。
- 「The Environment Club should hold Eco Week every single month from now on.」… 開催頻度の提案は下線部の内容と別物。しかも本文は「one week is too short to change daily habits」と述べており、毎月開催を主張してはいない。
- 「Most students already knew that wasting food and plastic was bad for the planet.」… 「すでに知っていた」は本文と逆。生徒は「they had never imagined the total could be so high」= 総量を想像していなかった。

questions.stem: Which words best replace underline (4) "a turning point" so that they summarize what Eco Week meant for the club as a whole?
choices: a quiet week with few visitors
a single survey about food waste
a difficult event that the members hope to forget
a new beginning that gave the club energy and direction
questions.explanation:
正解は「a new beginning that gave the club energy and direction」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `a turning point` (転機) の言い換えは、**直後の文が示す結果**から決める。
  「新会員が増え、将来の計画ができた」= 前向きな出発点。
- `not only A but also B` の also B が**新しく加わった意味**。
  ここでは「行事であるだけでなく、転機でもあった」。
- 語句置換型は、**本文の結論の温度 (肯定 / 否定)** を必ず合わせる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
下線部 (4) を含む文とその直後:
`For our club, [Eco Week] was therefore not only [an event] but also [a turning point].`
  S=Eco Week / V=was / C=not only an event but also a turning point (相関接続詞)
`[We] now have [many new members] and [a clear plan for the future].`
  S=We / V=have / O=many new members と a clear plan for the future が等位 / M=now
選択肢側:
`[a new beginning [that gave the club energy and direction]]`
  関係節: S=that (=beginning) / V=gave / O1=the club / O2=energy and direction
→ 「新会員 = energy」「将来の計画 = direction」と1対1で対応する。

## 📍 本文の根拠
最終段。「For our club, Eco Week was therefore not only an event but also」…「a turning point. We now have many new members and a clear plan for the future.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「a quiet week with few visitors」… 「来場者が少ない静かな週」は事実と逆。「more than three hundred students had joined at least one of our activities, which was far more than we had hoped for」と述べている。
- 「a single survey about food waste」… 食品ロス調査は木曜の1企画にすぎない。エコウィーク全体の要約にはならない。
- 「a difficult event that the members hope to forget」… 「忘れたい困難な行事」は本文の締めくくりと正反対。反省点は挙げつつも「the feedback we collected was encouraging」と肯定的に結んでいる。

question_data.passage:
You are a member of the library committee at your high school. One of your classmates, Mei, has written a draft to introduce the school's upcoming Reading Week. Your teacher, Ms. Carter, has read the draft and left comments. Read the draft and the comments, and help Mei improve her writing.

Mei's draft:

Welcome to Reading Week!

Every November, our school library holds a special event called Reading Week. This year it will run from Monday, November 16, to Friday, November 20. The library committee has been planning it since September, and we are excited to finally share the details with you. <A> Reading Week is not only for students who already love books. (1) It is also for those who have never thought of reading as fun, because we have prepared activities that anyone can enjoy.

The main event is the "Book Exchange Corner." If you bring a book you have already read and no longer need, you can swap it for a book that another student has brought. <B> Last year, more than two hundred books were exchanged in a single week, and many students told us they discovered authors they had never heard of before. (2) We expect this year to be even more successful, since the number of students taking part has grown steadily.

We will also hold daily "Lunchtime Talks." Each day, a different teacher will speak for ten minutes about a book that changed the way they think. <C> The talks are short, so you can drop in during lunch without missing your meal. We hope these talks will show you that reading is not a lonely activity but something we can share and discuss together.

Finally, do not forget the "Reading Passport." Every time you borrow a book during Reading Week, a librarian will stamp your passport. <D> Students who collect five stamps will receive a small bookmark designed by our art club. The point is not the prize itself; rather, the passport is meant to encourage you to keep coming back to the library.

So please join us. Whether you read one page or one hundred, Reading Week is a chance to (3) make reading a habit you carry beyond a single week. We look forward to seeing you in the library!

Comments:

(1) Good start, but the sentence stops too suddenly. Add a phrase that completes your point about who Reading Week is for.

(2) This is a strong claim. Replace this sentence with one that supports your expectation using the evidence you already mentioned, rather than just repeating the claim.

(3) You want to leave readers with your main message. Choose the phrase that best captures the overall purpose of Reading Week as described in your draft.

Insertion: You also have one extra sentence that you cut earlier. Decide where it fits best: "No special skill is needed; you only have to be willing to try."
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: 下線部 (1) の文「It is also for those who have never thought of reading as fun, ...」の後に続けるのに最も適切な語句を選びなさい。
choices: so we have decided to cancel some of the events
because we have prepared activities that anyone can enjoy
because the library will be closed during the event
although we only welcome experienced readers
questions.explanation:
正解は「because we have prepared activities that anyone can enjoy」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 文を完成させる型は、**直前の文との論理関係**を先に決める。
  ここは `not only A` → `also B` の流れなので、B を支える理由が要る。
- `those who have never thought of reading as fun` の
  `think of A as B` は「A を B とみなす」。**never が経験の否定**。
- 続く語句は because (理由) が最も自然。**「本好きでない人にも向く」根拠**を述べる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
下線部 (1) を含む2文:
`[Reading Week] is not only [for students [who already love books]].`
  S=Reading Week / V=is / C=for students who already love books / M=not only
`[It] is also [for those [who have never thought of reading as fun]], because
 [we] have prepared [activities [that anyone can enjoy]].`
  S=It / V=is / C=for those ~ / M=also
  because 節: S=we / V=have prepared / O=activities that anyone can enjoy
→ 「本好き以外にも向く」の理由が「誰でも楽しめる活動を用意した」。
  この後に Book Exchange・Lunchtime Talks・Reading Passport が並ぶ構成とも一致する。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第1段。「Reading Week is not only for students who already love books.」…「It is also for those who have never thought of reading as fun, because we have prepared activities that anyone can enjoy.」
実際に「The main event is the "Book Exchange Corner."」「We will also hold daily "Lunchtime Talks."」「Finally, do not forget the "Reading Passport."」と3種の企画が続く。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「so we have decided to cancel some of the events」… 行事の中止は本文と正反対。この後に3つの企画が具体的に紹介される。
- 「because the library will be closed during the event」… 図書館が閉まるという記述は無い。むしろ「keep coming back to the library」と来館を促している。
- 「although we only welcome experienced readers」… 「経験者しか歓迎しない」は「not only for students who already love books」と真っ向から矛盾する。

questions.stem:
次の1文を入れるのに最も適切な位置を <A>〜<D> から選びなさい。
挿入文: "No special skill is needed; you only have to be willing to try."
questions.explanation:
正解は「<A>」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 挿入位置は**一般論か具体論か**で決まる。「特別な技能は要らない」は
  参加の敷居を語る**一般論**なので、具体的な企画説明の途中には入らない。
- `No special skill is needed; you only have to be willing to try.`
  のセミコロンは前後を対等に結ぶ。**言い換え・補足**の関係。
- 直後の文が「本好きでない生徒にも向く」と続くので、その**導入**として噛み合う。

## 🔬 文構造分析
挿入する文:
`[No special skill] is needed; [you] only have [to be willing [to try]].`
  前半: S=No special skill / V=is needed (受動)
  後半: S=you / V=have / O=to be willing to try / M=only
<A> の直後の文:
`[Reading Week] is not only [for students [who already love books]].`
  S=Reading Week / V=is / C=for students who already love books
→ 「技能不要」→「本好き以外も歓迎」と、参加のハードルの低さで話題が続く。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第1段。「The library committee has been planning it since September, and we are excited to finally share the details with you. <A> Reading Week is not only for students who already love books.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「<B>」… <B> は Book Exchange Corner の交換方法を説明した直後。次に来るのは「Last year, more than two hundred books were exchanged」という実績で、一般論を挟むと流れが切れる。
- 「<C>」… <C> は Lunchtime Talks の説明の途中。直後は「The talks are short, so you can drop in during lunch」と、同じ企画の続きを述べている。
- 「<D>」… <D> は Reading Passport のスタンプ説明の直後。直後は「Students who collect five stamps will receive a small bookmark」と具体的な特典の説明が続く。

questions.stem: コメント (2) に従い、下線部 (2) の文「We expect this year to be even more successful, since the number of students taking part has grown steadily.」を置き換えるのに最も適切な文を選びなさい。
choices: We are not sure whether anyone will join the Book Exchange Corner this year.
The Book Exchange Corner will be held only if enough teachers agree to help.
Students who bring books will be asked to pay a small fee at the corner.
Because the number of participants has increased every year, we believe even more books will be exchanged this time.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Because the number of participants has increased every year, we believe even more books will be exchanged this time.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「主張を繰り返すな、根拠で支えよ」という指示への対応は、
  **すでに本文に出た事実を because / since で前に置く**のが定石。
- `Because ~, we believe ~` は「根拠 → 判断」の順。
  元の文は `We expect ~, since ~` で判断が先。**指示は根拠を前に出せ**という意味。
- 置換型では、**本文が述べた事実と矛盾しないか**を必ず確認する。

## 🔬 文構造分析
置き換え後の文:
`Because [the number of participants] has increased [every year], [we] believe
 [(that) [even more books] will be exchanged [this time]].`
  M=Because 節: S=the number of participants / V=has increased / M=every year
  主節: S=we / V=believe / O=that 節 (that 省略)
  節内: S=even more books / V=will be exchanged (受動) / M=this time
根拠となる本文:
`Last year, [more than two hundred books] were exchanged [in a single week]`
  S=more than two hundred books / V=were exchanged / M=in a single week
→ 既出の「200冊超」「参加者が増加」を根拠に、結論を導く形になっている。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段。「Last year, more than two hundred books were exchanged in a single week, and many students told us they discovered authors they had never heard of before.」…「We expect this year to be even more successful, since the number of students taking part has grown steadily.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「We are not sure whether anyone will join the Book Exchange Corner this year.」… 「参加者がいるか分からない」は、すでに述べた「200冊超が交換された」「参加者が着実に増えている」という根拠と矛盾する。
- 「The Book Exchange Corner will be held only if enough teachers agree to help.」… 開催が教員の協力次第という条件は本文に無い。Book Exchange Corner は生徒同士で本を交換する企画。
- 「Students who bring books will be asked to pay a small fee at the corner.」… 有料化は本文と矛盾する。「you can swap it for a book that another student has brought」= 交換であって売買ではない。

questions.stem: コメント (3) に従い、本文の主旨をまとめる下線部 (3)「make reading a habit you carry beyond a single week」を置き換えるのに最も適切な語句を選びなさい。
choices: turn reading into a lasting part of your daily life
finish reading as many books as possible in five days
win the bookmark prize before anyone else does
avoid going to the library after Reading Week ends
questions.explanation:
正解は「turn reading into a lasting part of your daily life」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 主旨の言い換えは、**本文中の別の箇所が同じことを言っている**はず。
  ここでは Reading Passport の説明が「通い続けてもらうため」と述べている。
- `a habit you carry beyond a single week` の carry は「持ち運ぶ」から
  「(習慣を) 保ち続ける」。beyond ~ が**期間を超える**ことを示す。
- `turn A into B` は「A を B に変える」。**lasting (持続する)** が
  「beyond a single week」の言い換えになっている。

## 🔬 文構造分析
下線部 (3) を含む文:
`Whether [you] read [one page] or [one hundred], [Reading Week] is [a chance
 [to make [reading] [a habit [you carry beyond a single week]]]].`
  M=Whether 節 (譲歩) / S=Reading Week / V=is / C=a chance
  不定詞句: to make / O=reading / C=a habit ~ (make O C = O を C にする)
本文の別の根拠:
`[the passport] is meant [to encourage [you] [to keep coming back to the library]]`
  S=the passport / V=is meant / C=to encourage you to keep coming back
→ 「1週間を超えて続く習慣」=「通い続ける」。この2つが主旨として重なる。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第4段。「The point is not the prize itself; rather, the passport is meant to encourage you to keep coming back to the library.」
最終段。「Whether you read one page or one hundred, Reading Week is a chance to」…「make reading a habit you carry beyond a single week.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「finish reading as many books as possible in five days」… 「5日間でできるだけ多く読む」は短期の量を目的化しており、「beyond a single week」= 期間を超えるという主旨と正反対。
- 「win the bookmark prize before anyone else does」… 本文は「The point is not the prize itself」と、賞品が目的でないことを明言している。
- 「avoid going to the library after Reading Week ends」… 終了後に図書館へ行かないというのは、「keep coming back to the library」と真逆。

question_data.passage: Why Our River Park Needs Your Help (Riku's draft; positions [A] [B] [C] [D]) Last spring my sister cut her hand on broken glass left in River Park. (1) The cut was not deep, but it made me realize something important. The park used to be our town's pride, yet today it is full of litter and the benches are breaking apart. [A] Many families no longer bring their children because they worry about safety. [B] I asked a city worker about repair costs. (2) Replacing the ten benches would cost about 200,000 yen, and three trash bins another 60,000 yen. [C] Cleaning the river itself is far more expensive, since equipment must be rented and trained workers hired. The total comes to nearly 800,000 yen. [D] Our student council has started a collection box. (3) Some students have said that one school cannot change anything, but I do not agree. So I ask each of you to do one small thing. (4) No single person can finish this job, but together we can bring our park back to life.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: Look at the underlined part (1). Which phrase best continues the sentence so that it connects naturally to the idea that comes right after it?
choices: that the city had wasted a great deal of money on the park
that a small accident can point to a much larger problem
that broken glass is the only danger families need to fear
that my sister should have been more careful while running
questions.explanation:
正解は「that a small accident can point to a much larger problem」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 文を完成させる型は**直後の展開**を先に読む。ここでは個人の怪我 →
  公園全体の荒廃へと話が広がるので、「小 → 大」をつなぐ表現が要る。
- `point to ~` は「〜を指し示す」。**小さな事象が大きな問題の兆候である**ことを表す。
- `it made me realize something important` の something important の中身が
  そのまま下線部。**次段落の内容を予告する役割**を持つ。

## 🔬 文構造分析
下線部 (1) を含む文:
`[The cut] was not [deep], but [it] made [me] realize [something important].`
  前半: S=The cut / V=was / C=deep / M=not
  逆接: S=it / V=made / O=me / C=realize something important (使役の make + 原形)
選択肢側:
`[that [a small accident] can point [to a much larger problem]]`
  節内: S=a small accident / V=can point / M=to a much larger problem
直後の本文:
`[The park] used to be [our town's pride], yet [today] [it] is [full of litter]`
  S=The park / V=used to be / C=our town's pride
  逆接 yet: S=it / V=is / C=full of litter / M=today
→ 「浅い傷」という小さな事実から、公園全体の荒廃という大きな問題へ話が移る。

## 📍 本文の根拠
冒頭。「Last spring my sister cut her hand on broken glass left in River Park.」…「The cut was not deep, but it made me realize something important. The park used to be our town's pride, yet today it is full of litter and the benches are breaking apart.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「that the city had wasted a great deal of money on the park」… 市が金を浪費したという主張は本文に無い。むしろこの後、修理に必要な金額を積み上げて支援を訴えている。
- 「that broken glass is the only danger families need to fear」… 「ガラスだけが唯一の危険」は、直後に「the benches are breaking apart」と別の危険が挙がることと矛盾する。only が言い過ぎ。
- 「that my sister should have been more careful while running」… 妹の不注意を責める内容は本文に無く、「小さな事故 → 大きな問題」という展開ともつながらない。

questions.stem: A sentence has been removed from the second paragraph. The removed sentence is: These two repairs are not very expensive, and I think we could cover them quite soon. Where is the best place to put it back?
questions.explanation:
正解は「[C]」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 文の復元は**指示語と対比**で決まる。`These two repairs` の these two が
  直前に**2つの修理**が並んでいることを要求する。
- 直後は `Cleaning the river itself is far more expensive` と**対比**が続く。
  「安い2件」→「(それに対し) 川は高い」の順にしか置けない。
- 金額の列挙 (200,000 / 60,000 / 800,000) を先に整理すると位置が一意に決まる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
復元する文:
`[These two repairs] are not [very expensive], and [I] think [(that) [we] could cover
 [them] [quite soon]].`
  前半: S=These two repairs / V=are / C=very expensive / M=not
  後半: S=I / V=think / O=that 節 (that 省略) → 節内 S=we / V=could cover / O=them
直前の本文:
`Replacing [the ten benches] would cost [about 200,000 yen], and [three trash bins]
 [another 60,000 yen].`
  S=Replacing the ten benches (動名詞句) / V=would cost / O=about 200,000 yen
  後半は cost が省略された等位節
直後の本文:
`[Cleaning the river itself] is [far more expensive]`
  S=Cleaning the river itself / V=is / C=far more expensive
→ these two = ベンチと ゴミ箱。その直後、川の清掃との対比が始まる [C] が唯一。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段。「I asked a city worker about repair costs.」…「Replacing the ten benches would cost about 200,000 yen, and three trash bins another 60,000 yen. [C] Cleaning the river itself is far more expensive, since equipment must be rented and trained workers hired. The total comes to nearly 800,000 yen.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「[A]」… [A] の直前は公園の荒廃の描写で、まだ修理費の話が出ていない。These two repairs が指すものが無い。
- 「[B]」… [B] の直前は「Many families no longer bring their children because they worry about safety」= 利用者の減少の話。金額はこの後に出てくる。
- 「[D]」… [D] の直前は「The total comes to nearly 800,000 yen」= 総額。ここに「2件は高くない」を置くと、直前の高額な総額と噛み合わず対比が壊れる。

questions.stem: The writer wants to replace the underlined sentence (3) with a stronger version that keeps the same meaning. Which is the best replacement?
choices: Some students believe one school cannot matter, which is why the city should solve this problem alone.
Some students think one school cannot help, and honestly I sometimes share their doubts about it.
Some students say one school cannot change anything, so perhaps we should ask other schools to lead instead.
Some students doubt that one school can have any effect, but I am sure our efforts will prove them wrong.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Some students doubt that one school can have any effect, but I am sure our efforts will prove them wrong.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「同じ意味のまま強くせよ」型は、**元の文の論理構造を保つ**のが条件。
  元は「反対意見の紹介 + 自分は同意しない」。この2要素を両方残す。
- `but I am sure our efforts will prove them wrong` の
  `prove O C` は「O が C だと証明する」。**反論の強さ**を作る形。
- 誤答は「同調してしまう」「他人任せにする」など、**主張の向きが変わる**ものが並ぶ。

## 🔬 文構造分析
元の下線部 (3):
`[Some students] have said [(that) [one school] cannot change [anything]], but
 [I] do not agree.`
  S=Some students / V=have said / O=that 節 (that 省略)
  逆接: S=I / V=do not agree
置き換え後:
`[Some students] doubt [that [one school] can have [any effect]], but [I] am [sure
 [(that) [our efforts] will prove [them] [wrong]]].`
  S=Some students / V=doubt / O=that 節
  逆接: S=I / V=am / C=sure + that 節
  節内: S=our efforts / V=will prove / O=them / C=wrong
→ 「懐疑の紹介 + 強い反論」という骨格が保たれ、反論だけが強化されている。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第3段。「Our student council has started a collection box.」…「Some students have said that one school cannot change anything, but I do not agree. So I ask each of you to do one small thing.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Some students believe one school cannot matter, which is why the city should solve this problem alone.」… 「市が単独で解決すべき」は、直後の「So I ask each of you to do one small thing」= 一人ひとりへの呼びかけと正反対。
- 「Some students think one school cannot help, and honestly I sometimes share their doubts about it.」… 「私も時々同じ疑いを共有する」は反論を弱めている。元の文は「I do not agree」と明確に否定しており、意味が変わる。
- 「Some students say one school cannot change anything, so perhaps we should ask other schools to lead instead.」… 「他校に主導を任せよう」は、自校の生徒会が募金箱を始めたという文脈と噛み合わない。責任の転嫁になっている。

questions.stem: The underlined sentence (4) expresses the main message of the essay. Which phrase best replaces it while summing up the central idea of the whole essay?
choices: change becomes possible when many people each contribute a little
a beautiful park is mainly the responsibility of the city government
the park will recover on its own if we simply wait long enough
keeping the park clean matters less than keeping it safe at night
questions.explanation:
正解は「change becomes possible when many people each contribute a little」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 主旨の言い換えは**最終文の対比構造**をそのまま移す。
  `No single person can ~, but together we can ~` は「個人では無理 / 皆でなら可能」。
- `each contribute a little` の each が「一人ひとりが少しずつ」。
  元の together の言い換えとして正確。
- 誤答は「行政任せ」「放置すれば直る」など、**呼びかけの前提を崩す**ものが並ぶ。

## 🔬 文構造分析
下線部 (4):
`[No single person] can finish [this job], but together [we] can bring [our park]
 [back to life].`
  前半: S=No single person / V=can finish / O=this job
  逆接: S=we / V=can bring / O=our park / M=together, back to life
選択肢側:
`[change] becomes [possible] [when [many people] each contribute [a little]]`
  S=change / V=becomes / C=possible / M=when 節
  when 節: S=many people / V=contribute / O=a little / M=each
→ 「一人では不可 → 皆でなら可能」という骨格が完全に一致する。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第3段。「So I ask each of you to do one small thing.」…「No single person can finish this job, but together we can bring our park back to life.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「a beautiful park is mainly the responsibility of the city government」… 「主に市の責任」は、生徒一人ひとりへの呼びかけという本文の主旨と衝突する。
- 「the park will recover on its own if we simply wait long enough」… 「待てば自然に回復する」は、修理費を積み上げて支援を求める本文と正反対。
- 「keeping the park clean matters less than keeping it safe at night」… 「清潔さより夜の安全」という優先順位づけは本文に無い。安全に触れるのは families worry about safety の1箇所のみ。

question_data.passage:
You are a member of your school's science club. A first-year student, Kenji, wrote the draft below for a guide that will be handed to families visiting the school's Science Fair. Read his draft and the comments from your teacher.

Welcome to the Greenhill High School Science Fair!

Thank you for coming today. Our club has been preparing for this event for almost three months, and we are excited to share what we have learned. This guide will help you (1)make the most of, so please keep it with you as you walk around.

The fair is held in three rooms on the second floor. <A> In the Blue Room, you will find experiments about plants and animals. The Green Room is full of machines and robots that our members built by hand. <B> In the Red Room, you can watch short chemistry shows that start every thirty minutes. <C> Because the rooms can become crowded, we recommend that families with small children visit the Red Room first, while it is still quiet in the morning. <D>

There are a few things we would like you to remember. Please do not touch the displays unless a sign says you may, because (2)some of the experiments are still running and a small change could ruin a whole week of work. If you have a question, look for a student wearing a yellow badge; they are happy to explain anything. (3)We would be glad if you ask us many questions, and we think it is a good thing to do.

At noon, the winners of the poster contest will be announced in the main hall. Voting closes at 11:30, so be sure to choose your favourite poster before then. Each visitor may vote only once.

We hope you enjoy your visit. (4)Science is fun, and we made this fair to share it.

Comments:
(1) You started this sentence but did not finish it. "Make the most of" needs an object. Add words so the sentence is complete and natural.
(2) This underlined part is fine, but please look at the sentence that follows the plant experiments. I want to add the sentence "Some of these were planted by elementary school children who visit us each spring." Where in the second paragraph should it go? Choose the best position from <A>, <B>, <C>, and <D>.
(3) This sentence repeats the same idea twice and sounds wordy. Rewrite it as one clear, polite sentence.
(4) The ending is a little flat. Replace this underlined sentence with one that states our main message more strongly.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: Which is the best phrase to complete underlined part (1) so that the sentence is grammatically complete and natural in context?
choices: make the most of and enjoy it
make the most of your time here
make the most, of course
make the most of it three months
questions.explanation:
正解は「make the most of your time here」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `make the most of ~` は「〜を最大限に活かす」。**of は前置詞なので目的語が要る**。
  目的語を欠いたまま文を終えると非文になる。
- `help O (to) V` は「O が V するのを助ける」。ここでは
  `This guide will help you make the most of ...` の形。
- 案内文なので、目的語は**来場者がこの場で使うもの**= 時間が最も自然。

## 🔬 文構造分析
下線部 (1) を含む文の骨格:
`[This guide] will help [you]` … `so please keep [it] [with you] [as you walk around]`
  S=This guide / V=will help / O=you / C=原形不定詞句 (ここが欠けている)
  後半は命令文: V=keep / O=it / M=with you, as you walk around
補う句:
`make the most of your time here`
  V=make / O=the most / of の目的語=your time here
→ help O + 原形不定詞 の C の位置に入る句なので、of の目的語まで埋めて
  初めて C が完成する。your time here が「来場中の時間」として文脈に合う。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第1段。「Our club has been preparing for this event for almost three months, and we are excited to share what we have learned. This guide will help you」…「make the most of, so please keep it with you as you walk around.」
教師コメント (1)。「"Make the most of" needs an object. Add words so the sentence is complete and natural.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「make the most of and enjoy it」… and enjoy it を足しても of の目的語は空のまま。「make the most of and enjoy it」は文法的に成立しない。
- 「make the most, of course」… of course は独立した副詞句で、熟語 make the most of を分断してしまう。「最大限に活かす」の意味が消える。
- 「make the most of it three months」… three months は準備期間 (「preparing for this event for almost three months」) の数値。来場者が活かす対象ではなく、意味が通らない。

questions.stem: Comment (3) says underlined part (3) is wordy and repeats the same idea. Which is the best single sentence to replace it?
choices: It is good, so please ask us, and we are glad, and ask many.
We ask many questions, and asking is a good thing for us to do.
Please feel free to ask us as many questions as you like.
We would be glad, and we think asking many questions is good.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Please feel free to ask us as many questions as you like.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 冗長の解消は、**同じ内容を2度言っている箇所を1つに畳む**。
  元の文は「嬉しい」と「良いことだと思う」で同じ主旨を反復している。
- `feel free to V` は「遠慮なく〜してください」。**丁寧な勧誘**の定型。
- `as many questions as you like` は同等比較を使った「好きなだけ」。
  **数量の自由**を1語句で表せるので、反復が消える。

## 🔬 文構造分析
元の下線部 (3):
`[We] would be [glad] [if [you] ask [us] [many questions]], and [we] think
 [(that) [it] is [a good thing to do]].`
  節1: S=We / V=would be / C=glad / M=if 節
  節2: S=we / V=think / O=that 節 → 同じ主旨の反復
置き換え後:
`Please feel free [to ask [us] [as many questions as you like]].`
  命令文: V=feel / C=free / 不定詞句: to ask / O1=us / O2=as many questions as you like
→ 依頼の主体が「来場者に問うてほしい側」であることも保たれている。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第3段。「If you have a question, look for a student wearing a yellow badge; they are happy to explain anything.」…「We would be glad if you ask us many questions, and we think it is a good thing to do.」
教師コメント (3)。「This sentence repeats the same idea twice and sounds wordy. Rewrite it as one clear, polite sentence.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「It is good, so please ask us, and we are glad, and ask many.」… and が3つ連なり、元の文より冗長になっている。指摘に応えていない。
- 「We ask many questions, and asking is a good thing for us to do.」… 主語が We になっているため「私たちが多くの質問をする」となり、来場者に質問を促すという元の意図と逆転する。
- 「We would be glad, and we think asking many questions is good.」… 「嬉しい」と「良いことだと思う」という元の二重表現をほぼそのまま残しており、冗長さが解消されていない。

questions.stem: Comment (4) asks for a stronger closing sentence to replace underlined part (4). Which best states the writers' main message?
choices: Thank you again for coming to the Greenhill High School Science Fair today.
Science is sometimes difficult, but you should try your best to understand it.
We made this fair in three months, so please look at every single display.
We hope today sparks your own curiosity and shows you that science belongs to everyone.
questions.explanation:
正解は「We hope today sparks your own curiosity and shows you that science belongs to everyone.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「締めが平板だから強くせよ」型は、**下書き全体の目的**を言い直す。
  ここでは「科学は楽しい・それを分かち合う」を、より力のある形にする。
- `spark` は「火花を散らす」から「(好奇心などを) 呼び起こす」。
  **抽象名詞を目的語に取る比喩**として使われる。
- `science belongs to everyone` は「科学は皆のもの」。
  元の「share it」を、より広い主張に押し上げた言い換え。

## 🔬 文構造分析
元の下線部 (4):
`[Science] is [fun], and [we] made [this fair] [to share it].`
  節1: S=Science / V=is / C=fun
  節2: S=we / V=made / O=this fair / M=to share it (目的の不定詞)
置き換え後:
`[We] hope [(that) [today] sparks [your own curiosity] and shows [you]
 [that [science] belongs [to everyone]]].`
  S=We / V=hope / O=that 節 (that 省略)
  節内: S=today / V=sparks と shows が等位 / O=your own curiosity ／ O1=you, O2=that 節
→ 「楽しい」→「好奇心を呼び起こす」、「分かち合う」→「皆のもの」と、
  元の2要素をそれぞれ強い語に置き換えている。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第1段。「Our club has been preparing for this event for almost three months, and we are excited to share what we have learned.」
最終段。「We hope you enjoy your visit.」…「Science is fun, and we made this fair to share it.」
教師コメント (4)。「The ending is a little flat. Replace this underlined sentence with one that states our main message more strongly.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Thank you again for coming to the Greenhill High School Science Fair today.」… 単なる礼で終わっており、主張が無い。「平板 (flat)」という指摘がそのまま残る。
- 「Science is sometimes difficult, but you should try your best to understand it.」… 「難しいが努力せよ」は別の主旨へのすり替え。下書きは科学の楽しさと共有を語っており、努力を求めてはいない。
- 「We made this fair in three months, so please look at every single display.」… 準備期間という枝葉に焦点が移り、しかも「全部見よ」と来場者に負担を課している。主旨の要約になっていない。

question_data.passage:
You are a member of the book club at Greenfield High School. The club is organizing a charity book fair, and you find the leaflet below on the club's notice board.

--- LEAFLET ---

Greenfield High School Charity Book Fair — "Pass It On"

Saturday, July 18, 10:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m. in the School Gymnasium

This year, students sell used books they love so that others can enjoy them. All money goes to the Greenfield Children's Library, which buys new books for kids in our town.

How to take part as a seller:
- Choose up to FIVE books you have read and want to pass on.
- Fill in one Recommendation Form for EACH book and submit all forms by Friday, July 3.
- Write a short comment so buyers can decide. Forms with no comment will be returned to you.
- Set a price between 100 and 500 yen. Books in the "Classics" group may be priced higher, up to 800 yen.
- We cannot accept textbooks, magazines, or any book published this year.

On the fair day, books will be displayed by GROUP, not by seller. Visitors can read your comment before they buy. Thank you for passing your favorite stories on to a younger reader!

--- RECOMMENDATION FORMS (submitted by club members) ---

Form 1
Seller: Mika
Title: The Silent Forest
Author: Helen Carter
Group: Mystery
Price: 300 yen
Comment: I read this twice. The ending surprised me both times, and I still think about it.

Form 2
Seller: Daniel
Title: Voices of the Sea
Author: Robert Lane
Group: Classics
Price: 700 yen
Comment: My grandfather gave me this old novel. The language is a little difficult, but the story of a fishing village stayed with me.

Form 3
Seller: Mika
Title: Cooking for Beginners
Author: Sophie Bell
Group: Hobby
Price: 250 yen
Comment: (blank)

Form 4
Seller: Aiko
Title: The Long Road Home
Author: James Wood
Group: Adventure
Price: 400 yen
Comment: A boy walks across a country to find his family. I could not stop turning the pages on a rainy weekend.

Form 5
Seller: Daniel
Title: Numbers and You
Author: Greenfield Math Dept.
Group: Hobby
Price: 200 yen
Comment: This is the math textbook our school used last year. It helped me a lot before exams.

--- EMAIL FROM THE ORGANIZER ---

From: Ms. Porter (Book Club Adviser)
To: All sellers
Date: July 6
Subject: Two quick things before the fair

Hello everyone,

Thank you for your forms. The fair is going to be wonderful. Before we print the price labels, I need to fix two problems.

First, one form cannot be accepted in its current state because the rules clearly say what every book needs in order to go on the table. Please send me the missing part by July 8, or that book will not be displayed.

Second, one book has been placed in a group that does not fit what the book actually is, so I will move it to the correct group myself — no action is needed from you for that one.

I also have a request for two of you. Mika and Aiko, could each of you bring one large box on the fair day? We need boxes to carry the unsold books back to the club room, and yours are the books most likely to attract many buyers, so your tables will empty fastest. Daniel, please arrive 30 minutes early to help set up the Classics corner.

See you on July 18!

Ms. Porter
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: Which combination correctly describes two of the submitted forms?
choices: Daniel's Classics book is the most expensive, and Aiko's adventure book costs more than Mika's mystery book.
Mika's mystery book is the cheapest, and Daniel's Classics book is the most expensive.
