Aiko's adventure book is the cheapest, and Mika's hobby book is the most expensive.
Mika's mystery book costs the same as Daniel's hobby book, and both are Classics.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Daniel's Classics book is the most expensive, and Aiko's adventure book costs more than Mika's mystery book.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 複数資料型は**表を作ってから照合する**。ここでは 5 枚のフォームを
  「出品者 / 分類 / 価格」の3列に落とすと一瞬で解ける。
- `up to 800 yen` の up to は「〜まで」= 上限。Classics だけ上限が高い。
- 選択肢が2つの主張を並べる形なら、**両方が成立するものだけ**が正解。
  片方が正しくても、もう片方が誤れば切る。

## 🔬 文構造分析
価格規定の文:
`Set [a price] [between 100 and 500 yen]. [Books [in the "Classics" group]] may be priced
 [higher], [up to 800 yen].`
  命令文: V=Set / O=a price / M=between 100 and 500 yen
  次文: S=Books in the "Classics" group / V=may be priced (受動) / C=higher / M=up to 800 yen
→ Classics だけが 500 円超を許される。Daniel の Voices of the Sea (Classics) 700 円が
  唯一 500 円を超えており、全 5 冊中の最高額になる。
  Aiko 400 円 > Mika 300 円 も、フォームの数値をそのまま比べれば成立する。

## 📍 本文の根拠
リーフレット。「Set a price between 100 and 500 yen. Books in the "Classics" group may be priced higher, up to 800 yen.」
Form 2。「Seller: Daniel」「Group: Classics」「Price: 700 yen」
Form 4。「Seller: Aiko」「Group: Adventure」「Price: 400 yen」
Form 1。「Seller: Mika」「Group: Mystery」「Price: 300 yen」
Form 5。「Seller: Daniel」「Group: Hobby」「Price: 200 yen」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Mika's mystery book is the cheapest, and Daniel's Classics book is the most expensive.」… 最安は Daniel の Numbers and You の 200 yen。Mika のミステリーは 300 yen なので最安ではない。前半が誤り。
- 「Aiko's adventure book is the cheapest, and Mika's hobby book is the most expensive.」… 最安は Aiko の 400 yen ではなく Daniel の 200 yen。最高額も Mika の Hobby (250 yen) ではなく Daniel の Classics (700 yen)。両方誤り。
- 「Mika's mystery book costs the same as Daniel's hobby book, and both are Classics.」… Mika のミステリーは 300 yen、Daniel の Hobby は 200 yen で同額ではない。さらにどちらも Classics ではない。

questions.stem: Based on the leaflet's rules, which book among the submitted forms is NOT allowed to be sold at the fair at all?
choices: The Silent Forest by Helen Carter
Numbers and You by the Greenfield Math Dept.
The Long Road Home by James Wood
Voices of the Sea by Robert Lane
questions.explanation:
正解は「Numbers and You by the Greenfield Math Dept.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「規則上そもそも出せないのはどれか」型は、**禁止事項の列挙**を先に押さえる。
  ここでは textbooks / magazines / any book published this year の3つ。
- 禁止に該当するかは、**出品者自身のコメント**が決め手になることがある。
  分類欄 (Group) が Hobby でも、コメントが textbook と明かしていれば失格。
- `We cannot accept ~` は主催者側の明確な拒否。**例外規定は無い**。

## 🔬 文構造分析
禁止規定:
`[We] cannot accept [textbooks, magazines, or any book [published this year]].`
  S=We / V=cannot accept / O=textbooks, magazines, or any book (3つが等位)
  published this year は any book を後置修飾する過去分詞
該当するコメント:
`[This] is [the math textbook [our school used last year]].`
  S=This / V=is / C=the math textbook (our school used last year が関係節で後置修飾)
→ C が the math textbook。禁止対象の textbooks にそのまま該当する。

## 📍 本文の根拠
リーフレット。「We cannot accept textbooks, magazines, or any book published this year.」
Form 5。「Title: Numbers and You」「Author: Greenfield Math Dept.」「Comment: This is the math textbook our school used last year. It helped me a lot before exams.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The Silent Forest by Helen Carter」… Mystery 分類・300 yen・コメントあり (「I read this twice.」) で、禁止3項目のいずれにも当たらない。
- 「The Long Road Home by James Wood」… Adventure 分類・400 yen・コメントあり。禁止対象ではない。
- 「Voices of the Sea by Robert Lane」… Classics 分類で 700 yen は上限 800 yen の範囲内。祖父から譲られた古い小説であり、今年出版された本でもない。

questions.stem: In her email, Ms. Porter asks the sellers to do two things. Which combination correctly states what she requests?
choices: Daniel must add a missing comment, and Mika must arrive 30 minutes early.
Aiko must change her book's group, and Daniel must bring a large box.
Mika must add a missing comment, and she and Aiko must each bring a large box.
Mika must change her book's group, and Daniel must arrive 30 minutes early.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Mika must add a missing comment, and she and Aiko must each bring a large box.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 依頼を読み取る型は「**誰に何を求めたか**」を1対1で対応させる。
  メール中の呼びかけ (Mika and Aiko / Daniel) が対応表になっている。
- `no action is needed from you for that one` は**依頼ではない**ことの明示。
  分類の修正は主催者が行うので、生徒の作業から外れる。
- `the missing part` が何かは、フォームを見て**空欄になっている項目**を探して特定する。

## 🔬 文構造分析
不備の指摘:
`[one form] cannot be accepted [in its current state] [because [the rules] clearly say
 [what every book needs [in order to go on the table]]].`
  S=one form / V=cannot be accepted / M=in its current state, because 節
  because 節: S=the rules / V=say / O=what 節 (間接疑問)
箱の依頼:
`[Mika and Aiko], could [each of you] bring [one large box] [on the fair day]?`
  呼びかけ=Mika and Aiko / S=each of you / V=could bring / O=one large box
→ 不備は「コメント欄が空」= Mika の Form 3。箱は Mika と Aiko の2人。
  どちらも Mika が関わるので、この組み合わせだけが成立する。

## 📍 本文の根拠
リーフレット。「Write a short comment so buyers can decide. Forms with no comment will be returned to you.」
Form 3。「Seller: Mika」「Comment: (blank)」
メール。「First, one form cannot be accepted in its current state because the rules clearly say what every book needs in order to go on the table. Please send me the missing part by July 8, or that book will not be displayed.」
「Mika and Aiko, could each of you bring one large box on the fair day?」「Daniel, please arrive 30 minutes early to help set up the Classics corner.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Daniel must add a missing comment, and Mika must arrive 30 minutes early.」… コメント欄が空なのは Mika の Form 3。Daniel の2枚はどちらもコメントが記入されている。また 30 分前に来るのは Daniel であって Mika ではない。
- 「Aiko must change her book's group, and Daniel must bring a large box.」… 分類の変更は「I will move it to the correct group myself — no action is needed from you for that one」と主催者が行う。また箱を頼まれたのは Mika と Aiko で、Daniel ではない。
- 「Mika must change her book's group, and Daniel must arrive 30 minutes early.」… 分類の変更は主催者が行うので Mika の作業ではない。早く来るのは Daniel だが、前半が誤りなので組み合わせとして成立しない。

question_data.passage:
You are planning to take part in a community activity. You found a leaflet, a filled-in entry form, and an email about it.

=== RESOURCE 1: LEAFLET ===

GREENFIELD COMMUNITY GARDEN — "GROW & SHARE" FESTIVAL

The Greenfield Community Garden invites you to our biggest event of the year! For the past six years, neighbors have come together to grow vegetables and flowers on land that was once an empty parking lot. This summer, we want to celebrate what we have grown and share it with everyone in town.

When: Saturday, August 22nd, 10:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m.
Where: Greenfield Garden, behind the public library

At the festival, members will display the plants they have grown in their own garden beds. Visitors can taste fresh vegetables, learn how to start a garden at home, and buy young plants to take away. If you want to display your plants, please fill in the entry form below.

Rules for displaying plants:
- Each member may display up to three plants.
- Every plant must have been grown in our garden this year. Plants bought from a shop are not allowed.
- Plants for sale must be priced between $2 and $8. Plants that are only for display (not for sale) do not need a price.
- Vegetables, flowers, and herbs are all welcome. We cannot accept trees.
- Please write a short comment so visitors can learn about each plant.

The member whose plant gets the most visitor votes will win a free gardening workshop in September. Only plants that are for sale can take part in the voting.

=== RESOURCE 2: ENTRY FORM (filled in by a member) ===

Name: Daniel Park    Garden Bed Number: 14

| Plant | Type | For Sale? | Price | My Comment |
|-------|------|-----------|-------|------------|
| Sungold Tomato | Vegetable | Yes | $6 | These small tomatoes are very sweet. My children eat them like candy! |
| Lavender | Flower/Herb | Yes | $4 | I planted this in spring. Its smell helps me relax after a long day. |
| Giant Pumpkin | Vegetable | No | — | This is the biggest thing I have ever grown. I want to show it, not sell it. |

=== RESOURCE 3: EMAIL FROM THE ORGANIZER ===

From: Maria Lopez, Festival Team
To: Daniel Park
Subject: Your entry — almost ready!

Dear Daniel,

Thank you for your entry. We are happy that you are joining the festival again. I have checked your form, and I have two small requests before the big day.

First, your Sungold Tomato and your Lavender are both fine, and they will be part of the visitor voting. Your Giant Pumpkin will be displayed next to the entrance so that everyone can see it as they arrive, but please remember it cannot win the workshop prize.

Second, could you bring a few photos showing how these plants grew from seed to now? We would like to put them on a board so visitors can understand the whole process. Also, we still need helpers to welcome visitors at the gate from 9:30 a.m. Could you arrive thirty minutes early and help us greet people before we open? Many hands make the morning easier.

Please reply by August 15th to let me know about the photos and the early help. If you cannot come early, that is no problem — just tell me so we can ask another member.

Warm wishes,
Maria
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the leaflet (Resource 1)?
choices: To explain how the garden was built on an old parking lot
To announce the winner of this year's gardening workshop
To advertise a shop that sells young vegetables and flowers
To invite people to an event and to ask members to enter their plants
questions.explanation:
正解は「To invite people to an event and to ask members to enter their plants」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「主目的は何か」型は**冒頭と末尾**を見る。中間の背景説明に引きずられない。
- `invites you to ~` (来場の呼びかけ) と `please fill in the entry form below`
  (出品の依頼) の**2つが並んでいる**ので、両方を含む選択肢が正解。
- 誤答は「本文に出てくる語」を使うが、**役割が違う**。
  駐車場は背景、workshop は賞品であって発表ではない。

## 🔬 文構造分析
冒頭の呼びかけ:
`[The Greenfield Community Garden] invites [you] [to our biggest event of the year]!`
  S=The Greenfield Community Garden / V=invites / O=you / M=to our biggest event of the year
出品の依頼:
`[If [you] want [to display your plants]], please fill in [the entry form below].`
  M=If 節 (条件): S=you / V=want / O=to display your plants
  主節は命令文: V=fill in / O=the entry form below
→ 「来場の招待」+「会員への出品依頼」。この2つを併記した選択肢を選ぶ。

## 📍 本文の根拠
リーフレット冒頭。「The Greenfield Community Garden invites you to our biggest event of the year!」
「At the festival, members will display the plants they have grown in their own garden beds. Visitors can taste fresh vegetables, learn how to start a garden at home, and buy young plants to take away. If you want to display your plants, please fill in the entry form below.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「To explain how the garden was built on an old parking lot」… 駐車場の話は「on land that was once an empty parking lot」= 沿革の背景説明にすぎない。主目的ではない。
- 「To announce the winner of this year's gardening workshop」… workshop は「The member whose plant gets the most visitor votes will win a free gardening workshop in September」= これから決まる賞品。受賞者の発表ではない。
- 「To advertise a shop that sells young vegetables and flowers」… これは店の広告ではなく地域菜園の催しの案内。苗の販売は会員が行い、売上も会の催しの一部。

questions.stem: According to the leaflet, which plant would NOT be accepted at the festival?
choices: A small tree grown in the garden this year and offered for sale at $7
A flower grown in the garden this year shown only for display with no price
A herb grown in the garden this year and offered for sale at $5
A vegetable grown in the garden this year and offered for sale at $3
questions.explanation:
正解は「A small tree grown in the garden this year and offered for sale at $7」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「受け付けられないのはどれか」型は、**禁止条項を先に抜き出す**。
  ここでは「店で買った苗」「木」の2つが明確な NG。
- `Vegetables, flowers, and herbs are all welcome. We cannot accept trees.`
  は許可と禁止を隣り合わせに置いた形。**列挙に無いもの = 禁止**とは限らないが、
  ここは直後に明示的な禁止が置かれている。
- 価格条件 ($2〜$8) は**売る場合だけ**。非売品は価格不要。この非対称が誤答の種になる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
許可と禁止:
`[Vegetables, flowers, and herbs] are all [welcome]. [We] cannot accept [trees].`
  S=Vegetables, flowers, and herbs / V=are / C=welcome / M=all
  次文: S=We / V=cannot accept / O=trees
価格規定:
`[Plants [for sale]] must be priced [between $2 and $8]. [Plants [that are only for display
 (not for sale)]] do not need [a price].`
  S=Plants for sale / V=must be priced / M=between $2 and $8
  S=Plants that are only for display / V=do not need / O=a price
→ 木は栽培場所や価格に関係なく不可。他の3つは種類も価格も条件内。

## 📍 本文の根拠
リーフレットの Rules for displaying plants。「Every plant must have been grown in our garden this year. Plants bought from a shop are not allowed.」
「Plants for sale must be priced between $2 and $8. Plants that are only for display (not for sale) do not need a price.」
「Vegetables, flowers, and herbs are all welcome. We cannot accept trees.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「A flower grown in the garden this year shown only for display with no price」… 花は「Vegetables, flowers, and herbs are all welcome」に含まれ、非売品は「do not need a price」なので価格が無くても問題ない。
- 「A herb grown in the garden this year and offered for sale at $5」… ハーブは歓迎対象で、$5 は $2〜$8 の範囲内。条件を満たしている。
- 「A vegetable grown in the garden this year and offered for sale at $3」… 野菜は歓迎対象で、$3 は範囲内。今年この菜園で育てたものであり条件を満たす。

questions.stem: Which combination correctly describes two of Daniel's plants based on the form and the email?
choices: The Sungold Tomato and the Giant Pumpkin will both take part in the voting.
The Sungold Tomato and the Lavender will both take part in the voting.
The Lavender and the Giant Pumpkin are both priced for sale.
The Lavender and the Giant Pumpkin will both be placed by the entrance.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The Sungold Tomato and the Lavender will both take part in the voting.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 複数資料の照合型は、**フォームの欄とメールの記述が一致するか**を1件ずつ確認する。
- `Only plants that are for sale can take part in the voting.` は
  投票参加の**必要条件**。For Sale? が No のものは自動的に除外される。
- メールの `they will be part of the visitor voting` が、フォームの内容を追認している。
  **2つの資料が同じことを言っている**組み合わせが正解。

## 🔬 文構造分析
リーフレットの条件:
`Only [plants [that are for sale]] can take part [in the voting].`
  S=Only plants that are for sale / V=can take part / M=in the voting
メールの確認:
`[your Sungold Tomato and your Lavender] are both [fine], and [they] will be part
 [of the visitor voting].`
  S=your Sungold Tomato and your Lavender / V=are / C=fine / M=both
  後半: S=they / V=will be / C=part of the visitor voting
→ フォームで For Sale? が Yes なのはこの2つ。メールもそれを追認している。

## 📍 本文の根拠
リーフレット。「Only plants that are for sale can take part in the voting.」
エントリーフォーム。「| Sungold Tomato | Vegetable | Yes | $6 |」「| Lavender | Flower/Herb | Yes | $4 |」「| Giant Pumpkin | Vegetable | No | — |」
メール。「First, your Sungold Tomato and your Lavender are both fine, and they will be part of the visitor voting.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The Sungold Tomato and the Giant Pumpkin will both take part in the voting.」… Giant Pumpkin はフォームで「For Sale? No」。「Only plants that are for sale can take part in the voting」により投票対象外。
- 「The Lavender and the Giant Pumpkin are both priced for sale.」… Giant Pumpkin は価格欄が「—」で値付けされていない。売り物ではない。
- 「The Lavender and the Giant Pumpkin will both be placed by the entrance.」… 入口に置かれるのは Giant Pumpkin だけ (「Your Giant Pumpkin will be displayed next to the entrance」)。Lavender は該当しない。

questions.stem: Why can Daniel's Giant Pumpkin NOT win the workshop prize?
choices: Because it was not grown in the Greenfield Garden this year
Because it will be placed at the entrance instead of inside
Because it is for display only and not for sale
Because Daniel has already entered three plants in total
questions.explanation:
正解は「Because it is for display only and not for sale」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 理由を問う型では、**規則 → 個別事例**の順で結ぶ。
  「売り物だけが投票対象」→「これは非売品」→「だから賞を取れない」。
- `The member whose plant gets the most visitor votes will win ~` の
  whose は所有格の関係代名詞。**賞の条件が投票であること**を示す。
- 誤答は本文に出てくる事実 (入口に置く / 3つ出品) を**理由にすり替える**。
  事実として正しくても、理由として機能しなければ誤り。

## 🔬 文構造分析
賞の規定:
`[The member [whose plant gets the most visitor votes]] will win [a free gardening workshop]
 [in September]. Only [plants [that are for sale]] can take part [in the voting].`
  S=The member whose plant gets the most visitor votes / V=will win / O=a free gardening workshop
  次文: S=Only plants that are for sale / V=can take part / M=in the voting
該当のフォーム記述:
`[This] is [the biggest thing [I have ever grown]]. [I] want [to show it, not sell it].`
  S=I / V=want / O=to show it, not sell it (不定詞の目的語に否定の対比)
→ 「投票 = 賞の前提」+「非売品は投票不可」→ 賞の対象外、という2段の推論。

## 📍 本文の根拠
リーフレット。「The member whose plant gets the most visitor votes will win a free gardening workshop in September. Only plants that are for sale can take part in the voting.」
エントリーフォーム。「| Giant Pumpkin | Vegetable | No | — | This is the biggest thing I have ever grown. I want to show it, not sell it. |」
メール。「Your Giant Pumpkin will be displayed next to the entrance so that everyone can see it as they arrive, but please remember it cannot win the workshop prize.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Because it was not grown in the Greenfield Garden this year」… 栽培場所は問題になっていない。規則は「Every plant must have been grown in our garden this year」で、Daniel の出品はこれを満たしている。
- 「Because it will be placed at the entrance instead of inside」… 入口に置かれるのは事実だが、それが賞を逃す理由ではない。理由は投票の条件を満たさないこと。
- 「Because Daniel has already entered three plants in total」… 出品は3つで、規則の「Each member may display up to three plants」の上限内。数は問題ではない。

questions.stem: In the email, what two things does Maria ask Daniel to do?
choices: To lower the price of his plants and to bring extra young plants to sell
To remove the Giant Pumpkin from the entry and to reply after the festival
To vote for other members' plants and to arrive at 9:30 a.m. as a visitor
To bring photos of how the plants grew and to come early to help greet visitors
questions.explanation:
正解は「To bring photos of how the plants grew and to come early to help greet visitors」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「2つ何を頼まれたか」型は、**依頼文の形 (Could you ~?)** を数える。
  メールの Second 段落に2つ並んでいる。
- `Could you ~?` は丁寧な依頼。**疑問の形をとった要請**なので、質問と読み違えない。
- `If you cannot come early, that is no problem` は**断ってもよい**という但し書き。
  依頼であることを打ち消すものではない。

## 🔬 文構造分析
依頼1:
`could [you] bring [a few photos [showing [how these plants grew from seed to now]]]?`
  S=you / V=could bring / O=a few photos
  showing ~ は photos を後置修飾する現在分詞 / how 節は showing の目的語
依頼2:
`Could [you] arrive [thirty minutes early] and help [us] [greet people] [before we open]?`
  S=you / V=could arrive と help が等位 / M=thirty minutes early
  help us greet ~ は help O + 原形不定詞
→ 「写真を持ってくる」+「早く来て受付を手伝う」の2つ。

## 📍 本文の根拠
メールの Second 段落。「Second, could you bring a few photos showing how these plants grew from seed to now? We would like to put them on a board so visitors can understand the whole process. Also, we still need helpers to welcome visitors at the gate from 9:30 a.m. Could you arrive thirty minutes early and help us greet people before we open?」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「To lower the price of his plants and to bring extra young plants to sell」… 値下げの依頼は無い。価格については「your Sungold Tomato and your Lavender are both fine」と問題なしとされている。苗の追加持参も述べられていない。
- 「To remove the Giant Pumpkin from the entry and to reply after the festival」… Giant Pumpkin は取り消しではなく「will be displayed next to the entrance」= 展示される。返信も「Please reply by August 15th」= 祭りの前が期限。
- 「To vote for other members' plants and to arrive at 9:30 a.m. as a visitor」… 他人の作品への投票依頼は無い。9:30 に来るのは来場者としてではなく、受付を手伝う側として。

question_data.passage:
You are a second-year student at Sakura High School. Your class is preparing for a three-day school trip in October, and each student must choose one of four day-trip courses for the second day. Read the leaflet, the choice forms filled in by four students, and an email from the teacher in charge, and then answer the questions.

【Leaflet: Day 2 Course Guide】

Welcome to the Day 2 course selection! On the second day of our school trip, you will leave the hotel in the morning and spend the whole day on the course you choose. Buses return to the hotel by 6:00 p.m. Please read the four options carefully before you decide.

Course A: Mountain Hiking
Walk a 9-kilometer forest trail and enjoy the autumn leaves from the top of Mt. Aoba. A guide goes with each group. You need strong shoes and a raincoat. This course is not available if it rains, so people who choose it must also write a second choice.

Course B: City History Walk
Visit three old temples and a castle in the city center. A local volunteer explains the history of each place. There is a lot of walking on flat roads, so anyone can join. Lunch is eaten at a traditional restaurant near the castle.

Course C: Sea Kayaking
Paddle a kayak along the calm coast with an instructor. No experience is needed, but you must be able to swim 25 meters. All equipment is provided. Because of safety rules, each group can take only eight students.

Course D: Craft Workshop
Make your own cup at a pottery studio and paint it freely. The finished cup is sent to your home two weeks later. This is an indoor course, so the weather does not matter. The fee includes the cost of mailing.

Notes:
- The fee for each course is 2,000 yen, except Course C, which is 3,500 yen because of the boat and safety staff.
- Course A and Course C may be canceled for safety reasons. Course B and Course D run in any weather.
- Write your name, your first choice, and a short comment on the form.

【Choice Forms】

Form 1 — Name: Kenji
First choice: Course A
Second choice: Course D
Comment: I love walking in the mountains, and I want to see the red and yellow leaves. If the weather is bad, I would rather stay inside and make something with my hands.

Form 2 — Name: Mai
First choice: Course C
Second choice: (none)
Comment: I joined a kayak club last summer, so I am confident in the water. I can swim well, and I really want to try the sea here.

Form 3 — Name: Sota
First choice: Course B
Second choice: (none)
Comment: I hurt my knee in May, so I cannot do hard exercise yet. A walk on flat ground is fine, and I am interested in old buildings.

Form 4 — Name: Yuna
First choice: Course D
Second choice: (none)
Comment: I am not good at sports, and I get tired easily. I would like a calm, indoor day. I also like the idea of keeping something I made myself.

【Email from the teacher】

From: Mr. Tanaka (Trip Leader)
To: All Day 2 course members
Subject: Two things to check before Day 2

Hello, everyone. Thank you for sending your forms. I have checked them all, and most are fine. However, two students need to do something more.

First, Mai, you chose Course C but left the second-choice box empty. Course C may be canceled for safety reasons, so every member of that course must write a second choice in case it cannot run. Please send me your second choice by Friday.

Second, the safety office told me that Course C now has nine students who want to join, but each group can take only eight. So one student will have to move to another course. I will decide who moves by the order in which the forms arrived, and Mai's form was the last one. I am sorry, Mai. Please be ready for this.

To the others: there is nothing you need to change. Just remember to bring the right clothes for your course, and bring 2,000 yen, or 3,500 yen for Course C, on the morning of Day 2. See you soon.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the leaflet?
choices: To help students choose one course for the second day of the trip
To explain how students can change their hotel rooms during the trip
To advertise the city's temples and castle to tourists from other towns
To collect money for the school trip before the students leave home
questions.explanation:
正解は「To help students choose one course for the second day of the trip」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 資料の目的は**冒頭の呼びかけ文**に出る。`Welcome to ~ selection!` が最短の手がかり。
- `before you decide` は「決める前に」。**読み手が選択する立場**であることを示す。
- 誤答は本文に出てくる語 (temples, castle, 2,000 yen) を使うが、
  **文書の宛先と目的**が違う。誰に向けた文書かを常に確認する。

## 🔬 文構造分析
リーフレット冒頭:
`Welcome [to the Day 2 course selection]! On the second day of our school trip, [you] will
 leave [the hotel] [in the morning] and spend [the whole day] [on the course [you choose]].`
  S=you / V=will leave と spend が等位 / O=the hotel ／ the whole day
  the course you choose は関係節が後置修飾 (目的格の関係代名詞が省略)
締め: `Please read [the four options] [carefully] [before you decide].`
  命令文: V=read / O=the four options / M=carefully, before you decide
→ 「4案から1つを選ぶための案内」。目的がそのまま書かれている。

## 📍 本文の根拠
リーフレット冒頭。「Welcome to the Day 2 course selection! On the second day of our school trip, you will leave the hotel in the morning and spend the whole day on the course you choose. Buses return to the hotel by 6:00 p.m. Please read the four options carefully before you decide.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「To explain how students can change their hotel rooms during the trip」… ホテルの部屋変更についての記述は無い。ホテルに触れるのは出発と帰着の時刻のみ。
- 「To advertise the city's temples and castle to tourists from other towns」… 寺や城は Course B の内容として紹介されるだけ。宛先は自校の生徒であり、他の町の観光客ではない。
- 「To collect money for the school trip before the students leave home」… 料金は「bring 2,000 yen, or 3,500 yen for Course C, on the morning of Day 2」= 当日持参。事前集金ではない。

questions.stem: According to the leaflet, which statement is true?
choices: Course C is the cheapest of the four courses because all equipment is free.
Course D's fee already covers the cost of sending the finished cup home.
Course A and Course D both continue even when it rains.
Course B requires students to be able to swim 25 meters before joining.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Course D's fee already covers the cost of sending the finished cup home.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 内容真偽は**各選択肢を1つずつ本文に当てる**。全部当てるまで決めない。
- `The fee includes the cost of mailing.` の include は「含む」。
  **追加料金が要らない**ことを1語で示す。
- 誤答は「別のコースの条件を移植する」型が多い。
  25m 泳力は C の条件、雨天可は B と D。**条件とコースの対応表**を作ると防げる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Course D の説明:
`Make [your own cup] [at a pottery studio] and paint [it] [freely]. [The finished cup]
 is sent [to your home] [two weeks later]. ... [The fee] includes [the cost of mailing].`
  S=The finished cup / V=is sent (受動) / M=to your home, two weeks later
  S=The fee / V=includes / O=the cost of mailing
→ 郵送費が料金に含まれる = 別途支払いは不要。選択肢の「already covers」がこの言い換え。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Course D。「Make your own cup at a pottery studio and paint it freely. The finished cup is sent to your home two weeks later. This is an indoor course, so the weather does not matter. The fee includes the cost of mailing.」
Notes。「The fee for each course is 2,000 yen, except Course C, which is 3,500 yen because of the boat and safety staff.」「Course A and Course C may be canceled for safety reasons. Course B and Course D run in any weather.」
Course C。「No experience is needed, but you must be able to swim 25 meters.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Course C is the cheapest of the four courses because all equipment is free.」… Course C は 3,500 yen で4コース中**最も高い**。「the cheapest」は正反対。
- 「Course A and Course D both continue even when it rains.」… 雨天でも行うのは B と D (「Course B and Course D run in any weather」)。A は「not available if it rains」。
- 「Course B requires students to be able to swim 25 meters before joining.」… 25m の泳力は Course C の条件。Course B は「There is a lot of walking on flat roads, so anyone can join」で泳力は不要。

questions.stem: Look at the forms. Which pair of students gave a reason that matches a course rule or feature stated in the leaflet?
choices: Kenji's reason for Course D and Mai's reason for Course C
Yuna's reason for Course A and Sota's reason for Course D
Sota's reason for Course B and Mai's reason for Course C
Kenji's reason for Course C and Yuna's reason for Course B
questions.explanation:
正解は「Sota's reason for Course B and Mai's reason for Course C」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「理由が規則と合っている組み合わせ」型は、**規則と申告の対応**を1件ずつ検証する。
  さらに、その生徒が**実際にそのコースを希望しているか**も確認が要る。
- Course B の `so anyone can join` は「誰でも参加できる」= 体力の制約が無い。
  Sota の「膝を痛めたが平地なら大丈夫」と噛み合う。
- Course C の `you must be able to swim 25 meters` は必須条件。
  Mai の「I can swim well」が要件を満たす申告になっている。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Course B の規則:
`There is [a lot of walking] [on flat roads], so [anyone] can join.`
  There 構文: V=There is / S=a lot of walking / M=on flat roads
  結果節: S=anyone / V=can join
Sota の申告:
`[I] hurt [my knee] [in May], so [I] cannot do [hard exercise] [yet]. [A walk on flat ground]
 is [fine]`
  S=I / V=hurt / O=my knee ｜ 結果節: S=I / V=cannot do / O=hard exercise
  次文: S=A walk on flat ground / V=is / C=fine
Course C の規則: `[you] must be able to swim [25 meters]` → S=you / V=must be able to swim
Mai の申告: `[I] can swim [well]` → S=I / V=can swim / M=well
→ 2組とも「規則が求める条件」と「申告した事情」が一致している。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Course B。「There is a lot of walking on flat roads, so anyone can join.」
Form 3 (Sota)。「I hurt my knee in May, so I cannot do hard exercise yet. A walk on flat ground is fine, and I am interested in old buildings.」
Course C。「No experience is needed, but you must be able to swim 25 meters.」
Form 2 (Mai)。「I joined a kayak club last summer, so I am confident in the water. I can swim well, and I really want to try the sea here.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Kenji's reason for Course D and Mai's reason for Course C」… Kenji の第1希望は Course A で、D は第2希望。しかも Course D に規則上の条件は無く、「理由が規則に合う」形にならない。
- 「Yuna's reason for Course A and Sota's reason for Course D」… Yuna の希望は Course D であって A ではない。Sota の希望も B であって D ではない。両方とも希望コースが違う。
- 「Kenji's reason for Course C and Yuna's reason for Course B」… Kenji は Course C を希望していない (第1希望 A・第2希望 D)。Yuna も B ではなく D を希望している。

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT something the leaflet says about the courses?
choices: A guide or instructor goes with the students on Course A and Course C.
Course D is held indoors, so the weather does not affect it.
Course B includes lunch at a traditional restaurant near the castle.
Students on every course must write a second choice on their form.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Students on every course must write a second choice on their form.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- NOT 問題は**書かれているものを3つ潰して残りを選ぶ**のが速い。
  「書いていない」を直接証明するより確実。
- `people who choose it must also write a second choice` の it は Course A。
  **第2希望が要るのは A だけ**で、全コースの義務ではない。
- `every / all / must` のような**全称・義務の語**が付いた選択肢は、
  本文の限定条件と衝突しやすい。真っ先に疑う。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Course A の但し書き:
`[This course] is not available [if it rains], so [people [who choose it]] must also write
 [a second choice].`
  S=This course / V=is not available / M=if it rains
  結果節: S=people who choose it / V=must write / O=a second choice / M=also
→ S が「それを選ぶ人」に限定されている。全員に掛かる義務ではない。
  メールでも「every member of that course must write a second choice」と
  **that course (=C)** に限って求めており、やはり全コースではない。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Course A。「This course is not available if it rains, so people who choose it must also write a second choice.」
Course A。「A guide goes with each group.」 Course C。「Paddle a kayak along the calm coast with an instructor.」
Course D。「This is an indoor course, so the weather does not matter.」
Course B。「Lunch is eaten at a traditional restaurant near the castle.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「A guide or instructor goes with the students on Course A and Course C.」… Course A に「A guide goes with each group」、Course C に「with an instructor」とあり、どちらも本文に書かれている。
- 「Course D is held indoors, so the weather does not affect it.」… Course D に「This is an indoor course, so the weather does not matter」と明記されている。
- 「Course B includes lunch at a traditional restaurant near the castle.」… Course B に「Lunch is eaten at a traditional restaurant near the castle」と明記されている。

questions.stem: In the email, what does Mr. Tanaka ask Mai to do?
choices: Write a second choice and be ready to move to another course
Pay an extra fee for Course C and arrive earlier than the others
Bring her own kayak equipment and a second pair of shoes
Change her first choice to Course B and tell her friends about it
questions.explanation:
正解は「Write a second choice and be ready to move to another course」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 依頼が2つある型は、**メールの First / Second の段落構成**をそのまま拾う。
- `Please send me your second choice by Friday.` は明示的な指示。
- `Please be ready for this.` の this は直前の「1人が別コースへ移る」こと。
  **指示語の中身**を前文から特定する。

## 🔬 文構造分析
依頼1:
`[Mai], [you] chose [Course C] but left [the second-choice box] [empty]. ...
 Please send [me] [your second choice] [by Friday].`
  S=you / V=chose と left が等位 / O=Course C ／ the second-choice box / C=empty
  命令文: V=send / O1=me / O2=your second choice / M=by Friday
依頼2:
`[one student] will have to move [to another course]. ... Please be [ready] [for this].`
  S=one student / V=will have to move / M=to another course
  命令文: V=be / C=ready / M=for this (this = 別コースへの移動)
→ 「第2希望を出す」+「移動に備える」。この2つが Mai への依頼。

## 📍 本文の根拠
メール。「First, Mai, you chose Course C but left the second-choice box empty. Course C may be canceled for safety reasons, so every member of that course must write a second choice in case it cannot run. Please send me your second choice by Friday.」
「Second, the safety office told me that Course C now has nine students who want to join, but each group can take only eight. So one student will have to move to another course. I will decide who moves by the order in which the forms arrived, and Mai's form was the last one. I am sorry, Mai. Please be ready for this.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Pay an extra fee for Course C and arrive earlier than the others」… 追加料金の話は無い。料金は「bring 2,000 yen, or 3,500 yen for Course C」= 当日持参で、早着の指示も Mai には出ていない。
- 「Bring her own kayak equipment and a second pair of shoes」… Course C は「All equipment is provided」= 用具はすべて提供される。自前の持参は不要。
- 「Change her first choice to Course B and tell her friends about it」… Course B への変更は指示されていない。求められたのは第2希望の記入であり、移動先はまだ決まっていない。

question_data.passage:
You are a member of the art club at Greenfield High School. You found this leaflet on the club's notice board and decided to apply. Below are the leaflet, the online form you filled in, and an email you later received from the organizer.

=== LEAFLET ===

GREENFIELD CITY ART MUSEUM
Student Volunteers Wanted for the Summer Art Show

This August, the Greenfield City Art Museum will hold its biggest event of the year, "Young Eyes," an exhibition of paintings created by local students. We are looking for high school students to help us run the show. No experience is needed, but you must enjoy talking with visitors.

There are four roles. Please choose one when you apply.
- Guide: walk around the gallery and answer visitors' questions about the paintings.
- Greeter: stand at the front door, welcome visitors, and hand out programs.
- Helper: set up and clean the rooms before and after each day.
- Reporter: take notes during the show and write a short article for our website.

Important conditions:
- You must be 15 years old or older by August 1.
- Guides and Reporters must come to a one-day training session on July 25. Greeters and Helpers do not need training.
- Every volunteer must work at least two days during the show (August 5-9).
- Reporters must be able to use a computer at home to write their article.

To apply, fill in the online form by July 10. We will email you within one week.

=== ONLINE FORM (your saved copy) ===

Name: Kenji Mori
Age (on August 1): 16
Role you want: Reporter
Days you can work: August 5, 6, 8
Comment: I write for my school newspaper, so I think I can do this job well. I have my own computer, and I would love to learn how museums plan an exhibition. I am a little worried because I have a family trip from August 9 in the evening, but I can work in the morning that day too if needed.

We also asked three friends to apply. Here is what they wrote.

Name: Aya Tanaka
Age (on August 1): 15
Role you want: Greeter
Days you can work: August 5, 6, 7, 8, 9
Comment: I love meeting new people and I am good at remembering faces. I cannot draw well, so I was happy to find a job that does not need art skills. I can come every single day of the show.

Name: Sho Yamada
Age (on August 1): 14
Role you want: Helper
Days you can work: August 7, 8, 9
Comment: I am strong and I do not mind carrying heavy things. My birthday is on August 10, so I will turn 15 right after the show. I hope that is okay.

Name: Rina Kato
Age (on August 1): 17
Role you want: Guide
Days you can work: August 5, 9
Comment: I have visited many art museums and I can explain paintings in an easy way. I can only come on the first and last days because of cram school on the other days.

=== EMAIL ===

From: Greenfield City Art Museum
To: Kenji Mori
Subject: About your application

Dear Kenji,

Thank you for applying to be a Reporter for "Young Eyes." We are glad to have you on the team. Your experience with the school newspaper will be very useful.

We have two small requests. First, please come to the training session on July 25 at 10:00. There you will meet the other Reporters and learn what to write about. Second, because you will leave on the evening of August 9, please send your finished article to us by August 12, three days after the show ends, so that we can put it on the website on time.

One more thing: we noticed that one of the friends you told us about cannot join this year. We will contact that person directly to explain the reason. The other two will receive emails like this one soon.

We look forward to seeing you in July.

Best wishes,
Ms. Carter
Event Organizer
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: Among the four people who filled in the form, who cannot become a volunteer this year?
choices: Aya Tanaka, because she cannot draw well
Sho Yamada, because he is not old enough
Kenji Mori, because he has a family trip
Rina Kato, because she can only work two days
questions.explanation:
正解は「Sho Yamada, because he is not old enough」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「資格を満たさないのは誰か」型は、**数値条件**から潰すのが最速。
  年齢・日数・期限は機械的に判定できる。
- `15 years old or older by August 1` の by は**基準日**。
  「8月1日時点で」なので、8月10日の誕生日は間に合わない。
- 誤答は「本人が不安に書いたこと」を失格理由にすり替える。
  **本人の心配 ≠ 規則違反**。規則に照らして初めて判定する。

## 🔬 文構造分析
年齢条件:
`[You] must be [15 years old or older] [by August 1].`
  S=You / V=must be / C=15 years old or older / M=by August 1
該当者の申告:
`[My birthday] is [on August 10], so [I] will turn [15] [right after the show].`
  S=My birthday / V=is / M=on August 10
  結果節: S=I / V=will turn / C=15 / M=right after the show
→ フォームの「Age (on August 1): 14」と合わせて、基準日時点で 14 歳。
  本人も「右 after the show」= 催し後に 15 歳になると認めている。

## 📍 本文の根拠
リーフレットの Important conditions。「You must be 15 years old or older by August 1.」「Every volunteer must work at least two days during the show (August 5-9).」
Sho Yamada のフォーム。「Age (on August 1): 14」「My birthday is on August 10, so I will turn 15 right after the show. I hope that is okay.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Aya Tanaka, because she cannot draw well」… リーフレットは「No experience is needed」と述べ、Greeter に絵の技能は要求していない。Aya 自身も「I was happy to find a job that does not need art skills」と書いている。
- 「Kenji Mori, because he has a family trip」… Kenji の旅行は「a family trip from August 9 in the evening」= 9日夕方から。勤務予定は 5・6・8 日なので支障が無い。
- 「Rina Kato, because she can only work two days」… 「Every volunteer must work at least two days」= 2日以上が条件。Rina の 5日と9日はちょうど2日で条件を満たす。

questions.stem: Which statement correctly matches a role with a person who chose it?
choices: Aya chose the role that must attend the July 25 training.
Kenji chose the role that hands out programs at the front door.
Rina chose the role that answers visitors' questions in the gallery.
Sho chose the role that writes an article for the website.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Rina chose the role that answers visitors' questions in the gallery.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 役割と人物の対応型は、**リーフレットの職務説明**と**フォームの希望欄**を
  1対1で結ぶ。片方だけ見ると必ず外す。
- Guide の職務は `answer visitors' questions about the paintings`。
  選択肢の `answers visitors' questions in the gallery` はその言い換え。
- 誤答は「別の役割の職務」を当てはめる型。**職務の一覧表**を先に作ると防げる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
リーフレットの役割説明:
`Guide: walk [around the gallery] and answer [visitors' questions] [about the paintings].`
  V=walk と answer が等位 (原形・箇条書き) / O=visitors' questions / M=about the paintings
選択肢側:
`[Rina] chose [the role [that answers visitors' questions in the gallery]].`
  S=Rina / V=chose / O=the role (that 以下が関係節で後置修飾)
→ フォームの「Role you want: Guide」と職務説明が一致する。

## 📍 本文の根拠
リーフレット。「Guide: walk around the gallery and answer visitors' questions about the paintings.」「Greeter: stand at the front door, welcome visitors, and hand out programs.」「Helper: set up and clean the rooms before and after each day.」「Reporter: take notes during the show and write a short article for our website.」
「Guides and Reporters must come to a one-day training session on July 25. Greeters and Helpers do not need training.」
各フォーム。Kenji「Role you want: Reporter」／ Aya「Role you want: Greeter」／ Sho「Role you want: Helper」／ Rina「Role you want: Guide」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Aya chose the role that must attend the July 25 training.」… 研修が必要なのは Guides と Reporters。Aya は Greeter で「Greeters and Helpers do not need training」に該当し、研修は不要。
- 「Kenji chose the role that hands out programs at the front door.」… プログラムを配るのは Greeter の職務。Kenji は Reporter を希望している。
- 「Sho chose the role that writes an article for the website.」… 記事を書くのは Reporter の職務。Sho は Helper を希望している。

questions.stem: Which is NOT something the leaflet lists as a condition for volunteers?
choices: Working at least two days during August 5-9
Being 15 or older by August 1
Attending training on July 25 for some roles
Paying a fee to join the volunteer team
questions.explanation:
正解は「Paying a fee to join the volunteer team」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- NOT 問題は**書かれている3つを消す**。残った1つが答え。
- Important conditions の箇条書きを**そのまま照合表**として使う。
  年齢・研修・勤務日数・自宅PC の4項目しか無い。
- 費用に関する記述が**一切無い**ことが決め手。募集要項では
  「書いていない = 条件ではない」と判断してよい。

## 🔬 文構造分析
条件の箇条書き:
`[You] must be [15 years old or older] [by August 1].`
`[Guides and Reporters] must come [to a one-day training session] [on July 25].`
`[Every volunteer] must work [at least two days] [during the show (August 5-9)].`
`[Reporters] must be able to use [a computer] [at home] [to write their article].`
  いずれも S + must + V の同型。4項目すべてが義務として並ぶ
→ 主語は You / Guides and Reporters / Every volunteer / Reporters の4つ。
  費用を主語または目的語に取る文はどこにも無い。

## 📍 本文の根拠
リーフレットの Important conditions。「You must be 15 years old or older by August 1.」「Guides and Reporters must come to a one-day training session on July 25. Greeters and Helpers do not need training.」「Every volunteer must work at least two days during the show (August 5-9).」「Reporters must be able to use a computer at home to write their article.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Working at least two days during August 5-9」… 「Every volunteer must work at least two days during the show (August 5-9)」と明記されている。
- 「Being 15 or older by August 1」… 「You must be 15 years old or older by August 1」と明記されている。
- 「Attending training on July 25 for some roles」… 「Guides and Reporters must come to a one-day training session on July 25」と、一部の役割について明記されている。

questions.stem: In the email, what two things does Ms. Carter ask Kenji to do?
choices: Attend the training on July 25 and send his article by August 12
Bring his own computer to the museum and work every day of the show
Hand out programs at the door and clean the rooms after the show
Train the other Reporters and post the article on the website himself
questions.explanation:
正解は「Attend the training on July 25 and send his article by August 12」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 依頼の数え上げは **First / Second** の段落構成をそのまま使う。
- `so that we can put it on the website on time` は目的の副詞節。
  **記事を載せるのは美術館側**であり、本人が投稿するのではない。
- `because you will leave on the evening of August 9` は理由の従属節。
  **個別事情に合わせた期限**であることを示す。

## 🔬 文構造分析
依頼1:
`please come [to the training session] [on July 25] [at 10:00].`
  命令文: V=come / M=to the training session, on July 25, at 10:00
依頼2:
`please send [your finished article] [to us] [by August 12], [three days after the show ends],
 [so that [we] can put [it] [on the website] [on time]].`
  命令文: V=send / O=your finished article / M=to us, by August 12
  so that 節: S=we / V=can put / O=it / M=on the website, on time
→ 「7/25 の研修に来る」+「8/12 までに原稿を送る」の2つ。

## 📍 本文の根拠
メール。「We have two small requests. First, please come to the training session on July 25 at 10:00. There you will meet the other Reporters and learn what to write about. Second, because you will leave on the evening of August 9, please send your finished article to us by August 12, three days after the show ends, so that we can put it on the website on time.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Bring his own computer to the museum and work every day of the show」… 自宅PCは「Reporters must be able to use a computer at home」= 応募の条件であって、館へ持参する依頼ではない。毎日勤務も求められていない。
- 「Hand out programs at the door and clean the rooms after the show」… プログラム配布は Greeter、部屋の清掃は Helper の職務。Kenji は Reporter。
- 「Train the other Reporters and post the article on the website himself」… 他の Reporter の指導は依頼されていない。記事の掲載も「so that we can put it on the website」= 美術館側が行う。

question_data.passage:
You are in an English class. Read the following story and complete the Story Outline below.

The Corner Bakery

Mr. Tani had run a small bakery at the entrance of the shopping street for almost forty years. He rarely spoke. Customers came in, pointed at the bread they wanted, and Mr. Tani wrapped it without a single unnecessary word. Some neighbors thought he was cold. But those who watched him closely knew that his silence hid a warm heart.

Every morning at six, before the other shops opened, Mr. Tani left a paper bag of yesterday's unsold bread on the bench in front of the closed flower shop. He never told anyone, and he never put his name on it. The bag was simply there, and by seven it was always gone.

Aya, a fifteen-year-old student, noticed the bag one cold winter morning while waiting for her early bus. She watched an old man named Mr. Sato, who slept in the small park nearby because he had lost his home, take the bag quietly and walk away. Aya wanted to know who left the bread, so the next day she came even earlier and hid behind a vending machine. At five forty, she saw Mr. Tani place the bag on the bench and return to his shop without looking back. Aya said nothing, but from that day she began to greet him every morning.

Mr. Tani never responded with words. Still, Aya noticed small changes. One rainy day, she found a clean towel folded on the bakery counter, clearly placed there for her wet hair. Another day, when she mentioned she was hungry before a test, a warm roll appeared in her bag, though she had not bought it. She understood that Mr. Tani spoke through actions, not speech.

When spring came, the city announced a plan to widen the road, which meant the old shopping street would be torn down. Many shop owners decided to close and move away. Mr. Tani, however, said nothing about his plans. Aya was worried. If the bakery closed, what would happen to Mr. Sato, who still depended on the morning bread?

On the last day before the demolition began, Aya arrived early as always. The bench was empty. Her heart sank. But then she saw a new, larger paper bag, and beside it a small handwritten note — the first words she had ever seen from Mr. Tani. It read: "The bread will continue. New shop, two streets east. Tell our friend." Aya smiled and ran to the park to find Mr. Sato.

The corner bakery disappeared, but the quiet kindness did not. Mr. Tani had simply moved it, like he moved everything in his life, without asking for thanks.

Story Outline
- Setting: a small bakery at the entrance of an old shopping street
- Main character: Mr. Tani, a quiet baker who shows kindness through actions
- Other characters: Aya (a student), Mr. Sato (a homeless old man)
- Key events: [arranged in questions below]
- Theme: [explored in questions below]
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: Choose the two phrases that best describe Mr. Tani. (You may choose in any order.) ① talkative with regular customers ② generous in a hidden way ③ eager to receive public praise ④ consistent in his daily habits ⑤ quick to explain his feelings in words
choices: ① and ③
① and ⑤
② and ④
② and ③
④ and ⑤
③ and ⑤
questions.explanation:
正解は「② and ④」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 人物像を2つ選ぶ型は、**本文の否定文**が強力な消去材料になる。
  `He rarely spoke` / `He never told anyone` がそのまま①③⑤を潰す。
- `hidden` (隠れた) は本文の `He never put his name on it` の言い換え。
  **名乗らない善行**という核が①②の分かれ目。
- `consistent in his daily habits` は「almost forty years」「Every morning at six」
  という**期間と頻度の記述**が裏づける。

## 🔬 文構造分析
隠れた親切:
`[Mr. Tani] left [a paper bag of yesterday's unsold bread] [on the bench] [in front of the
 closed flower shop]. [He] never told [anyone], and [he] never put [his name] [on it].`
  S=Mr. Tani / V=left / O=a paper bag ~ / M=on the bench, in front of ~
  次文: S=He / V=told / O=anyone / M=never ｜ S=he / V=put / O=his name / M=never, on it
習慣の一貫性:
`[Mr. Tani] had run [a small bakery] [at the entrance of the shopping street] [for almost
 forty years].`
  S=Mr. Tani / V=had run (過去完了) / O=a small bakery / M=for almost forty years
→ 「名乗らない」= ②、「40年間毎朝」= ④。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第1段。「Mr. Tani had run a small bakery at the entrance of the shopping street for almost forty years. He rarely spoke.」
第2段。「Every morning at six, before the other shops opened, Mr. Tani left a paper bag of yesterday's unsold bread on the bench in front of the closed flower shop. He never told anyone, and he never put his name on it.」
第4段。「She understood that Mr. Tani spoke through actions, not speech.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「① and ③」… ①が「He rarely spoke」と矛盾し、③も「He never told anyone」「never put his name on it」と矛盾する。二重に誤り。
- 「① and ⑤」… ①が「He rarely spoke」と矛盾し、⑤も「spoke through actions, not speech」と矛盾する。
- 「② and ③」… ②は正しいが、③の「公の称賛を求める」は「He never told anyone」「without asking for thanks」と正反対。片方が誤りなので不可。
- 「④ and ⑤」… ④は正しいが、⑤の「言葉で気持ちをすぐ説明する」は「spoke through actions, not speech」と矛盾する。
- 「③ and ⑤」… ③も⑤も本文と矛盾する。両方誤り。

questions.stem: Put the following events into the order in which they happened. ㋐ Aya hid behind a vending machine and saw who left the bread. ㋑ Aya found a folded towel placed for her wet hair. ㋒ Aya saw Mr. Sato take the morning bag of bread. ㋓ Aya read Mr. Tani's first handwritten note.
questions.explanation:
正解は「㋒ → ㋐ → ㋑ → ㋓」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 時系列は**時を示す語**で確定する。`one cold winter morning` → `the next day`
  → `One rainy day` → `On the last day before the demolition` の順。
- `the next day she came even earlier and hid` の the next day が
  **㋒の翌日が㋐**であることを固定する。
- 手紙 (㋓) は `the first words she had ever seen from Mr. Tani` = 最後の出来事。

## 🔬 文構造分析
順序を決める文:
`[Aya] noticed [the bag] [one cold winter morning] [while waiting for her early bus].`
  S=Aya / V=noticed / O=the bag / M=one cold winter morning, while 節
`[Aya] wanted [to know [who left the bread]], so [the next day] [she] came [even earlier]
 and hid [behind a vending machine].`
  S=Aya / V=wanted / O=to know who left the bread
  結果節: S=she / V=came と hid が等位 / M=the next day, even earlier, behind a vending machine
`One rainy day, [she] found [a clean towel [folded on the bakery counter]]`
  M=One rainy day / S=she / V=found / O=a clean towel
→ ㋒ (冬の朝) → ㋐ (その翌日) → ㋑ (ある雨の日) → ㋓ (春・取り壊し前日)。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第3段。「Aya, a fifteen-year-old student, noticed the bag one cold winter morning while waiting for her early bus. She watched an old man named Mr. Sato... take the bag quietly and walk away. Aya wanted to know who left the bread, so the next day she came even earlier and hid behind a vending machine.」
第4段。「One rainy day, she found a clean towel folded on the bakery counter, clearly placed there for her wet hair.」
第6段。「On the last day before the demolition began, Aya arrived early as always... beside it a small handwritten note — the first words she had ever seen from Mr. Tani.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「㋐ → ㋒ → ㋑ → ㋓」… ㋐ を㋒より前に置いている。本文は「noticed the bag one cold winter morning」→「the next day she... hid behind a vending machine」の順。
- 「㋒ → ㋑ → ㋐ → ㋓」… ㋑ (タオル) を㋐ (自販機の陰) より前に置いている。タオルは Aya が挨拶を始めた**後**の出来事。
- 「㋐ → ㋑ → ㋒ → ㋓」… ㋐ を㋒より前に置き、さらに㋑ を㋒より前に置いている。順序が二重に崩れている。
- 「㋑ → ㋒ → ㋐ → ㋓」… ㋑ を最初に置いている。タオルは物語の中盤で、パンの袋を見つけるより後。
- 「㋒ → ㋐ → ㋓ → ㋑」… ㋓ (メモ) を㋑ (タオル) より前に置いている。メモは「the last day before the demolition」= 最後の出来事。

questions.stem: What does the story tell us about Mr. Sato?
choices: He repaired the bench in front of the flower shop every morning.
He relied on the bread Mr. Tani left out because he had no home.
He worked at the bakery together with Mr. Tani for forty years.
He was the one who first told Aya about the hidden bread.
questions.explanation:
正解は「He relied on the bread Mr. Tani left out because he had no home.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 人物の説明を問う型は、**その人物に付いた関係節**を拾えば足りる。
  `who slept in the small park nearby because he had lost his home` が核心。
- `depend on ~` は「〜に頼る」。`who still depended on the morning bread` が
  「パンに頼っていた」を明示する。
- 誤答は本文に**そもそも記述が無い**ものが多い。書かれていない = 選べない。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Mr. Sato の描写:
`[She] watched [an old man [named Mr. Sato], [who slept in the small park nearby
 [because he had lost his home]]], take [the bag] [quietly] and walk [away].`
  S=She / V=watched / O=an old man named Mr. Sato / C=take the bag, walk away (原形不定詞)
  who 節 (非制限): S=who / V=slept / M=in the small park nearby, because 節
後の言及: `[Mr. Sato], [who still depended on the morning bread]`
  who 節: S=who / V=depended / M=on the morning bread / M=still
→ 「家を失って公園で寝ていた」+「朝のパンに頼っていた」。この2点が答えの内容。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第3段。「She watched an old man named Mr. Sato, who slept in the small park nearby because he had lost his home, take the bag quietly and walk away.」
第5段。「If the bakery closed, what would happen to Mr. Sato, who still depended on the morning bread?」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「He repaired the bench in front of the flower shop every morning.」… ベンチを修理したという記述は無い。ベンチはパンの袋が置かれる場所として出てくるだけ。
- 「He worked at the bakery together with Mr. Tani for forty years.」… Mr. Sato がパン屋で働いたという記述は無い。40年働いたのは Mr. Tani。
- 「He was the one who first told Aya about the hidden bread.」… Aya は「noticed the bag one cold winter morning」= 自分で気づいた。Mr. Sato が教えたのではない。

questions.stem: What is the main theme the story conveys about Mr. Tani?
choices: People should always announce their good deeds so others can join them.
A successful business depends on speaking warmly to every customer.
True kindness can be expressed quietly through actions rather than words.
Moving to a new place means leaving old responsibilities behind.
questions.explanation:
正解は「True kindness can be expressed quietly through actions rather than words.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 主題は**最終段の一般化**で決まる。個々の出来事ではなく、それらを貫くものを選ぶ。
- `The corner bakery disappeared, but the quiet kindness did not.` の
  but が主題の在りかを示す。**消えたもの / 消えなかったもの**の対比。
- `without asking for thanks` が「見返りを求めない」= 静かな親切の核心。

## 🔬 文構造分析
最終段:
`[The corner bakery] disappeared, but [the quiet kindness] did not. [Mr. Tani] had simply
 moved [it], [like he moved everything in his life], [without asking for thanks].`
  前半: S=The corner bakery / V=disappeared
  逆接: S=the quiet kindness / V=did not (disappear が省略された代動詞)
  次文: S=Mr. Tani / V=had moved / O=it / M=simply, like 節, without asking for thanks
第4段の要約: `[She] understood [that [Mr. Tani] spoke [through actions, not speech]].`
  節内: S=Mr. Tani / V=spoke / M=through actions, not speech
→ 「言葉ではなく行動で示す静かな親切」。この2文が主題を直接述べている。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第4段。「She understood that Mr. Tani spoke through actions, not speech.」
最終段。「The corner bakery disappeared, but the quiet kindness did not. Mr. Tani had simply moved it, like he moved everything in his life, without asking for thanks.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「People should always announce their good deeds so others can join them.」… 「善行は公表すべき」は「He never told anyone」「without asking for thanks」と正反対。
- 「A successful business depends on speaking warmly to every customer.」… 商売の成功に話を矮小化している。Mr. Tani は「He rarely spoke」であり、温かく話しかける経営論は本文の主題ではない。
- 「Moving to a new place means leaving old responsibilities behind.」… 「移転は古い責任を置いていくこと」は、メモの「The bread will continue. New shop, two streets east.」と正反対。責任を持ち越している。

question_data.passage:
You are an exchange student in Canada. In your English class, you read the following story written by a classmate and made notes to complete a Story Outline.

**My Coach, My Compass**

When I joined the school basketball team in my first year, I thought talent was everything. I had been the best player at my middle school, and I expected the same here. Our coach, Mr. Dawson, did not seem impressed. At my first practice, he watched me make a long, difficult shot and simply said, "Nice. Now do it ten times in a row." I missed seven of the next ten. He nodded as if that proved a point and walked away. I felt insulted. I had come to show what I could do, not to be corrected by a man in an old grey tracksuit.

For weeks, Mr. Dawson made the whole team repeat the same basic movements until they were boring. While other players practised exciting plays, he kept me passing the ball against a wall and catching it cleanly, again and again. One afternoon I complained loudly that this was a waste of my ability. He did not get angry. He only said quietly, "A house built on a weak floor falls in the first storm." I did not understand him then, and I was too proud to ask.

The storm came in our regional final. We were ahead by two points with seconds left when I received the ball under pressure. My hands, trained by all those hours against the wall, caught it cleanly without my thinking. I passed to an open teammate, who scored. We won. In the noise that followed, I looked for Mr. Dawson. He was not celebrating with the others. He stood at the side, arms folded, watching me with a small, satisfied smile, and then he gave a single nod—the same nod from my first practice.

Later that season, my closest teammate, Leah, broke her wrist and could not play. She came to every practice anyway, calling out advice and keeping our spirits up. I admired how she stayed part of the team even when she could not play. Mr. Dawson noticed her too. He quietly asked her to keep statistics and help plan our defence. "An injured player who still serves the team," he told me, "is worth more than a healthy one who only serves himself." Leah's notes later helped us beat a stronger rival.

At our final dinner, I expected Mr. Dawson to praise our victories. Instead, he spoke about effort, patience, and caring for one another. He never once mentioned the championship trophy on the table. When it was my turn to speak, I admitted that I had arrived believing I already knew everything, and that he had taught me how little I understood. He laughed warmly and said, "Now you are ready to learn." I realised that his hardest lessons had never been about basketball at all. They were about becoming a person worth following, the way I had come to follow him.

**Story Outline**

Main character: the narrator, a new and talented but proud team member
Key person 1: Mr. Dawson, the coach
Key person 2: Leah, an injured teammate

Important events (to be put in order)
Theme of the story (to be decided)
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem:
Choose the best combination to describe **Mr. Dawson** as he is shown in the story. (You may choose more than one.)

① He praises new players quickly to build their confidence.
② He values steady, repeated practice over flashy skill.
③ He cares more about character than about winning trophies.
④ He loses his temper when players question his methods.
⑤ He refuses to give responsibility to players who cannot play.
choices: ① and ④
① and ⑤
② and ③
② and ④
③ and ⑤
④ and ⑤
questions.explanation:
正解は「② and ③」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 人物像を2つ選ぶ型は、**否定の描写**で誤答を潰すのが速い。
  `He did not get angry` `He only said quietly` が④を、Leah への依頼が⑤を潰す。
- `made the whole team repeat the same basic movements until they were boring`
  の make O V (原形) は使役。**反復練習を課した**ことが②の根拠。
- `He never once mentioned the championship trophy` の never once が
  「一度も」。**勝利より人格**という③を決定づける。

## 🔬 文構造分析
反復重視 (②の根拠):
`[Mr. Dawson] made [the whole team] [repeat the same basic movements [until they were
 boring]].`
  S=Mr. Dawson / V=made / O=the whole team / C=repeat ~ (使役 make + 原形不定詞)
`[he] kept [me] [passing the ball against a wall and catching it cleanly], again and again.`
  S=he / V=kept / O=me / C=passing ~ and catching ~ (現在分詞)
人格重視 (③の根拠):
`[he] spoke [about effort, patience, and caring for one another]. [He] never once mentioned
 [the championship trophy [on the table]].`
  S=he / V=spoke / M=about ~ ｜ S=He / V=mentioned / O=the championship trophy / M=never once

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段。「For weeks, Mr. Dawson made the whole team repeat the same basic movements until they were boring. While other players practised exciting plays, he kept me passing the ball against a wall and catching it cleanly, again and again.」「He did not get angry. He only said quietly, "A house built on a weak floor falls in the first storm."」
第4段。「He quietly asked her to keep statistics and help plan our defence.」
第5段。「Instead, he spoke about effort, patience, and caring for one another. He never once mentioned the championship trophy on the table.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「① and ④」… ①は最初の練習で「Nice. Now do it ten times in a row.」と要求した場面と矛盾する。④も「He did not get angry」と正反対。
- 「① and ⑤」… ①が矛盾するうえ、⑤も怪我をした Leah に統計と守備計画を任せた場面と矛盾する。
- 「② and ④」… ②は正しいが、④の「怒る」は「He did not get angry. He only said quietly」と矛盾する。
- 「③ and ⑤」… ③は正しいが、⑤の「出られない選手に責任を与えない」は Leah への依頼と正反対。
- 「④ and ⑤」… ④も⑤も本文と矛盾する。両方誤り。

questions.stem:
Put the following events (A〜D) into the order in which they happened in the story.

A. The narrator's well-trained hands caught the ball cleanly in the regional final and led to the winning score.
B. Mr. Dawson asked the injured Leah to keep statistics and help plan the defence.
C. At his first practice, the narrator made a hard shot but then missed seven of ten attempts.
D. At the final dinner, the narrator admitted he had once believed he knew everything.
choices: C → B → A → D
A → C → B → D
C → A → D → B
A → C → D → B
C → D → A → B
C → A → B → D
questions.explanation:
正解は「C → A → B → D」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 時系列は**段落の冒頭句**が決める。`At my first practice` → `The storm came in our
  regional final` → `Later that season` → `At our final dinner`。
- `Later that season` は「そのシーズンの後半に」。**決勝より後**であることを固定する。
- 比喩 (`The storm came`) が第2段の「A house built on a weak floor falls in the first storm」
  を受けている。**比喩の呼応**も順序の手がかりになる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
順序を決める文:
`At my first practice, [he] watched [me] [make a long, difficult shot] and simply said,
 "Nice. Now do it ten times in a row." [I] missed [seven of the next ten].`
  M=At my first practice / S=he / V=watched / O=me / C=make ~ (知覚動詞 + 原形)
`[The storm] came [in our regional final].`
  S=The storm / V=came / M=in our regional final
`Later that season, [my closest teammate, Leah], broke [her wrist]`
  M=Later that season / S=my closest teammate, Leah (同格) / V=broke / O=her wrist
`At our final dinner, [I] expected [Mr. Dawson] [to praise our victories].`
  M=At our final dinner / S=I / V=expected / O=Mr. Dawson / C=to praise our victories
→ C (初練習) → A (決勝) → B (Leah への依頼) → D (最後の夕食)。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第1段。「At my first practice, he watched me make a long, difficult shot and simply said, "Nice. Now do it ten times in a row." I missed seven of the next ten.」
第3段。「The storm came in our regional final.」
第4段。「Later that season, my closest teammate, Leah, broke her wrist and could not play... He quietly asked her to keep statistics and help plan our defence.」
第5段。「At our final dinner, I expected Mr. Dawson to praise our victories.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「C → B → A → D」… B (Leah への依頼) を A (決勝) より前に置いている。本文は「Later that season」= 決勝の後と明示している。
- 「A → C → B → D」… A (決勝) を C (初練習) より前に置いている。決勝は反復練習の成果として描かれており、初練習が先。
- 「C → A → D → B」… D (最後の夕食) を B (Leah への依頼) より前に置いている。夕食は「At our final dinner」= 締めくくりの場面。
- 「A → C → D → B」… A を C より前に置き、さらに D を B より前に置いている。二重に崩れている。
- 「C → D → A → B」… D (最後の夕食) を A (決勝) より前に置いている。夕食は物語の最後。

questions.stem: What does the story tell us about **Leah**?
choices: She was a more naturally talented player than the narrator before her injury.
She quit coming to practice after she broke her wrist and lost interest in the team.
She resented Mr. Dawson for giving her statistical work instead of letting her rest.
She kept contributing to the team in a new role even though her injury stopped her from playing.
questions.explanation:
正解は「She kept contributing to the team in a new role even though her injury stopped her from playing.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 人物の説明は**その人物が主語の文**をすべて拾ってから選ぶ。
- `came to every practice anyway` の anyway が「それでも」。
  **怪我をしても来続けた**ことを一語で示す。
- `An injured player who still serves the team` というコーチの言葉が、
  Leah の行動を要約している。**他人の評価**も根拠になる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Leah の行動:
`[She] came [to every practice] [anyway], calling out [advice] and keeping [our spirits] [up].`
  S=She / V=came / M=to every practice, anyway
  calling out ~ / keeping ~ は分詞構文 (付帯状況)
新しい役割:
`[He] quietly asked [her] [to keep statistics and help plan our defence].`
  S=He / V=asked / O=her / C=to keep ~ and (to) help ~ (不定詞2つが等位)
`[Leah's notes] later helped [us] [beat a stronger rival].`
  S=Leah's notes / V=helped / O=us / C=beat a stronger rival (help O + 原形)
→ 「出られなくても練習に来る」+「統計と守備計画という新しい役割」+「成果」。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第4段。「Later that season, my closest teammate, Leah, broke her wrist and could not play. She came to every practice anyway, calling out advice and keeping our spirits up. I admired how she stayed part of the team even when she could not play. Mr. Dawson noticed her too. He quietly asked her to keep statistics and help plan our defence. "An injured player who still serves the team," he told me, "is worth more than a healthy one who only serves himself." Leah's notes later helped us beat a stronger rival.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「She was a more naturally talented player than the narrator before her injury.」… Leah と語り手の才能を比較した記述は無い。語り手の才能に触れるのは「I had been the best player at my middle school」のみ。
- 「She quit coming to practice after she broke her wrist and lost interest in the team.」… 「She came to every practice anyway」と正反対。練習には来続けている。
- 「She resented Mr. Dawson for giving her statistical work instead of letting her rest.」… コーチへの反感は描かれていない。語り手は「I admired how she stayed part of the team」と称賛している。

questions.stem: Which statement best expresses the main theme the **narrator** learns through the story?
choices: Patient effort and humble concern for others matter more than raw ability.
Natural talent alone guarantees success once a player reaches a higher level.
A coach should always reward his most gifted player with public praise.
Winning championships is the truest measure of a team's worth.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Patient effort and humble concern for others matter more than raw ability.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 主題は**語り手の変化の前後**を対比させる。
  出発点は `I thought talent was everything`、到達点は最終段。
- `his hardest lessons had never been about basketball at all` の
  never ~ at all が「まったく〜でない」。**競技を超えた学び**であることを示す。
- 誤答は語り手が**捨てた考え**をそのまま並べる。出発点を答えにしない。

## 🔬 文構造分析
出発点:
`[I] thought [(that) [talent] was [everything]].`
  S=I / V=thought / O=that 節 → 節内 S=talent / V=was / C=everything
到達点:
`[I] realised [that [his hardest lessons] had never been [about basketball] at all].
 [They] were [about becoming a person [worth following]]`
  S=I / V=realised / O=that 節
  節内: S=his hardest lessons / V=had been / M=never, about basketball, at all
  次文: S=They / V=were / C=about becoming a person worth following
夕食での話題: `[he] spoke [about effort, patience, and caring for one another]`
→ 「才能がすべて」→「努力・忍耐・他者への配慮」への転換が主題。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第1段。「When I joined the school basketball team in my first year, I thought talent was everything.」
第5段。「Instead, he spoke about effort, patience, and caring for one another. He never once mentioned the championship trophy on the table.」「I realised that his hardest lessons had never been about basketball at all. They were about becoming a person worth following, the way I had come to follow him.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Natural talent alone guarantees success once a player reaches a higher level.」… これは語り手が入部時に抱いていて、物語を通して**捨てた**考え。主題は正反対。
- 「A coach should always reward his most gifted player with public praise.」… コーチは最初の練習で褒めるどころか「Now do it ten times in a row」と課題を出した。公の称賛を主題とはしていない。
- 「Winning championships is the truest measure of a team's worth.」… 「He never once mentioned the championship trophy on the table」と、優勝を価値の尺度から外している。

question_data.passage:
You are in an English class. You are going to read the following story written by a high school student named Sora for a school magazine. After reading, you will organize the story by completing a "Story Outline."

**The Taste of Sunday**

When I was small, my grandmother Hana lived only two streets away from us. Every Sunday morning, my mother would send me to her house to deliver fresh vegetables from our garden. I always ran the whole way, because the moment I stepped through her door, the smell of warm soup would wrap around me like a blanket. Grandma Hana made a soup she called *imo-jiru*, a thick potato soup that no restaurant could ever copy. She never wrote the recipe down. "It lives in my hands," she would say, laughing, "not on paper."

For years I begged her to teach me, but she always gave the same answer: "When you are ready, the soup will tell you." I did not understand what she meant, and honestly, I thought she was just being mysterious. I was happy enough simply to eat it.

Everything changed the spring I turned fifteen. Grandma Hana fell ill and had to move into our house so my mother could care for her. She grew weaker each week, and the kitchen, once full of steam and the sound of chopping, went silent. One quiet evening she called me to her room. From under her pillow she took a small, worn notebook and pressed it into my hands. "I finally wrote it down," she whispered. "But the words are not enough. You must cook it yourself to learn the rest."

I opened the notebook that night. The recipe was there, but the handwriting was shaky and several lines were hard to read. I felt a sudden fear: what if I cooked it wrong? What if I lost her soup forever? I closed the notebook and did not open it again for a long time. I was afraid that my failure would somehow make her absence more real.

Grandma Hana passed away that summer. The notebook stayed in my desk drawer, untouched, for almost a year. Then, on the first Sunday of the following spring, my younger brother Riku, who was only seven, climbed onto a kitchen chair and asked me a question that I could not escape: "Sora, what did Grandma's soup taste like? I can't remember anymore." His words frightened me more than the recipe ever had. A memory was disappearing, and I held the only key to it.

That afternoon I took out the notebook. My hands shook as I peeled the potatoes, exactly as I had watched her do a hundred times. The first pot was a disaster—too salty, too thin. I tried again the next Sunday, and the next. Each week I adjusted one small thing. My mother would taste a spoonful, close her eyes, and say, "Closer. Keep going." Slowly, I began to understand what Grandma had meant. The recipe on paper was only a beginning; the real knowledge came from my own hands, from tasting and correcting and remembering.

On the seventh Sunday, Riku took one sip, looked up at me with wide eyes, and said, "That's it. That's Grandma's soup." I had to turn away so he would not see me cry.

Now I make *imo-jiru* every Sunday. Riku helps me peel the potatoes, and I tell him about the grandmother he barely knew. I finally understand her words. The soup did tell me when I was ready—not before I needed it, but exactly when our family needed to be reminded that she was still with us, in our hands and at our table.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: Choose the two phrases that best describe Sora at the beginning of the story, before Grandma Hana became ill. (You may choose in any order.)  ① eager to be taught the recipe  ② confident in the kitchen  ③ uninterested in why the lesson was delayed  ④ resentful toward the grandmother  ⑤ content simply to enjoy the soup
choices: ① and ②
① and ⑤
② and ④
③ and ⑤
④ and ⑤
② and ③
questions.explanation:
正解は「① and ⑤」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「冒頭の人物像を2つ」型は、**時期を限定する条件**(祖母が病気になる前) を守る。
  後半の失敗や成長を根拠にすると外す。
- `beg 人 to V` は「〜してくれと懇願する」。**熱心にせがんだ**ことを示す。
- `be happy enough simply to V` は「ただ〜するだけで十分満足だ」。
  enough と simply が「それ以上を求めない」姿勢を作る。

## 🔬 文構造分析
熱心さ (①の根拠):
`For years [I] begged [her] [to teach me], but [she] always gave [the same answer]`
  S=I / V=begged / O=her / C=to teach me / M=For years
  逆接: S=she / V=gave / O=the same answer / M=always
満足 (⑤の根拠):
`[I] was [happy enough] [simply to eat it].`
  S=I / V=was / C=happy enough / M=simply to eat it (程度を限定する不定詞)
→ 「教わりたい」と「食べられれば十分」は矛盾しない。
  レシピは欲しいが、切実に必要としてはいなかった段階を表す。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段。「For years I begged her to teach me, but she always gave the same answer: "When you are ready, the soup will tell you." I did not understand what she meant, and honestly, I thought she was just being mysterious. I was happy enough simply to eat it.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「① and ②」… ①は正しいが、②の「料理に自信がある」を裏づける記述は無い。最初の鍋は「The first pot was a disaster—too salty, too thin」と失敗している。
- 「② and ④」… ②に根拠が無く、④の「祖母を恨む」も本文に無い。せがみはするが恨みは描かれていない。
- 「③ and ⑤」… ③の「なぜ先延ばしにされるのか気にしない」は「I did not understand what she meant」「I thought she was just being mysterious」と合わない。気にはしている。
- 「④ and ⑤」… ④の「恨み」に根拠が無い。
- 「② and ③」… ②にも③にも根拠が無い。両方誤り。

questions.stem: Put the following four events into the order in which they happened in the story.  (A) Riku tells Sora he can no longer remember the soup's taste.  (B) Grandma Hana presses a worn notebook into Sora's hands.  (C) Sora delivers vegetables to Grandma Hana every Sunday.  (D) Grandma Hana moves into Sora's house because she is ill.
choices: C → B → D → A
D → C → B → A
C → D → A → B
D → B → C → A
C → D → B → A
C → A → D → B
questions.explanation:
正解は「C → D → B → A」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 時系列は**人生の段階**で刻む。「幼少期の日曜 → 15歳の春 → その夜 → 約1年後の春」。
- `Everything changed the spring I turned fifteen.` が第1の転換点。
  **祖母が家に移る (D)** はここ。
- `I opened the notebook that night.` の that night が、
  **ノートを渡された (B) のが移住 (D) の後**であることを固定する。

## 🔬 文構造分析
幼少期 (C):
`Every Sunday morning, [my mother] would send [me] [to her house] [to deliver fresh
 vegetables from our garden].`
  S=my mother / V=would send (過去の習慣) / O=me / M=to her house, to deliver ~
転換 (D):
`[Grandma Hana] fell [ill] and had to move [into our house] [so my mother could care for her].`
  S=Grandma Hana / V=fell と had to move が等位 / C=ill / M=into our house, so 節
ノート (B):
`From under her pillow [she] took [a small, worn notebook] and pressed [it] [into my hands].`
  M=From under her pillow / S=she / V=took と pressed が等位 / O=a small, worn notebook / it
弟の問い (A): 祖母の死から `for almost a year` 後の `the first Sunday of the following spring`
→ C → D → B → A。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第1段。「Every Sunday morning, my mother would send me to her house to deliver fresh vegetables from our garden.」
第3段。「Everything changed the spring I turned fifteen. Grandma Hana fell ill and had to move into our house so my mother could care for her.」「One quiet evening she called me to her room. From under her pillow she took a small, worn notebook and pressed it into my hands.」
第5段。「Grandma Hana passed away that summer. The notebook stayed in my desk drawer, untouched, for almost a year. Then, on the first Sunday of the following spring, my younger brother Riku... asked me a question」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「C → B → D → A」… B (ノート) を D (移住) より前に置いている。ノートを渡されたのは祖母が家に移った後の「One quiet evening」。
- 「D → C → B → A」… D (移住) を C (幼少期の配達) より前に置いている。配達は物語の冒頭、幼少期の習慣。
- 「C → D → A → B」… A (弟の問い) を B (ノート) より前に置いている。弟の問いは祖母の死から約1年後で、ノートより後。
- 「D → B → C → A」… D を C より前に置き、さらに B を C より前に置いている。二重に崩れている。
- 「C → A → D → B」… A (弟の問い) を D (移住) より前に置いている。弟の問いは祖母の死後。

questions.stem: What does the story tell us about Riku?
choices: He learned the recipe directly from Grandma Hana before she died.
His question pushed Sora to finally try cooking the recipe.
He refused to eat the soup until it tasted exactly right.
He was the one who first wrote the recipe in the notebook.
questions.explanation:
正解は「His question pushed Sora to finally try cooking the recipe.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 人物の役割を問う型では、**その人物の言動が物語をどう動かしたか**を見る。
- `His words frightened me more than the recipe ever had.` の比較級が
  「弟の言葉こそが最大の契機だった」ことを示す。
- 直後の `That afternoon I took out the notebook.` が**行動の開始**。
  問い → 恐れ → 行動、という因果が1本につながる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
弟の問い:
`[my younger brother Riku], [who was only seven], climbed [onto a kitchen chair] and asked
 [me] [a question [that I could not escape]]`
  S=my younger brother Riku / V=climbed と asked が等位 / O1=me / O2=a question
その効果:
`[His words] frightened [me] [more than the recipe ever had].`
  S=His words / V=frightened / O=me / M=more than 節 (比較)
行動の開始:
`That afternoon [I] took out [the notebook].`
  M=That afternoon / S=I / V=took out / O=the notebook
→ 「弟の問い」→「レシピ以上の恐れ」→「その日の午後に着手」。

## 📍 本文の根拠
第5段。「Then, on the first Sunday of the following spring, my younger brother Riku, who was only seven, climbed onto a kitchen chair and asked me a question that I could not escape: "Sora, what did Grandma's soup taste like? I can't remember anymore." His words frightened me more than the recipe ever had.」
第6段。「That afternoon I took out the notebook.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「He learned the recipe directly from Grandma Hana before she died.」… Riku は「the grandmother he barely knew」= ほとんど知らない。直接教わってはいない。
- 「He refused to eat the soup until it tasted exactly right.」… 味見をして「Closer. Keep going.」と言ったのは母。Riku は7週目に一口飲んで「That's it.」と言っただけ。
- 「He was the one who first wrote the recipe in the notebook.」… ノートに書いたのは祖母自身 (「I finally wrote it down」)。Riku ではない。

questions.stem: Which statement best expresses what the story tells us about Sora and the lesson she learns?
choices: A written recipe alone is enough to preserve a family tradition perfectly.
Sora regrets ever asking her grandmother to teach her the soup.
True understanding of the recipe came only through cooking it herself when her family needed it.
The soup matters less than the vegetables the family grew in their garden.
questions.explanation:
正解は「True understanding of the recipe came only through cooking it herself when her family needed it.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 主題は**祖母の謎めいた言葉が最後に回収される**箇所にある。
  `When you are ready, the soup will tell you.` の答えが最終段。
- `The recipe on paper was only a beginning; the real knowledge came from my own hands`
  のセミコロンが「紙 vs 手」の対比を作る。
- `not before I needed it, but exactly when our family needed ~` の
  not A but B が「必要になった時こそが ready だった」を明示する。

## 🔬 文構造分析
学びの核心:
`[The recipe on paper] was only [a beginning]; [the real knowledge] came [from my own hands],
 [from tasting and correcting and remembering].`
  前半: S=The recipe on paper / V=was / C=a beginning / M=only
  後半: S=the real knowledge / V=came / M=from my own hands, from tasting ~
締め:
`[The soup] did tell [me] [when I was ready]—not [before I needed it], but exactly
 [when our family needed to be reminded [that she was still with us]]`
  S=The soup / V=did tell (強調の do) / O1=me / O2=when 節
  ダッシュ以下は not A but B の対比

## 📍 本文の根拠
第6段。「Slowly, I began to understand what Grandma had meant. The recipe on paper was only a beginning; the real knowledge came from my own hands, from tasting and correcting and remembering.」
最終段。「I finally understand her words. The soup did tell me when I was ready—not before I needed it, but exactly when our family needed to be reminded that she was still with us, in our hands and at our table.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「A written recipe alone is enough to preserve a family tradition perfectly.」… 祖母自身が「the words are not enough. You must cook it yourself to learn the rest」と述べており、紙のレシピだけでは足りないというのが本文の立場。
- 「Sora regrets ever asking her grandmother to teach her the soup.」… 後悔の記述は無い。むしろ最後は「Now I make imo-jiru every Sunday」と続けている。
- 「The soup matters less than the vegetables the family grew in their garden.」… 野菜は幼少期の配達の品として出てくるだけ。スープとの優劣は論じられていない。

question_data.passage:
Your team is reading a story written by a young office worker named Sora about her first months at a publishing company. Read the story and complete the Story Outline below.

The Quiet Desk

When Sora joined Marlow Press, she was sure she had made a mistake. The other new employees seemed to laugh easily and ask questions without fear, while she sat in silence, afraid that one wrong word would prove she did not belong. Her desk was at the far end of the room, next to a man named Mr. Okada, who had worked there for nearly twenty years. He rarely spoke. He drank black coffee, edited manuscripts with a red pen, and left at exactly six o'clock every day. Sora decided he must dislike her, and so she said nothing to him for two whole weeks.
