- `the sharp pain of a bad experience tends to fade faster than the pleasant feeling of
  a good one` — **嫌な記憶の方が速く薄れる**。
- `remember their past more positively than it actually was` が結果。
  **実際より良く思い出す**。これが選択肢の判定基準。

## 🔬 文構造分析
比較:
`[Studies] suggest [that, over time, [the sharp pain of a bad experience] tends [to fade
 faster than the pleasant feeling of a good one]].`
  節内: S=the sharp pain of a bad experience / V=tends / C=to fade faster than ~
結果:
`Because of this gentle forgetting, [many people] remember [their past] [more positively
 than it actually was].`
  M=Because of this gentle forgetting / S=many people / V=remember / O=their past
  M=more positively than it actually was (比較)
限定:
`[This] does not mean [(that) [we] forget [serious events]], but [the small daily annoyances]
 usually lose [their power].`
  S=This / V=does not mean / O=that 節 ｜ 逆接: S=the small daily annoyances / V=lose / O=their power

## 📍 本文の根拠
第5段。「Studies suggest that, over time, the sharp pain of a bad experience tends to fade faster than the pleasant feeling of a good one. Because of this gentle forgetting, many people remember their past more positively than it actually was. This does not mean we forget serious events, but the small daily annoyances usually lose their power.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Pleasant feelings disappear quickly, which makes people remember their past as worse than it really was.」… 速く薄れるのは不快な記憶の方。「実際より悪く思い出す」も本文の「more positively」と正反対。
- 「Both good and bad feelings fade at exactly the same speed, leaving memories perfectly balanced.」… 本文は「fade faster than」と速さの差を明示している。同じ速さではない。
- 「Serious bad events are forgotten first, while small daily annoyances stay strong forever.」… 「This does not mean we forget serious events」と、重大な出来事は忘れないと明言。日常の小さな苛立ちこそが「lose their power」= 力を失う側。

questions.stem:
After the presentation, four classmates describe their study habits. Whose habits best match the passage's advice for a healthy memory? 

Mika: "I review my notes once on the test day, but I never sleep more than four hours because I study all night." 
Daniel: "I go over new material a few times across several days, and I make sure to sleep a full night before a test." 
Sara: "I try to memorize everything I read and feel upset whenever I forget even a tiny detail." 
Kenji: "I get plenty of sleep, and instead of cramming, I revisit key points several times with breaks between them."
choices: Mika and Sara
Mika and Daniel
Sara and Kenji
Mika and Kenji
Daniel and Kenji
Daniel and Sara
questions.explanation:
正解は「Daniel and Kenji」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 助言との照合は、最終段の3つの柱で判定する。
  ①十分眠る ②間を空けて複数回復習する ③細部の忘却を気に病まない。
- `with breaks in between` が「間を空けて」= 分散学習。
  **一夜漬け (cramming) の対義**として置かれている。
- 2人選ぶ型は、**1人でも外れたら組み合わせごと切る**。

## 🔬 文構造分析
助言の中心:
`Sleeping enough gives [the brain] [the time [it needs to sort memories]].`
  S=Sleeping enough (動名詞句) / V=gives / O1=the brain / O2=the time it needs ~
`Reviewing [important material] [more than once], [with breaks in between], strengthens
 [the connections [we want to keep]].`
  S=Reviewing important material more than once (動名詞句) / V=strengthens
  O=the connections we want to keep / M=with breaks in between
`And accepting [that some details will slip away] allows [us] [to focus our limited attention
 on what truly matters].`
  S=accepting that ~ / V=allows / O=us / C=to focus ~
→ Daniel は①②、Kenji は①②③に合致する。

## 📍 本文の根拠
最終段。「Sleeping enough gives the brain the time it needs to sort memories. Reviewing important material more than once, with breaks in between, strengthens the connections we want to keep. And accepting that some details will slip away allows us to focus our limited attention on what truly matters.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Mika and Sara」… Mika は「never sleep more than four hours because I study all night」で①に反し、復習も試験当日1回のみで②にも反する。Sara も細部の忘却に動揺しており③に反する。
- 「Mika and Daniel」… Daniel は合致するが、Mika が睡眠不足と一夜漬けで助言に反する。
- 「Sara and Kenji」… Kenji は合致するが、Sara が「feel upset whenever I forget even a tiny detail」で③に反する。
- 「Mika and Kenji」… Kenji は合致するが、Mika が「never sleep more than four hours」で①に、試験当日1回の復習で②に反する。
- 「Daniel and Sara」… Daniel は合致するが、Sara は細部の忘却に動揺しており「accepting that some details will slip away」に反する。

question_data.passage:
Your English class is preparing a small magazine. As part of a writing project, your group is studying how social media affects people's connections and their ability to focus. Each member has written a short comment, and you have also collected two sources to support the discussion.

Comments from group members:

Hana: I joined social media to keep in touch with my old friends after we moved to different high schools. It really works for that. Last month I saw that a friend from my old town was visiting my city, and we met for the first time in two years. Without the app, I would never have known she was nearby. So I think these tools genuinely help us hold on to relationships that distance would otherwise break. The problem is not the connection itself; it is how often we check.

Kenji: I agree that staying connected is valuable, but I have noticed something about my own studying. When my phone is on my desk, I unlock it again and again without deciding to. Even after I put it in another room, my mind keeps wondering what messages I might be missing. I am not saying social media is bad for friendship. I am saying it quietly steals the attention I need for deep work, and I only realized this after tracking my own habits for two weeks.

Mei: For me the real worry is the comparison. When I scroll, I see only the best moments of everyone's lives, and I start to feel that my own ordinary days are not enough. I still message my close friends and that part is fine, but the endless stream of polished photos leaves me feeling more alone, not less. So I would not say the tools simply bring us together. They can also push us apart from how we feel about ourselves.

Taro: I run a club account, and honestly social media is the only reason our small club survived. We post about events and new students find us. People who were too shy to speak to us in person send messages first, and then come to a meeting. For students who feel left out at school, an online door can be easier to open than a real one. The focus problem is real, but I think we blame the tool when the habit is ours to manage.

Source A (a short article):
A psychologist writing for a student newspaper explained that the human brain treats a buzzing or flashing phone as a small reward to be chased. Each notification, she wrote, pulls attention away from whatever task is in front of us, and returning fully to that task can take several minutes. The danger, she argued, is not a single interruption but the steady habit of switching, which trains the mind to crave new input and makes long, uninterrupted thinking feel uncomfortable. She added that turning off notifications, rather than relying on willpower, is the most reliable fix, because it removes the trigger instead of fighting it.

Source B (results of a survey of 600 students at one high school):
Students were asked about their experiences with social media. The results below show the percentage who agreed with each statement.

- "Social media helps me stay in touch with friends I rarely see in person": 71%
- "I check my phone without meaning to while studying": 64%
- "I sometimes feel worse about my own life after using social media": 49%
- "I have made a new friend or joined a group through social media": 38%
- "I would find it hard to concentrate even if my phone were in another room": 52%
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: Which statement best summarizes Kenji's main point?
choices: Social media damages friendships more than it helps them.
Putting his phone in another room completely solves his focus problem.
Keeping in touch with old friends is not worth the effort it requires.
Social media harms his concentration even when he does not intend to use it.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Social media harms his concentration even when he does not intend to use it.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 主張の要約は**その人が否定した内容**も併せて拾う。
  `I am not saying A. I am saying B.` は主張を1点に絞る強い型。
- `steal` の目的語が attention。**盗む = 意図せず奪われる**という含みが核心。
- `without deciding to` は「そうしようと決めないまま」。
  **無意識の行動**であることを示し、選択肢の "does not intend to" と対応する。

## 🔬 文構造分析
無意識の行動:
`When [my phone] is [on my desk], [I] unlock [it] [again and again] [without deciding to].`
  M=When 節 / S=I / V=unlock / O=it / M=again and again, without deciding to
主張の限定:
`[I] am not saying [(that) social media is bad for friendship]. [I] am saying [(that) [it]
 quietly steals [the attention [I need for deep work]]]`
  文1: S=I / V=am not saying / O=that 節 (that 省略)
  文2: S=I / V=am saying / O=that 節 → 節内 S=it / V=steals / O=the attention ~ / M=quietly
→ 「友情への害は否定」+「集中は静かに奪われる」。後者だけが主張。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Kenji のコメント。「When my phone is on my desk, I unlock it again and again without deciding to. Even after I put it in another room, my mind keeps wondering what messages I might be missing. I am not saying social media is bad for friendship. I am saying it quietly steals the attention I need for deep work, and I only realized this after tracking my own habits for two weeks.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Social media damages friendships more than it helps them.」… Kenji は「I am not saying social media is bad for friendship」と明言している。友情への害は彼の主張ではない。
- 「Putting his phone in another room completely solves his focus problem.」… 「Even after I put it in another room, my mind keeps wondering」= 別室に置いても解決していない。completely solves は言い過ぎ。
- 「Keeping in touch with old friends is not worth the effort it requires.」… 旧友との連絡について否定的な発言はしていない。「I agree that staying connected is valuable」と価値を認めている。

questions.stem: What opinion do Hana and Taro share?
choices: Social media's main danger is making people compare their lives with others.
Social media can help maintain or build connections that might otherwise be lost.
The focus problem caused by phones is more serious than any benefit.
Online communication should replace meeting friends in person.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Social media can help maintain or build connections that might otherwise be lost.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「2人が共有する意見」型は、**表現が違っても機能が同じ**主張を探す。
  Hana は「維持」、Taro は「構築」だが、どちらも「つながり」。
- `relationships that distance would otherwise break` の otherwise は
  「そうでなければ」。**SNS が無ければ切れていた関係**を指す。
- Taro の `an online door can be easier to open than a real one` も
  比喩だが「つながる入口」を語っている。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Hana の主張:
`[these tools] genuinely help [us] [hold on to relationships [that distance would otherwise
 break]].`
  S=these tools / V=help / O=us / C=hold on to ~ (原形不定詞)
  関係節: S=that (=relationships) / V=would break / M=otherwise
Taro の主張:
`[People [who were too shy to speak to us in person]] send [messages] [first], and then come
 [to a meeting].`
  S=People who were too shy ~ / V=send と come が等位 / O=messages
`For students [who feel left out at school], [an online door] can be [easier to open than
 a real one].`
  S=an online door / V=can be / C=easier to open than a real one
→ 一方は「切れそうな関係を保つ」、他方は「新しくつながる」。共通するのは接続の効用。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Hana のコメント。「So I think these tools genuinely help us hold on to relationships that distance would otherwise break.」
Taro のコメント。「We post about events and new students find us. People who were too shy to speak to us in person send messages first, and then come to a meeting. For students who feel left out at school, an online door can be easier to open than a real one.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Social media's main danger is making people compare their lives with others.」… 比較の害を語るのは Mei (「When I scroll, I see only the best moments of everyone's lives」)。Hana も Taro も述べていない。
- 「The focus problem caused by phones is more serious than any benefit.」… Taro は「The focus problem is real, but I think we blame the tool when the habit is ours to manage」と、道具のせいにしすぎることを戒めている。利点を上回るとは述べていない。
- 「Online communication should replace meeting friends in person.」… 対面の置き換えを主張した人はいない。Hana は実際に会った話をし、Taro もオンラインを「入口」として対面につなげている。

questions.stem: Whose views are most directly supported by the argument in Source A?
choices: Kenji and Taro
Hana and Mei
Mei and Taro
Hana and Taro
questions.explanation:
正解は「Kenji and Taro」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「資料が支持するのは誰か」型は、**資料の論点を先に1文で要約**してから照合する。
  資料A の論点は「通知が注意を奪う」+「習慣が問題」+「引き金を消すのが確実」。
- `the steady habit of switching` が「切り替えの習慣」。
  **単発の中断ではなく習慣**が問題という主張。
- Taro の `the habit is ours to manage` が、この「習慣」の論点に直結する。

## 🔬 文構造分析
資料A の中心主張:
`[The danger], [she] argued, is not [a single interruption] but [the steady habit of
 switching], [which trains the mind to crave new input and makes long, uninterrupted
 thinking feel uncomfortable].`
  S=The danger / V=is / C=not a single interruption but the steady habit of switching
  which 節: S=which / V=trains と makes が等位
Kenji との対応:
`[it] quietly steals [the attention [I need for deep work]]` → 注意が奪われる論点
Taro との対応:
`[we] blame [the tool] [when [the habit] is [ours to manage]]` → 習慣の管理という論点
  M=when 節: S=the habit / V=is / C=ours to manage

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A。「Each notification, she wrote, pulls attention away from whatever task is in front of us, and returning fully to that task can take several minutes. The danger, she argued, is not a single interruption but the steady habit of switching, which trains the mind to crave new input and makes long, uninterrupted thinking feel uncomfortable.」
Kenji のコメント。「it quietly steals the attention I need for deep work」
Taro のコメント。「The focus problem is real, but I think we blame the tool when the habit is ours to manage.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Hana and Mei」… Hana は関係の維持、Mei は比較による自己評価の話。どちらも注意や習慣の論点ではない。
- 「Mei and Taro」… Mei の論点は比較であり、資料A の注意・習慣の議論とは別。
- 「Hana and Taro」… Hana の論点は関係維持で、資料A が扱う集中の問題ではない。

questions.stem: According to Source A, why does the psychologist recommend turning off notifications rather than relying on willpower?
choices: Because willpower works only for students who already study for long hours.
Because a single interruption is more harmful than a steady habit of switching.
Because turning off notifications removes the trigger instead of fighting it.
Because notifications are useful only when they appear during a reward.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Because turning off notifications removes the trigger instead of fighting it.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 理由を問う型は `because` 節をそのまま拾う。**根拠は文中に明示されている**。
- `remove the trigger instead of fighting it` の
  remove / fight の対比が核心。**引き金を消す vs 引き金と戦う**。
- 意志力に頼ることが「戦う」側だと分かれば、選択肢の判定が一意になる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
資料A の結論:
`[She] added [that [turning off notifications], rather than relying on willpower, is
 [the most reliable fix], because [it] removes [the trigger] [instead of fighting it]].`
  S=She / V=added / O=that 節
  節内: S=turning off notifications (動名詞句) / V=is / C=the most reliable fix
  挿入=rather than relying on willpower (対比)
  because 節: S=it / V=removes / O=the trigger / M=instead of fighting it
→ 「引き金そのものを取り除く」から確実。意志力は引き金と戦う方法にすぎない。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A。「She added that turning off notifications, rather than relying on willpower, is the most reliable fix, because it removes the trigger instead of fighting it.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Because willpower works only for students who already study for long hours.」… 学習時間の長短についての記述は無い。意志力が一部の生徒にだけ効くとも述べていない。
- 「Because a single interruption is more harmful than a steady habit of switching.」… 「The danger is not a single interruption but the steady habit of switching」と、単発の中断より習慣が問題だと述べている。正反対。
- 「Because notifications are useful only when they appear during a reward.」… 通知が有用になる条件は述べられていない。通知は「a small reward to be chased」= 追いかけたくなる刺激として問題視されている。

questions.stem: Which conclusion is best supported by the data in Source B?
choices: Fewer students stay in touch with distant friends than make new friends online.
A majority of students reported feeling worse about their own lives after using social media.
Most students said they had made a new friend through social media.
More than half of the students said they check their phone unintentionally while studying.
questions.explanation:
正解は「More than half of the students said they check their phone unintentionally while studying.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 数値から結論を作る型は、**過半数 (50%) の線**を基準に機械的に判定する。
- `More than half` は 50% 超。64% は該当、49% は非該当。
  **わずかな差**が正誤を分けるので、必ず数字を並べる。
- `Most` も「大半」= 過半数。38% は該当しない。

## 🔬 文構造分析
該当する調査項目:
`"[I] check [my phone] [without meaning to] [while studying]": 64%`
  S=I / V=check / O=my phone / M=without meaning to, while studying
選択肢側:
`[More than half of the students] said [(that) [they] check [their phone] [unintentionally]
 [while studying]].`
  S=More than half of the students / V=said / O=that 節
  節内: S=they / V=check / O=their phone / M=unintentionally, while studying
→ without meaning to = unintentionally の言い換え。64% > 50% なので成立。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source B。「"Social media helps me stay in touch with friends I rarely see in person": 71%」「"I check my phone without meaning to while studying": 64%」「"I sometimes feel worse about my own life after using social media": 49%」「"I have made a new friend or joined a group through social media": 38%」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Fewer students stay in touch with distant friends than make new friends online.」… 連絡維持は 71%、新しい友人は 38%。連絡維持の方が**多い**ので、大小関係が逆。
- 「A majority of students reported feeling worse about their own lives after using social media.」… 「feel worse」は 49% で過半数に届かない。majority とは言えない。
- 「Most students said they had made a new friend through social media.」… 新しい友人は 38%。Most (大半) には当たらない。

question_data.passage:
Your high school English class is preparing a short essay project on the question: "Should schools encourage students to use AI tools for studying?" Below are comments from four classmates, followed by two sources you collected for support.

**Comments from classmates**

Hana: I started using an AI study app last term, and it changed how I learn. When I get stuck on a math problem at night, I can ask the app and it explains each step until I understand. My teacher cannot answer my questions at midnight, but the app can. I used to give up on hard homework, but now I keep going because help is always there. For me, the biggest benefit is that AI removes the fear of getting stuck alone.

Kenji: I agree that AI can help, but I worry about one thing. When the app gives the full answer right away, some of my friends just copy it without thinking. They feel they have studied, but on the test they cannot solve anything. The problem is not the tool itself; it is how people use it. If AI only shows the final answer, it makes students lazy. Schools should teach students to use it as a guide, not as a machine that does the work for them.

Mei: My view is different. I think the danger is that students stop trusting their own thinking. Last month, my AI tutor confidently gave me a wrong explanation in history, and I believed it until my teacher corrected me. AI sounds sure even when it is mistaken, so younger students may not notice the errors. A human teacher knows when I am confused by my face; an app does not. I am not against AI, but I believe schools should keep teachers at the center.

Riku: I focus on fairness. Good AI tutoring apps often cost money, and a fast internet connection is not free either. If schools recommend these tools, students from richer families will get even more support, while others fall behind. In the past, everyone had the same textbook. Now, the gap may grow. So before we encourage AI, schools should make sure every student can actually use it equally.

**Source A (from a school newsletter)**

A teacher at our school ran a four-week experiment with two groups of first-year students. Group 1 used an AI app that gave full answers immediately. Group 2 used an AI app set to give only hints and questions, never the final answer. Both groups studied the same topics for the same number of hours. At the end, Group 2 scored higher on a problem-solving test and, more importantly, could explain their reasoning out loud. The teacher concluded that AI helps most when it is designed to make students think, not when it simply hands over answers.

**Source B (results of a survey of 300 students at our school)**

Students were asked which statements describe their own experience with AI study tools. The percentages who agreed were:

- "I understand difficult topics faster with AI help": all students 71%, students who own a paid app 88%, students with no paid app 49%
- "I sometimes accept AI answers without checking them": all students 64%
- "I can study at any time, even late at night": all students 80%
- "I feel I rely on AI too much": all students 45%
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: Which of the following best summarizes Kenji's opinion?
choices: Whether AI helps depends on how it is used, so schools should teach students to treat it as a guide.
AI tools are harmful and should not be allowed in schools at all.
AI is most useful because it is available at any hour of the day.
The main problem with AI is that it gives wrong answers too often.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Whether AI helps depends on how it is used, so schools should teach students to treat it as a guide.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `The problem is not A; it is B.` はセミコロンで対比を作る型。
  **B が主張の核**。
- `use it as a guide, not as a machine that does the work for them` の
  as A, not as B が**使い方の線引き**を示す。
- 「全面禁止」と「使い方次第」は別。**主張の強さ**を本文に合わせる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
問題の所在:
`[The problem] is not [the tool itself]; [it] is [how people use it].`
  前半: S=The problem / V=is / C=the tool itself / M=not
  後半: S=it / V=is / C=how people use it (間接疑問が補語)
結論:
`[Schools] should teach [students] [to use it [as a guide], not [as a machine [that does
 the work for them]]].`
  S=Schools / V=should teach / O=students / C=to use it ~
→ 「道具が悪いのではなく使い方」+「案内役として教えよ」。この2点を含む選択肢を選ぶ。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Kenji のコメント。「The problem is not the tool itself; it is how people use it. If AI only shows the final answer, it makes students lazy. Schools should teach students to use it as a guide, not as a machine that does the work for them.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「AI tools are harmful and should not be allowed in schools at all.」… Kenji は「I agree that AI can help」と有用性を認めており、全面禁止は主張していない。言い過ぎ。
- 「AI is most useful because it is available at any hour of the day.」… 24時間使える点を最大の利点とするのは Hana (「My teacher cannot answer my questions at midnight, but the app can」)。
- 「The main problem with AI is that it gives wrong answers too often.」… 誤答の多さを主問題とするのは Mei (「my AI tutor confidently gave me a wrong explanation」)。Kenji の論点は使い方。

questions.stem: A student argues: "Schools should not actively recommend AI study tools until every student can use them on equal terms." Whose comment most directly supports this argument?
choices: Hana, because AI removes the fear of being stuck alone
Riku, because paid apps and internet access may widen the gap between students
Mei, because AI sometimes gives confident but wrong explanations
Kenji, because students may copy answers without thinking
questions.explanation:
正解は「Riku, because paid apps and internet access may widen the gap between students」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「その主張を支えるのは誰か」型は、**主張の論点 (ここでは公平性)** を先に固定する。
- `on equal terms` は「対等な条件で」。**平等な利用可能性**が論点。
- Riku の `before we encourage AI, schools should make sure every student can actually
  use it equally` が、主張とほぼ同じ形をしている。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Riku の主張:
`[Good AI tutoring apps] often cost [money], and [a fast internet connection] is not [free]
 either.`
  S=Good AI tutoring apps / V=cost / O=money ｜ S=a fast internet connection / V=is not / C=free
`[If [schools] recommend [these tools]], [students from richer families] will get [even more
 support], while [others] fall [behind].`
  M=If 節 / S=students from richer families / V=will get / O=even more support
  while 節 (対比): S=others / V=fall / M=behind
`So [before we encourage AI], [schools] should make sure [(that) [every student] can actually
 use [it] [equally]].`
  M=before 節 / S=schools / V=should make sure / O=that 節
→ 「推奨の前に平等な利用を確保せよ」。設問の主張と構造まで一致する。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Riku のコメント。「Good AI tutoring apps often cost money, and a fast internet connection is not free either. If schools recommend these tools, students from richer families will get even more support, while others fall behind. In the past, everyone had the same textbook. Now, the gap may grow. So before we encourage AI, schools should make sure every student can actually use it equally.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Hana, because AI removes the fear of being stuck alone」… Hana の論点は「AI removes the fear of getting stuck alone」= 個人の学習体験。公平性の議論ではない。
- 「Mei, because AI sometimes gives confident but wrong explanations」… Mei の論点は誤答と教師の役割。利用機会の平等とは別の話。
- 「Kenji, because students may copy answers without thinking」… Kenji の論点は使い方の指導。経済格差の話はしていない。

questions.stem: Based on Source A, which statement is best supported?
choices: AI apps are equally effective no matter how they are designed.
Students who used AI for more hours scored higher on the test.
Students learn problem-solving better when the AI gives hints and questions instead of full answers.
Group 1 could explain their reasoning out loud better than Group 2.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Students learn problem-solving better when the AI gives hints and questions instead of full answers.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 実験の読み取りは**統制条件**を必ず確認する。
  `Both groups studied the same topics for the same number of hours.` が
  「時間差では説明できない」ことを担保する。
- `set to give only hints and questions, never the final answer` が Group 2 の条件。
  **設計の違い**だけが変数。
- 教師の結論 `AI helps most when it is designed to make students think` が要約そのもの。

## 🔬 文構造分析
統制と結果:
`[Both groups] studied [the same topics] [for the same number of hours]. At the end,
 [Group 2] scored [higher] [on a problem-solving test] and, more importantly, could explain
 [their reasoning] [out loud].`
  S=Both groups / V=studied / O=the same topics / M=for the same number of hours
  S=Group 2 / V=scored と could explain が等位 / C=higher / O=their reasoning
結論:
`[AI] helps [most] [when [it] is designed [to make students think]], not [when [it] simply
 hands over [answers]].`
  S=AI / V=helps / M=most, when 節 (2つが not で対比)
→ 変数は「設計」のみ。だから設計が結果を分けたと言える。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A。「Group 1 used an AI app that gave full answers immediately. Group 2 used an AI app set to give only hints and questions, never the final answer. Both groups studied the same topics for the same number of hours. At the end, Group 2 scored higher on a problem-solving test and, more importantly, could explain their reasoning out loud. The teacher concluded that AI helps most when it is designed to make students think, not when it simply hands over answers.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「AI apps are equally effective no matter how they are designed.」… 設計の違いが結果を分けたというのが実験の要旨。「設計に関係なく同等」は結論と正反対。
- 「Students who used AI for more hours scored higher on the test.」… 「Both groups studied the same topics for the same number of hours」= 学習時間は同じ。時間差では説明できない。
- 「Group 1 could explain their reasoning out loud better than Group 2.」… 理由を口頭で説明できたのは Group 2。「Group 2 ... could explain their reasoning out loud」とあり、人物の取り違え。

questions.stem: Hana claims that AI's greatest value is that students can get help at any time and therefore keep studying. Which result from Source B most strongly supports her claim?
choices: 64% of all students sometimes accept AI answers without checking them.
Among students with no paid app, only 49% understand difficult topics faster with AI help.
45% of all students feel they rely on AI too much.
80% of all students agreed that they can study at any time, even late at night.
questions.explanation:
正解は「80% of all students agreed that they can study at any time, even late at night.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「主張を支える数値はどれか」型は、**主張の核を1語に絞る**。
  Hana の核は「いつでも (深夜でも) 使える」。
- 調査項目のうち、**その語がそのまま出てくる項目**を選ぶ。
  "I can study at any time, even late at night" が完全対応。
- 誤答は**懸念を示す数値**を混ぜてくる。主張を支える向きかを確認する。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Hana の主張:
`[My teacher] cannot answer [my questions] [at midnight], but [the app] can.`
  S=My teacher / V=cannot answer / O=my questions / M=at midnight
  逆接: S=the app / V=can (answer が省略された代動詞)
`[I] used to give up [on hard homework], but now [I] keep going [because help is always
 there].`
  S=I / V=used to give up / M=on hard homework
  逆接: S=I / V=keep going / M=because 節
対応する調査項目:
`"[I] can study [at any time], even [late at night]": all students 80%`
→ 「深夜でも助けがある → 続けられる」を、80% という数値が直接裏づける。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Hana のコメント。「When I get stuck on a math problem at night, I can ask the app and it explains each step until I understand. My teacher cannot answer my questions at midnight, but the app can. I used to give up on hard homework, but now I keep going because help is always there.」
Source B。「"I can study at any time, even late at night": all students 80%」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「64% of all students sometimes accept AI answers without checking them.」… 無確認で受け入れる 64% は、Mei が指摘した誤答の危険を示す数値。Hana の主張を支えない。
- 「Among students with no paid app, only 49% understand difficult topics faster with AI help.」… 有料アプリ非所有者の 49% は Riku の公平性の論点。「いつでも使える」という主張の根拠ではない。
- 「45% of all students feel they rely on AI too much.」… 依存を感じる 45% は懸念を示す数値。主張を支えるどころか反証寄り。

question_data.passage:
Your English class is preparing essays on the topic "Should single-use plastics be banned?" Your teacher has asked everyone to read four classmates' comments and two sources before writing.

[Comments from classmates]

Maya: I strongly believe that single-use plastics, such as straws, bags, and food containers, should be banned completely. Last summer I volunteered to clean a beach near my house, and I was shocked to find hundreds of plastic bottles and broken bags buried in the sand. Animals can mistake these pieces for food and die. Some people say plastic is convenient, but I think our convenience should never come before the health of the ocean. A full ban would force companies to find better materials, and I am sure they could do it if the law required them to.

Daniel: I understand why people worry about pollution, but I do not think a complete ban is the right answer. Plastic is cheap, light, and very useful in hospitals and for keeping food fresh, which reduces food waste. The real problem is not plastic itself but the way we throw it away. If every town built a good recycling system and people learned to use the bins correctly, most of the harm would disappear. We should fix our habits, not ban a useful material.

Sophia: When I was younger, my family relied on cheap plastic bottles because we could not always afford other options. A sudden ban would hurt low-income families the most, because the alternatives, like glass or metal, often cost more. I agree that pollution is a serious issue, but any new rule must be fair. I would support a gradual change that gives people time and affordable choices, rather than a law that punishes those who have the least money.

Ken: To me, the most important question is whether a policy actually changes behavior. Banning straws feels good, but straws are only a tiny part of the plastic in the sea. If we ban one small item and feel satisfied, we may ignore the bigger sources of waste. I would rather see governments charge a fee on all plastic packaging. People notice when something costs more, and a fee would push both companies and shoppers to cut back across the board, not just on one product.

[Source A: a short news article]

A coastal town in northern Europe introduced a small fee on every plastic shopping bag two years ago. Shops kept the same bags on their shelves, but each one now cost a few extra coins. The town did not ban anything; customers were still free to buy plastic bags if they wished. Within a year, the number of plastic bags used in the town fell by almost half, as many shoppers simply brought their own reusable bags. Town officials reported that complaints from residents were rare, and most shops said the change was easy to manage. However, officials also noted that the use of other plastic items, such as food wrap and bottles, stayed almost the same, because the fee applied only to bags.

[Source B: a survey of 1,000 residents]

Residents were asked whether they agreed with different plastic policies. The results were as follows:
- Support a small fee on plastic bags: 78%
- Support a complete ban on all single-use plastics: 41%
- Worried that a ban would raise their living costs: 63%
- Already bring a reusable bag when shopping: 52%
- Believe better recycling is more important than a ban: 69%
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: Which of the following best summarizes Daniel's main opinion?
choices: Plastic is useful, so the focus should be on disposal and recycling rather than a ban.
Single-use plastics should be banned because they harm ocean animals.
A ban would be unfair because alternatives cost too much for poor families.
A fee on all plastic packaging would change people's behavior most effectively.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Plastic is useful, so the focus should be on disposal and recycling rather than a ban.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 主張の要約は `not A but B` / `should ~, not ~` の**対比の型**を拾えば足りる。
- `The real problem is not plastic itself but the way we throw it away.`
  の not A but B が主張の核。**素材ではなく捨て方**。
- 締めの `We should fix our habits, not ban a useful material.` が同じ主張の繰り返し。
  **2度言われていることが主張**。

## 🔬 文構造分析
問題の所在:
`[The real problem] is not [plastic itself] but [the way [we throw it away]].`
  S=The real problem / V=is / C=not plastic itself but the way we throw it away
条件付きの見通し:
`[If [every town] built [a good recycling system] and [people] learned [to use the bins
 correctly]], [most of the harm] would disappear.`
  M=If 節 (仮定法): 主語が2つ等位
  主節: S=most of the harm / V=would disappear
結論:
`[We] should fix [our habits], not ban [a useful material].`
  S=We / V=should fix / O=our habits / M=not ban a useful material (対比)

## 📍 本文の根拠
Daniel のコメント。「I understand why people worry about pollution, but I do not think a complete ban is the right answer. Plastic is cheap, light, and very useful in hospitals and for keeping food fresh, which reduces food waste. The real problem is not plastic itself but the way we throw it away. If every town built a good recycling system and people learned to use the bins correctly, most of the harm would disappear. We should fix our habits, not ban a useful material.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Single-use plastics should be banned because they harm ocean animals.」… 全面禁止を求めるのは Maya (「should be banned completely」)。Daniel は「I do not think a complete ban is the right answer」と反対の立場。
- 「A ban would be unfair because alternatives cost too much for poor families.」… 低所得層への不公平を論点にするのは Sophia (「A sudden ban would hurt low-income families the most」)。
- 「A fee on all plastic packaging would change people's behavior most effectively.」… 全包装への課金を提案するのは Ken (「I would rather see governments charge a fee on all plastic packaging」)。

questions.stem: Maya and Ken would most likely agree that
choices: a complete ban on all single-use plastics is the only acceptable solution.
the current amount of plastic harming the environment is a serious problem that requires action.
charging a fee on plastic packaging is better than banning any single item.
low-income families should be protected from any rise in living costs.
questions.explanation:
正解は「the current amount of plastic harming the environment is a serious problem that requires action.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「2人が一致しそうな点」型は、**手段ではなく認識のレベル**で探す。
  手段 (全面禁止 vs 課金) は違っても、問題認識は共有しうる。
- Maya は体験から深刻さを述べ、Ken は `straws are only a tiny part of the plastic in
  the sea` と述べる。**「海のプラスチックは多い」という前提は共通**。
- 選択肢が片方だけの主張なら切る。**両方に当てはまるか**を必ず確認する。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Maya の認識:
`[I] was [shocked] [to find hundreds of plastic bottles and broken bags [buried in the sand]].`
  S=I / V=was / C=shocked / M=to find ~ (感情の原因を示す不定詞)
`[Animals] can mistake [these pieces] [for food] and die.`
  S=Animals / V=can mistake と die が等位 / O=these pieces / M=for food
Ken の認識と提案:
`[straws] are only [a tiny part of the plastic in the sea]`
  S=straws / V=are / C=a tiny part of the plastic in the sea / M=only
`[I] would rather see [governments] [charge a fee on all plastic packaging].`
  S=I / V=would rather see / O=governments / C=charge ~ (原形不定詞)
→ 一方は全面禁止、他方は課金。手段は違うが「行動が必要な深刻な問題」で一致する。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Maya のコメント。「Last summer I volunteered to clean a beach near my house, and I was shocked to find hundreds of plastic bottles and broken bags buried in the sand. Animals can mistake these pieces for food and die.」
Ken のコメント。「Banning straws feels good, but straws are only a tiny part of the plastic in the sea. If we ban one small item and feel satisfied, we may ignore the bigger sources of waste. I would rather see governments charge a fee on all plastic packaging.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「a complete ban on all single-use plastics is the only acceptable solution.」… 全面禁止のみを解とするのは Maya の立場。Ken は「I would rather see governments charge a fee」と課金を推す。共有されていない。
- 「charging a fee on plastic packaging is better than banning any single item.」… 課金を推すのは Ken。Maya は「A full ban would force companies to find better materials」と全面禁止を支持しており、一致しない。
- 「low-income families should be protected from any rise in living costs.」… 低所得層の保護を論点にするのは Sophia。Maya も Ken も述べていない。

questions.stem: Which classmate's opinion is most strongly supported by Source A?
choices: Maya
Sophia
Daniel
Ken
questions.explanation:
正解は「Ken」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「資料が支持するのは誰か」型は、**資料が実際に検証した施策**を特定する。
  資料A が扱うのは「禁止しない課金」。
- `The town did not ban anything` が明示的な否定。**禁止ではない**ことを強調している。
- 効果 `fell by almost half` が「行動が変わった」証拠。
  Ken の `People notice when something costs more` と直結する。

## 🔬 文構造分析
資料A の施策と結果:
`[A coastal town in northern Europe] introduced [a small fee] [on every plastic shopping bag]
 [two years ago]. ... [The town] did not ban [anything]`
  S=A coastal town ~ / V=introduced / O=a small fee / M=on every plastic shopping bag
  S=The town / V=did not ban / O=anything
`Within a year, [the number of plastic bags [used in the town]] fell [by almost half], as
 [many shoppers] simply brought [their own reusable bags].`
  S=the number of plastic bags used in the town / V=fell / M=by almost half
  as 節 (理由): S=many shoppers / V=brought / O=their own reusable bags
Ken の主張: `[People] notice [when something costs more]` → S=People / V=notice / O=when 節
→ 「課金 → 行動が変わる」という因果が、Ken の主張と完全に重なる。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A。「A coastal town in northern Europe introduced a small fee on every plastic shopping bag two years ago... The town did not ban anything; customers were still free to buy plastic bags if they wished. Within a year, the number of plastic bags used in the town fell by almost half, as many shoppers simply brought their own reusable bags.」
Ken のコメント。「I would rather see governments charge a fee on all plastic packaging. People notice when something costs more」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Maya」… Maya は全面禁止を主張するが、資料A の町は「The town did not ban anything」= 何も禁止していない。支持にならない。
- 「Sophia」… Sophia の論点は低所得層への公平性。資料A は費用負担の公平性を扱っていない。
- 「Daniel」… Daniel はリサイクルの改善を主張するが、資料A が扱うのは課金であってリサイクル制度ではない。

questions.stem: Which statement is best supported by the survey data in Source B?
choices: More residents support a complete ban on single-use plastics than support a fee on plastic bags.
Most residents believe a ban is more important than improving recycling.
A clear majority of residents are concerned that a ban could increase their cost of living.
Fewer than half of the residents already bring a reusable bag when shopping.
questions.explanation:
正解は「A clear majority of residents are concerned that a ban could increase their cost of living.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 調査データの読み取りは、**該当する数値をすべて書き出してから**比較する。
- `A clear majority` は「明確な過半数」。63% は該当する。
- 誤答は**大小関係の逆転**や**過半数の線の取り違え**で作られる。
  78% vs 41%、69%、52% を確認すれば全部落ちる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
該当する調査項目:
`Worried [that [a ban] would raise [their living costs]]: 63%`
  V=Worried / O=that 節 → 節内 S=a ban / V=would raise / O=their living costs
選択肢側:
`[A clear majority of residents] are concerned [that [a ban] could increase [their cost of
 living]].`
  S=A clear majority of residents / V=are concerned / O=that 節
  節内: S=a ban / V=could increase / O=their cost of living
→ raise their living costs = increase their cost of living の言い換え。
  63% は明確な過半数。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source B。「Support a small fee on plastic bags: 78%」「Support a complete ban on all single-use plastics: 41%」「Worried that a ban would raise their living costs: 63%」「Already bring a reusable bag when shopping: 52%」「Believe better recycling is more important than a ban: 69%」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「More residents support a complete ban on single-use plastics than support a fee on plastic bags.」… 課金支持 78% > 全面禁止支持 41%。大小関係が逆。
- 「Most residents believe a ban is more important than improving recycling.」… 「Believe better recycling is more important than a ban: 69%」= リサイクルの方が重要と考える人が多数。逆。
- 「Fewer than half of the residents already bring a reusable bag when shopping.」… エコバッグ持参は 52% で半数を超えている。「半数未満」は誤り。

question_data.passage:
Your English class is preparing a small magazine on the theme "Should companies let employees work from home?" Four students wrote short opinions, and your teacher added two sources. Read them and complete the tasks.

Mika: I worked from home during a school project with my older sister, who is a software engineer, and I saw how much it helped her. She no longer spends two hours on crowded trains every day, so she starts work feeling calm and finishes her tasks faster. She told me that on days when she goes to the office, she is already tired before lunch. Companies should trust their workers and let them choose where they work best. People who are not forced to travel can use that time for sleep, family, or learning new skills.

Daniel: I agree that travelling less is good, but I worry about young workers. When my cousin started his first job fully from home, no one taught him the small things—how to write a polite email, how to ask for help, how to behave in a meeting. He felt lonely and almost quit. Older workers already have these skills, so home may suit them, but beginners need to sit near experienced people and watch how they work. Without that, they grow slowly and lose confidence.

Saki: For me the real problem is fairness. Not every home is a good office. My family lives in a small apartment, and my mother, who is an accountant, has no quiet room. She works at the kitchen table while my little brother plays nearby, so she cannot concentrate. Meanwhile, my friend's mother has a private study and loves working from home. If companies send everyone home, they help people with big houses and hurt people without them. The office, at least, gives everyone the same conditions.

Ren: I think the answer is a mix. My aunt's company lets staff come to the office two or three days a week and work from home the rest. On office days, the team meets, shares ideas, and trains new members. On home days, people do quiet tasks that need deep focus. My aunt says this plan keeps both the human connection and the freedom. Choosing only one side—all office or all home—throws away the good points of the other.

Source A (from a business magazine): A study followed one company that moved its sales team fully to remote work for a year. The total number of completed sales reports rose by 13 percent, because workers wasted less time travelling and could plan their own hours. However, the company also found that new employees hired during that year took almost twice as long to reach the same skill level as new employees from earlier years. Managers said the older, experienced staff did well alone, but beginners struggled because they had few chances to watch and copy skilled colleagues nearby.

Source B (from a national survey of office workers): Workers were asked, "Do you feel you can concentrate well where you work?" The results, sorted by home situation, were as follows:
- Workers with a private room at home: 81 percent said yes.
- Workers without a private room at home: 48 percent said yes.
- All workers when at the company office: 72 percent said yes.
Workers were also asked whether they wanted to return to the office full-time. Only 19 percent said yes.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes Saki's main opinion?
choices: A combination of office days and home days keeps both connection and freedom.
Working from home is good because it removes the stress of daily commuting.
Young workers should stay in the office so that experienced staff can train them.
Working from home is unfair because it benefits only those who have suitable space at home.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Working from home is unfair because it benefits only those who have suitable space at home.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 主張の要約は **`For me the real problem is ~` のような焦点宣言**を探す。
  Saki は冒頭で fairness と自分の論点を名乗っている。
- `help A and hurt B` は「A を助け B を害する」。**恩恵の偏り**を1文で表す。
- 4人の論点 (通勤 / 若手育成 / 公平性 / 折衷) を先に振り分けると、
  誤答が他人の主張であることが即座に分かる。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Saki の焦点:
`For me [the real problem] is [fairness]. Not [every home] is [a good office].`
  S=the real problem / V=is / C=fairness
  次文: S=every home / V=is / C=a good office / M=Not (部分否定)
恩恵の偏り:
`[If [companies] send [everyone] [home]], [they] help [people with big houses] and hurt
 [people without them].`
  M=If 節 / S=they / V=help と hurt が等位
  O=people with big houses ／ people without them
→ 「家に十分な空間がある人だけが得をする」= 不公平。これが主張の核。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Saki のコメント。「For me the real problem is fairness. Not every home is a good office. My family lives in a small apartment, and my mother, who is an accountant, has no quiet room... If companies send everyone home, they help people with big houses and hurt people without them. The office, at least, gives everyone the same conditions.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「A combination of office days and home days keeps both connection and freedom.」… 折衷案を述べるのは Ren (「I think the answer is a mix」)。Saki の論点ではない。
- 「Working from home is good because it removes the stress of daily commuting.」… 通勤の負担を語るのは Mika (「She no longer spends two hours on crowded trains every day」)。
- 「Young workers should stay in the office so that experienced staff can train them.」… 若手の育成を論じるのは Daniel (「beginners need to sit near experienced people」)。

questions.stem: Which two students would most likely agree that employees who must work entirely from home can have serious problems?
choices: Mika and Ren
Daniel and Saki
Mika and Daniel
Saki and Ren
questions.explanation:
正解は「Daniel and Saki」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「深刻な問題を指摘しているのは誰か」型は、**完全在宅の害**を述べた人を選ぶ。
- Daniel の `He felt lonely and almost quit.` は具体的な深刻さの証拠。
- Saki の `she cannot concentrate` も同じく実害。
  **利点を語る人 (Mika) と折衷案の人 (Ren) は含まれない**。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Daniel の指摘:
`When [my cousin] started [his first job] [fully from home], [no one] taught [him]
 [the small things]`
  M=When 節 / S=no one / V=taught / O1=him / O2=the small things
`[He] felt [lonely] and almost quit.`
  S=He / V=felt と quit が等位 / C=lonely
Saki の指摘:
`[She] works [at the kitchen table] [while [my little brother] plays [nearby]], so [she]
 cannot concentrate.`
  S=She / V=works / M=at the kitchen table, while 節
  結果節: S=she / V=cannot concentrate
→ 一方は孤立と成長の停滞、他方は集中できない環境。どちらも完全在宅の実害。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Daniel のコメント。「When my cousin started his first job fully from home, no one taught him the small things—how to write a polite email, how to ask for help, how to behave in a meeting. He felt lonely and almost quit.」
Saki のコメント。「She works at the kitchen table while my little brother plays nearby, so she cannot concentrate.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Mika and Ren」… Mika は在宅を強く支持し (「Companies should trust their workers」)、Ren は折衷案を述べる。どちらも完全在宅の害を主眼にしていない。
- 「Mika and Daniel」… Mika は在宅の利点を語る側。Daniel と組ませても「両者が害を指摘」にはならない。
- 「Saki and Ren」… Ren は「Choosing only one side—all office or all home—throws away the good points of the other」と両極を避ける立場。害の指摘が主眼ではない。

questions.stem: Whose opinion does Ren's idea most directly try to combine?
choices: Mika's view that workers should be free from commuting, and Daniel's view that beginners need experienced people nearby.
Saki's view about unfair housing, and Source B's survey numbers.
Daniel's view about loneliness, and Saki's view about kitchen tables.
Mika's view about trust, and Saki's view that the office gives equal conditions.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Mika's view that workers should be free from commuting, and Daniel's view that beginners need experienced people nearby.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「誰と誰の意見を結ぼうとしているか」型は、**折衷案の2つの柱**を分解する。
  Ren の案は「office days」と「home days」の2本立て。
- office days の目的が `the team meets, shares ideas, and trains new members`。
  → Daniel の「若手には近くに経験者が要る」に対応。
- home days の目的が `people do quiet tasks that need deep focus`。
  → Mika の「通勤から解放され集中できる」に対応。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Ren の折衷案:
`[My aunt's company] lets [staff] [come to the office two or three days a week and work
 from home the rest].`
  S=My aunt's company / V=lets / O=staff / C=come ~ and work ~ (原形不定詞2つ)
`On office days, [the team] meets, shares [ideas], and trains [new members].`
  M=On office days / S=the team / V=meets, shares, trains の3つが等位
`On home days, [people] do [quiet tasks [that need deep focus]].`
  M=On home days / S=people / V=do / O=quiet tasks that need deep focus
締め: `Choosing only one side ... throws away [the good points of the other].`
→ 「新人の訓練」= Daniel、「通勤なしの集中時間」= Mika。両者の長所を残す設計。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Ren のコメント。「My aunt's company lets staff come to the office two or three days a week and work from home the rest. On office days, the team meets, shares ideas, and trains new members. On home days, people do quiet tasks that need deep focus. My aunt says this plan keeps both the human connection and the freedom.」
Daniel のコメント。「beginners need to sit near experienced people and watch how they work」
Mika のコメント。「People who are not forced to travel can use that time for sleep, family, or learning new skills.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Saki's view about unfair housing, and Source B's survey numbers.」… Saki の住環境の不公平は Ren の案が直接扱う論点ではない。資料B は生徒の意見でもない。
- 「Daniel's view about loneliness, and Saki's view about kitchen tables.」… 孤独 (Daniel) と台所の机 (Saki) はどちらも在宅の害。Ren が結ぼうとしているのは害同士ではなく、在宅と出社それぞれの**長所**。
- 「Mika's view about trust, and Saki's view that the office gives equal conditions.」… Saki は「The office, at least, gives everyone the same conditions」と出社を評価しており、折衷案が結ぼうとする在宅の長所とは別。

questions.stem: According to Source A, which statement is best supported?
choices: Both experienced and new workers improved equally under remote work.
Remote work lowered the number of sales reports but helped new workers grow faster.
Remote work raised output but slowed the growth of newly hired workers.
Remote work failed because experienced staff could not work alone.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Remote work raised output but slowed the growth of newly hired workers.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 実験・調査の要約は**良い結果と悪い結果を両方**拾う。
  片方だけの選択肢は不十分、方向を逆にした選択肢は誤り。
- `rose by 13 percent` が生産性の向上、
  `took almost twice as long` が新人の成長の遅れ。
- `However` が転換の合図。**その前後で評価が分かれる**。

## 🔬 文構造分析
良い結果:
`[The total number of completed sales reports] rose [by 13 percent], because [workers]
 wasted [less time travelling] and could plan [their own hours].`
  S=The total number of completed sales reports / V=rose / M=by 13 percent
  because 節: S=workers / V=wasted と could plan が等位
悪い結果:
`However, [the company] also found [that [new employees [hired during that year]] took
 [almost twice as long] [to reach the same skill level as new employees from earlier years]].`
  S=the company / V=found / O=that 節
  節内: S=new employees hired during that year / V=took / O=almost twice as long
→ 「生産は上がった」+「新人の成長は遅れた」。両方を含む選択肢が正解。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A。「The total number of completed sales reports rose by 13 percent, because workers wasted less time travelling and could plan their own hours. However, the company also found that new employees hired during that year took almost twice as long to reach the same skill level as new employees from earlier years. Managers said the older, experienced staff did well alone, but beginners struggled because they had few chances to watch and copy skilled colleagues nearby.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Both experienced and new workers improved equally under remote work.」… 新人は「took almost twice as long」= 遅れており、経験者と同等に伸びてはいない。
- 「Remote work lowered the number of sales reports but helped new workers grow faster.」… 報告書は「rose by 13 percent」= 増えた。新人の成長も速まっていない。両方逆。
- 「Remote work failed because experienced staff could not work alone.」… 「the older, experienced staff did well alone」= 経験者はうまくやっていた。失敗の原因ではない。

questions.stem: Using the numbers in Source B, which conclusion is most clearly supported?
choices: Workers without a private room concentrate just as well as those with one.
Having a private room at home makes a large difference in whether workers feel they can concentrate.
Most workers want to go back to the office full-time.
Workers concentrate better in the office than anywhere at home.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Having a private room at home makes a large difference in whether workers feel they can concentrate.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 数値比較は**3つの数字を並べてから**判定する。81% / 48% / 72%。
- 専用部屋の有無で 81% と 48%。**33ポイントの差**は「大きな違い」と言える。
- オフィスの 72% は 48% より高いが 81% より低い。
  **「家のどこよりオフィスが上」は成立しない**。ここが最大の引っかけ。

## 🔬 文構造分析
調査結果:
`[Workers [with a private room at home]]: 81 percent said [yes].`
`[Workers [without a private room at home]]: 48 percent said [yes].`
`[All workers [when at the company office]]: 72 percent said [yes].`
  いずれも S + V(said) + O(yes) の同型。修飾語だけが条件を分ける
選択肢側:
`[Having a private room at home] makes [a large difference] [in whether workers feel they
 can concentrate].`
  S=Having a private room at home (動名詞句) / V=makes / O=a large difference
  M=in whether 節
→ 81 − 48 = 33 ポイント。差が大きいという結論だけが数値から直接言える。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source B。「Workers with a private room at home: 81 percent said yes.」「Workers without a private room at home: 48 percent said yes.」「All workers when at the company office: 72 percent said yes.」「Workers were also asked whether they wanted to return to the office full-time. Only 19 percent said yes.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Workers without a private room concentrate just as well as those with one.」… 81% と 48% で 33 ポイントの差がある。「同じくらい」は数値と矛盾する。
- 「Most workers want to go back to the office full-time.」… フルタイム復帰を望むのは「Only 19 percent」。大半どころか少数。
- 「Workers concentrate better in the office than anywhere at home.」… オフィスの 72% は、専用部屋がある人の 81% より低い。「家のどこより上」は成立しない。

question_data.passage:
Your English class is preparing essays on the theme "Tourism and Local Culture." Read the four students' opinions and the two sources below, and answer the questions that follow.

**Mika:** I grew up in a small mountain town that almost no one visited ten years ago. Now, thousands of travelers come every autumn to see the colored leaves. The visitors spend money at our shops and restaurants, so several closed stores have reopened, and three of my old classmates moved back to run a café and a guesthouse. Without tourism, our young people would have left forever. To me, the most important thing is that the town is alive again, even if the streets are sometimes crowded.

**Daniel:** I understand that tourism brings money, but I worry about what it does to a culture. In the old town where I live, the local craft shops that made pottery and woven baskets have been replaced by stores selling cheap key rings and the same T-shirts you can buy anywhere. The festivals that were once for the community are now performed mainly for cameras. Money is flowing in, yet what makes our town special is quietly disappearing. We should protect the real culture, not turn it into a show.

**Sora:** Both sides have a point, but the real question is who decides. In many places, big outside companies build the hotels and keep most of the profit, while local people only get low-paying jobs and rising rents. I believe tourism can be good, but only when the community itself controls it. If residents own the businesses and set the rules, the benefits stay local and the culture is respected. Otherwise, we are just selling our home to strangers.

**Emma:** I think we worry too much. Travel lets people from different countries meet and learn from one another. When I visited my grandparents' village, tourists asked me about our customs, and I felt proud to explain them. Sharing our culture with the world is not the same as losing it. As long as we keep teaching the meaning behind our traditions to the next generation, a few souvenir shops will not erase who we are.

**Source A (newspaper article):**
Last year, the historic district of Riverton introduced a "community tourism" rule. Any new hotel or restaurant must be at least half-owned by local residents, and a small share of every visitor's spending goes into a town fund. The fund has already paid to repair an old theater and to train young people in traditional weaving. The mayor reported that, unlike in nearby towns where outside firms dominate, most of Riverton's tourism income now stays in the community, and complaints about rising rents have fallen sharply. Several residents who had moved away have returned to open family businesses.

**Source B (survey data):**
A survey asked 500 residents of tourist towns whether they agreed that "tourism has improved life in my town." Results are shown by the type of town:
- Towns where most businesses are locally owned: 71% agreed, 18% disagreed, 11% unsure.
- Towns where most businesses are owned by outside companies: 34% agreed, 52% disagreed, 14% unsure.
- Towns with very few tourists: 40% agreed, 25% disagreed, 35% unsure.
The survey also found that in locally owned towns, 66% said local traditions were "well preserved," while in outside-owned towns only 29% said so.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: What is Daniel's main point?
choices: Tourism should be stopped because it never brings any money to small towns.
Local people should sell more T-shirts and key rings to earn money from visitors.
The income from tourism is causing the town's genuine culture to fade as authentic crafts and community festivals are replaced by commercial imitations.
Festivals are better when they are performed for tourists with cameras.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The income from tourism is causing the town's genuine culture to fade as authentic crafts and community festivals are replaced by commercial imitations.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `Money is flowing in, yet ~` の yet は逆接。
  **金は入るが失われるもの**という対比が主張の核。
- `have been replaced by ~` は受動の現在完了。
  「〜に取って代わられた」= 本物が消えて商業的な模造品が残る。
- 「観光を止めろ」とは述べていない。**主張の強さを本文に合わせる**。

## 🔬 文構造分析
置き換えの指摘:
`[the local craft shops [that made pottery and woven baskets]] have been replaced [by stores
 [selling cheap key rings and the same T-shirts [you can buy anywhere]]].`
  S=the local craft shops that made ~ / V=have been replaced (受動・現在完了)
  M=by stores selling ~
`[The festivals [that were once for the community]] are now performed [mainly for cameras].`
  S=The festivals that were once for the community / V=are performed / M=mainly for cameras
対比:
`[Money] is flowing in, yet [what makes our town special] is quietly disappearing.`
  S=Money / V=is flowing in ｜ 逆接: S=what makes our town special / V=is disappearing

## 📍 本文の根拠
Daniel のコメント。「In the old town where I live, the local craft shops that made pottery and woven baskets have been replaced by stores selling cheap key rings and the same T-shirts you can buy anywhere. The festivals that were once for the community are now performed mainly for cameras. Money is flowing in, yet what makes our town special is quietly disappearing. We should protect the real culture, not turn it into a show.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Tourism should be stopped because it never brings any money to small towns.」… Daniel は「I understand that tourism brings money」と収入を認めている。「一切金をもたらさない」は本文と逆で、観光の停止も主張していない。
- 「Local people should sell more T-shirts and key rings to earn money from visitors.」… 安い土産物こそ Daniel が問題視している対象。売れと主張するのは正反対。
- 「Festivals are better when they are performed for tourists with cameras.」… カメラ向けの祭りは「We should protect the real culture, not turn it into a show」と否定されている。

questions.stem: Which opinion is shared by both Mika and Emma?
choices: Tourism should be controlled only by local residents who own the businesses.
The arrival of tourists has, on balance, a positive effect and need not be feared.
Souvenir shops are destroying the identity of every town they appear in.
Outside companies take most of the profit and leave locals with low-paying jobs.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The arrival of tourists has, on balance, a positive effect and need not be feared.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「2人が共有する意見」型は、**態度の向き (肯定 / 否定)** を先に揃える。
  Mika は「町が生き返った」、Emma は「心配しすぎ」。どちらも肯定側。
- `even if the streets are sometimes crowded` の even if は譲歩。
  **欠点を認めたうえで肯定**という同じ構えを Emma も取る。
- 誤答は Sora の主張 (地域が管理すべき / 外部企業が利益を吸う) が中心。

## 🔬 文構造分析
Mika の肯定:
`To me, [the most important thing] is [that [the town] is [alive again]], [even if
 [the streets] are sometimes [crowded]].`
  S=the most important thing / V=is / C=that 節 / M=even if 節 (譲歩)
Emma の肯定:
`[I] think [(that) [we] worry [too much]].`
  S=I / V=think / O=that 節 → 節内 S=we / V=worry / M=too much
`As long as [we] keep teaching [the meaning behind our traditions] [to the next generation],
 [a few souvenir shops] will not erase [who we are].`
  M=As long as 節 (条件) / S=a few souvenir shops / V=will not erase / O=who we are
→ どちらも「欠点はあるが全体として良い、恐れるには及ばない」。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Mika のコメント。「Without tourism, our young people would have left forever. To me, the most important thing is that the town is alive again, even if the streets are sometimes crowded.」
Emma のコメント。「I think we worry too much... Sharing our culture with the world is not the same as losing it. As long as we keep teaching the meaning behind our traditions to the next generation, a few souvenir shops will not erase who we are.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Tourism should be controlled only by local residents who own the businesses.」… 住民による管理を主張するのは Sora (「tourism can be good, but only when the community itself controls it」)。Mika も Emma も述べていない。
- 「Souvenir shops are destroying the identity of every town they appear in.」… 土産物店が町の個性を壊すと述べるのは Daniel。Emma はむしろ「a few souvenir shops will not erase who we are」と否定している。
- 「Outside companies take most of the profit and leave locals with low-paying jobs.」… 外部企業が利益を持ち去るという指摘は Sora のもの (「big outside companies build the hotels and keep most of the profit」)。

questions.stem: Whose opinions are most directly supported by Source A?
choices: Daniel and Emma
Mika and Daniel
Emma and Sora
Sora and Mika
questions.explanation:
正解は「Sora and Mika」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「資料が支持するのは誰か」型は、**資料が示した事実を2つに分解**する。
  ①住民所有を義務づけ収入が地域に残る ②出ていた住民が戻り家業を始めた。
- ①は Sora の「地域が管理してこそ利益が残る」に対応。
- ②は Mika の「同級生が戻ってカフェと民宿を始めた」に対応。
  **具体的な出来事の一致**が決め手。

## 🔬 文構造分析
資料A の制度と効果:
`[Any new hotel or restaurant] must be [at least half-owned by local residents], and
 [a small share of every visitor's spending] goes [into a town fund].`
  S=Any new hotel or restaurant / V=must be / C=at least half-owned by local residents
  S=a small share of every visitor's spending / V=goes / M=into a town fund
`most of Riverton's tourism income now stays [in the community]`
  S=most of Riverton's tourism income / V=stays / M=in the community
`[Several residents [who had moved away]] have returned [to open family businesses].`
  S=Several residents who had moved away / V=have returned / M=to open family businesses
Sora の主張: `[tourism] can be [good], but only [when [the community itself] controls it]`
Mika の経験: `[three of my old classmates] moved back [to run a café and a guesthouse]`

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A。「Any new hotel or restaurant must be at least half-owned by local residents, and a small share of every visitor's spending goes into a town fund... most of Riverton's tourism income now stays in the community, and complaints about rising rents have fallen sharply. Several residents who had moved away have returned to open family businesses.」
Sora のコメント。「I believe tourism can be good, but only when the community itself controls it. If residents own the businesses and set the rules, the benefits stay local and the culture is respected.」
Mika のコメント。「several closed stores have reopened, and three of my old classmates moved back to run a café and a guesthouse」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Daniel and Emma」… Daniel の懸念 (文化の商業化) を裏づける記述は資料A に無い。むしろ伝統織物の訓練に資金が使われている。Emma の文化共有論も資料A の主題ではない。
- 「Mika and Daniel」… Mika は支持されるが、Daniel の文化衰退の懸念は資料A が示す内容と逆方向。
- 「Emma and Sora」… Sora は支持されるが、Emma の「観光客との交流で文化を共有する」という論点は資料A に現れない。

questions.stem: According to Source A, what is one specific result of Riverton's "community tourism" rule?
choices: Outside firms came to own most of the town's new hotels.
Rents in Riverton rose faster than in nearby towns.
The number of tourists visiting Riverton fell sharply.
A town fund financed the repair of an old theater and the training of young weavers.
questions.explanation:
正解は「A town fund financed the repair of an old theater and the training of young weavers.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「具体的な結果はどれか」型は、**資料が明示した動詞と目的語**をそのまま拾う。
  `The fund has already paid to repair ~ and to train ~`。
- `unlike in nearby towns where outside firms dominate` の unlike が対比。
  **リバートンは近隣とは違う**ことを示す。
- 誤答は資料の記述を**反転**させて作られる。家賃の不満は「fallen sharply」。

## 🔬 文構造分析
基金の使途:
`[The fund] has already paid [to repair an old theater] and [to train young people in
 traditional weaving].`
  S=The fund / V=has paid / M=to repair ~ と to train ~ (目的の不定詞2つが等位)
対比と効果:
`[The mayor] reported [that, [unlike in nearby towns [where outside firms dominate]],
 [most of Riverton's tourism income] now stays [in the community], and [complaints about
 rising rents] have fallen [sharply]].`
  節内: S=most of Riverton's tourism income / V=stays / M=in the community
  等位: S=complaints about rising rents / V=have fallen / M=sharply
→ 「劇場の修復」と「若者への織物の訓練」が、基金が実際に支払った具体例。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source A。「The fund has already paid to repair an old theater and to train young people in traditional weaving. The mayor reported that, unlike in nearby towns where outside firms dominate, most of Riverton's tourism income now stays in the community, and complaints about rising rents have fallen sharply.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Outside firms came to own most of the town's new hotels.」… 規則は「Any new hotel or restaurant must be at least half-owned by local residents」= 住民が半分以上所有する義務。外部企業の支配は近隣の町の話で、リバートンとは逆。
- 「Rents in Riverton rose faster than in nearby towns.」… 家賃については「complaints about rising rents have fallen sharply」= 不満が急減した。上昇が加速したのではない。
- 「The number of tourists visiting Riverton fell sharply.」… 観光客数の減少についての記述は資料A に無い。

questions.stem: Based on the data in Source B, which statement is best supported?
choices: In outside-owned towns, more residents disagreed than agreed that tourism had improved life, and fewer felt their traditions were well preserved than in locally owned towns.
Residents of towns with very few tourists agreed most strongly that tourism had improved their lives.
Local ownership made no difference to how residents viewed tourism.
In locally owned towns, most residents felt their traditions were poorly preserved.
questions.explanation:
正解は「In outside-owned towns, more residents disagreed than agreed that tourism had improved life, and fewer felt their traditions were well preserved than in locally owned towns.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 調査データの読み取りは**同じ町種の中で agree と disagree を比較**する。
  外部所有では 34% vs 52% で不同意が上回る。
- 伝統の保存は 66% (地元所有) vs 29% (外部所有)。**37ポイントの差**。
- 選択肢が2つの主張を含むなら、**両方が数値で成立**しなければならない。

## 🔬 文構造分析
調査結果:
`[Towns [where most businesses are owned by outside companies]]: 34% agreed, 52% disagreed`
  S=Towns where ~ / 数値が agreed / disagreed の別に並ぶ
`in locally owned towns, 66% said [local traditions were "well preserved"], while in
 outside-owned towns only 29% said so.`
  S=66% / V=said / O=that 節相当
  while 節 (対比): S=only 29% / V=said / O=so (= 前の内容を受ける代用語)
選択肢側は2つの主張を and で結ぶ:
`[In outside-owned towns], [more residents] disagreed [than agreed] ..., and [fewer]
 felt [their traditions were well preserved] [than in locally owned towns].`
→ 52 > 34 で前半成立、29 < 66 で後半成立。両方が数値で裏づけられる。

## 📍 本文の根拠
Source B。「Towns where most businesses are locally owned: 71% agreed, 18% disagreed, 11% unsure.」「Towns where most businesses are owned by outside companies: 34% agreed, 52% disagreed, 14% unsure.」「Towns with very few tourists: 40% agreed, 25% disagreed, 35% unsure.」「in locally owned towns, 66% said local traditions were "well preserved," while in outside-owned towns only 29% said so.」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Residents of towns with very few tourists agreed most strongly that tourism had improved their lives.」… 観光客が少ない町の同意は 40%。地元所有の町の 71% より低く、「最も強く同意」は成立しない。
- 「Local ownership made no difference to how residents viewed tourism.」… 地元所有 71% と外部所有 34% で 37 ポイントの差がある。「違いは無い」は数値と矛盾する。
- 「In locally owned towns, most residents felt their traditions were poorly preserved.」… 地元所有の町では 66% が「well preserved」と答えている。「保存されていないと感じる人が大半」は正反対。
